2026_02_MIN_CHI.headline: Vikings keep Bears out of the end zone in 9–3 win at Chicago
paragraphs: Chicago reached the red zone three times and came away with nothing each time, and the Minnesota Vikings made three field goals stand up for a 9–3 win at Soldier Field on Sunday. The Bears closed as 4.5-point favorites; instead the Vikings moved to 2-0 and Chicago fell to 1-1.

Will Reichard opened the scoring with a 35-yard field goal early in the first quarter, and Cairo Santos matched it from 50 yards. Reichard's 49-yarder midway through the second quarter put Minnesota ahead 6–3, and that margin held through a scoreless third quarter. Chicago also gave the ball away twice, on Byron Murphy Jr.'s interception of Caleb Williams late in the first quarter and a D'Andre Swift fumble in the third, but the Vikings punted after both.

Neither offense found much room. Minnesota finished with 246 yards and converted three of 13 third downs, while Chicago gained 297 yards but was sacked four times, twice by Dallas Turner. Aaron Jones Sr. carried 23 times for 105 yards, and Carson Wentz completed 11 of 20 passes for 143 yards.

Williams was hurt midway through the fourth quarter and did not return, leaving Tyson Bagent to finish. Minnesota then put together an 11-play, 67-yard drive from its own 12, and Reichard's 39-yard kick with 1:12 left made it 9–3. Bagent moved the Bears 44 yards on their last possession before they turned it over on downs. Minnesota won without a turnover, and three empty red-zone trips left Chicago with only Santos' field goal.

2026_03_CIN_PIT.headline: Boswell's late field goal lifts Steelers past Bengals 30–27
paragraphs: Pittsburgh's only sack of the game came at the right moment. Joe Burrow fumbled when he was brought down with 53 seconds left, the Steelers recovered, and Chris Boswell's 33-yard field goal stood up for a 30–27 win over the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday. The Bengals had closed as 3.5-point favorites; both teams are 2-1.

The game had four lead changes and three ties. Aaron Rodgers threw touchdown passes to Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek in the first quarter, and Burrow answered with scores to Ja'Marr Chase and, after Jordan Battle intercepted Rodgers late in the second quarter, Tee Higgins, tying it 17–17 at halftime.

Evan McPherson's 38-yard field goal put the Bengals ahead midway through the third, Rodgers found DK Metcalf from 6 yards late in the quarter, and Burrow's 25-yard touchdown pass to Mike Gesicki early in the fourth made it 27–24. Boswell tied it with a 36-yard field goal on a drive that began at the Cincinnati 14.

Pittsburgh then started at its own 8 with 7:39 left. Rodgers hit Darnell Washington for 47 yards and Jaylen Warren broke a 26-yard run before Boswell's kick with 2:18 to go. Warren finished with 127 rushing yards on 17 carries, and Rodgers threw for 292 yards.

Burrow completed 28 of 37 passes for 282 yards without an interception, and Dexter Lawrence II sacked Rodgers twice. But the Steelers averaged 7.0 yards per play and converted seven of 12 third downs, enough to offset Rodgers' interception.

2026_10_HOU_CLE.headline: Browns rally from 17–0 down to beat Texans 27–24 on Judkins' late run
paragraphs: C.J. Stroud threw two touchdown passes as Houston built a 17–0 lead early in the second quarter. The Cleveland Browns, 4.5-point underdogs by the closing line, then scored 20 unanswered points and won 27–24 on Sunday.

Deshaun Watson started the comeback. After Andre Szmyt's 49-yard field goal, Watson hit Jerry Jeudy for 65 yards and ran 6 yards for a touchdown on the next play. Tyson Campbell intercepted Stroud late in the half, and Cleveland trailed only 17–10 at the break.

KC Concepcion's 6-yard touchdown run tied it midway through the third quarter, and a 15-play, 74-yard drive ended with Szmyt's 26-yard field goal with 15 seconds left in the quarter. Stroud answered with an 11-yard touchdown pass to Dalton Schultz midway through the fourth, giving the Texans a 24–20 lead.

Calen Bullock intercepted Watson with 5:19 left, but Houston punted it back. Cleveland took over at the Houston 49 with 1:40 to play, Watson found Harold Fannin Jr. for 30 yards, and Quinshon Judkins ran in from 5 yards with 56 seconds left. The Texans' last possession, from their own 15, ended on downs.

Watson threw for 312 yards and ran for 49, and Fannin caught seven passes for 91 yards. Stroud threw for 211 yards and three touchdowns but completed 20 of 38 passes, and Houston converted three of 12 third downs and lost Woody Marks to an injury in the third quarter. Cleveland improved to 6-4. Houston fell to 3-6.

2026_10_NE_DET.headline: Gibbs, Lions pull away from Patriots 35–10 in Munich
paragraphs: New England lost Drake Maye on its opening drive in Munich, and the Detroit Lions never let the Patriots recover. Jahmyr Gibbs piled up 252 yards from scrimmage and scored twice in Detroit's 35–10 win on Sunday.

Maye went down with 9:43 left in the first quarter when Aidan Hutchinson sacked him, and Hutchinson was hurt on the same play. Neither returned. New England took a 3–0 lead on Andy Borregales' 33-yard field goal, but Jared Goff answered with a 56-yard touchdown pass to Amon-Ra St. Brown, the start of 28 unanswered Detroit points. New England had little to offer after the change. Tommy DeVito completed 12 of 24 passes for 81 yards in relief, and the Patriots finished the game sacked five times and four of 13 on third downs.

The last 5:53 of the first half brought three interceptions, two thrown by Goff, including Kevin Byard's end-zone pick with 12 seconds left. Neither team scored off any of them, and Gibbs' 5-yard touchdown run in between sent Detroit to halftime ahead 21–3.
St. Brown's second touchdown, a 28-yard catch in the third quarter, made it 28–3, and Gibbs answered Lan Larison's fourth-quarter touchdown with a 28-yard scoring run.

Goff's two interceptions were Detroit's only turnovers, and an offense that ran for 191 yards and held the ball for 32:57 left New England no way back. The Lions improved to 7-2 with their fifth straight win. The Patriots, who also lost A.J. Brown to an injury late in the third quarter, fell to 5-5.

2026_10_SF_DAL.headline: McCaffrey's 223 yards carry 49ers past Cowboys 46–40
paragraphs: The Dallas Cowboys had scored 13 straight points to pull within 38–32 late in the fourth quarter when Brock Purdy found Christian McCaffrey for a 66-yard touchdown on the second play of the next drive, and the San Francisco 49ers held on for a 46–40 win on Sunday. McCaffrey finished with 223 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns.

The lead changed hands three times in the first half. Purdy hit Deebo Samuel Sr. for an 11-yard touchdown, Dak Prescott found George Pickens for scores of 35 and 39 yards, and McCaffrey's 74-yard touchdown catch late in the second quarter sent San Francisco to halftime ahead 17–16.

San Francisco pulled away when Kaelon Black ran 25 yards for a touchdown early in the third quarter and Samuel broke a 70-yard touchdown run midway through it. After Malik Mustapha intercepted Prescott late in the quarter, the 49ers went 90 yards in 12 plays, and McCaffrey's 16-yard run early in the fourth made it 38–19.

Purdy completed 22 of 28 passes for 389 yards and three touchdowns, and San Francisco averaged 9.4 yards per play. Prescott answered with 343 yards and five touchdown passes, three of them to Pickens, who caught 11 passes for 145 yards. The last, a 1-yard throw to CeeDee Lamb with 47 seconds left, made it 46–40.

San Francisco did not turn the ball over despite being sacked five times, and Ryan Flournoy's fumble after a catch with 2 seconds left ended Dallas' final possession. The 49ers improved to 8-1 with their second straight win; Dallas fell to 4-6.

2026_01_ARI_LAC.headline: Cardinals upset Chargers 26–14 behind four Ryland field goals
paragraphs: Arizona controlled the ball and the scoreboard in Los Angeles, beating the Chargers 26–14 on Sunday as an 8.5-point underdog. The Cardinals held possession for 37:31, and Chad Ryland made four field goals to keep the Chargers chasing.

The teams traded first-quarter touchdown runs by Jeremiyah Love and Omarion Hampton before Arizona moved in front for good. Hampton fumbled early in the second quarter, and the Cardinals turned their next possession into Ryland's 27-yard field goal for a 10–7 lead. His 44-yarder with four seconds left in the half made it 13–7.

Los Angeles stayed within reach into the third quarter. After Ryland's third field goal, Justin Herbert found Ladd McConkey for an 8-yard touchdown midway through the period to cut the deficit to 16–14, but McConkey was hurt late in the quarter and did not return. Arizona answered early in the fourth, when Jacoby Brissett hit Trey McBride for a 3-yard score on a drive that began at the Los Angeles 3, and Andrew Wingard intercepted Herbert soon after.

Brissett completed 27 of 37 passes for 277 yards, and McBride caught nine passes for 95 yards. The Chargers converted two of eight third downs and gained 268 yards, and after Ryland's 49-yard field goal with 2:37 left, their final possession ended on downs. Arizona opened 1-0 without committing a turnover; Los Angeles fell to 0-1.

2026_01_ATL_PIT.headline: Watt's pick-six lifts Steelers past Falcons 20–13
paragraphs: Pittsburgh's defense supplied the points that decided a low-scoring opener. T.J. Watt intercepted Cooper Rush and returned it for a touchdown early in the fourth quarter, and the Steelers held on to beat the Atlanta Falcons 20–13 on Sunday.

Turnovers shaped the first half, too. Jaylen Warren fumbled late in the first quarter, and three plays later Rush found Bijan Robinson for a 23-yard touchdown and a 7–3 Atlanta lead. Pittsburgh got the ball back the same way: after Chris Boswell's 28-yard field goal, Jaquan Brisker intercepted Rush, and Aaron Rodgers hit Pat Freiermuth for a 6-yard touchdown that put the Steelers ahead 13–7 at halftime.

Nick Folk's 51-yard field goal late in the third quarter pulled Atlanta to 13–10, but Watt's return made it 20–10. Folk answered with a 43-yarder, and the Falcons got no closer. Watt finished with two sacks along with the interception, and Alex Highsmith added two more as Atlanta was sacked four times.

Robinson accounted for 173 yards from scrimmage, including eight catches for 90 yards, but little else worked for the Falcons. Rush completed 12 of 22 passes for 143 yards with two interceptions, and Atlanta converted two of 12 third downs. Pittsburgh missed a field goal on its final possession, yet the Falcons' last drive, which began at their own 46 with 6:58 left, ended in a punt. The Steelers opened 1-0; the Falcons fell to 0-1.

2026_01_BAL_IND.headline: Henry runs for three scores as Ravens rout Colts 41–23
paragraphs: Baltimore turned two early Indianapolis turnovers into touchdowns and had the game in hand by halftime, beating the Colts 41–23 on Sunday in Indianapolis. Derrick Henry ran for 144 yards and three touchdowns, and the Ravens averaged 7.9 yards per play.

Jonathan Taylor's 1-yard run gave Indianapolis a 6–0 lead, but Baltimore answered with 28 unanswered points. Lamar Jackson ran 5 yards for the first score, and after Roquan Smith intercepted Daniel Jones, Henry finished a short drive to make it 14–6. In the second quarter Jackson hit Zay Flowers for a 54-yard touchdown, Taylor then fumbled after a catch, and Henry broke a 32-yard scoring run three plays later for a 28–6 lead.

The Colts got one back when Jackson fumbled on a sack and Taylor scored from the 3 on the ensuing drive, but Tyler Loop's 57-yard field goal with five seconds left sent Baltimore to the break ahead 31–13. Indianapolis matched Baltimore over the second half, yet Henry's 3-yard run early in the fourth quarter made it 38–16.

Jackson completed 17 of 25 passes for 324 yards and ran for 40 more, and Flowers turned five catches into 150 yards. Baltimore outgained Indianapolis 506 yards to 251 and held the ball for 35:20. Taylor ran for 98 yards and two touchdowns for the Colts, who converted three of 10 third downs. The Ravens opened 1-0; the Colts fell to 0-1.

2026_01_BUF_HOU.headline: Allen's late 96-yard drive lifts Bills past Texans 36–31
paragraphs: Josh Allen got the ball at his own 4 with 3:13 left and Buffalo trailing 31–30, and seven plays later the Bills had the lead for good. Allen's 34-yard touchdown pass to Joshua Palmer with 1:41 remaining delivered a 36–31 win over the Houston Texans on Sunday in a game in which the lead changed hands eight times.

David Montgomery scored twice on the ground for Houston in the first half, and his second touchdown put the Texans ahead 14–10. Buffalo answered with 14 straight points: an Allen 1-yard run, then a 43-yard scoring pass to DJ Moore at the end of a three-play, 96-yard drive. C.J. Stroud's 12-yard touchdown pass to Nico Collins with 31 seconds left cut the halftime lead to 24–21.

The fourth quarter swung back and forth. Stroud's 7-yard touchdown pass to Montgomery early in the period put Houston ahead 28–27, Tyler Bass answered with a 33-yard field goal, and Ka'imi Fairbairn's 58-yarder midway through the quarter gave the Texans a 31–30 lead. Allen then drove Buffalo 96 yards again, hitting Dalton Kincaid for 35 yards on the way to the winning throw.

Houston's last chance began at its own 29 and moved 47 yards in 10 plays before Stroud fumbled on a sack with 16 seconds left and the Bills recovered. Buffalo did not commit a turnover. Allen finished 20 of 29 for 334 yards with two touchdown passes and two scoring runs, and Kincaid caught five passes for 130 yards. The Bills opened 1-0; the Texans fell to 0-1.

2026_01_CLE_JAX.headline: Lawrence throws four touchdowns as Jaguars rout Browns 34–10
paragraphs: Jacksonville turned both Cleveland turnovers into touchdowns and led 24–0 at halftime on the way to a 34–10 win over the Browns on Sunday. Trevor Lawrence completed 18 of 23 passes for 245 yards and four touchdowns, and the Jaguars did not give the ball away.

Foyesade Oluokun intercepted Deshaun Watson early in the first quarter, and Lawrence followed with a 30-yard touchdown pass to Parker Washington. He added a 4-yard scoring throw to Josh Cameron late in the quarter, and after Cam Little's 47-yard field goal, KC Concepcion fumbled after a catch. Lawrence needed five plays to cash that in, finding Brenton Strange from 14 yards out for a 24–0 lead.

Lawrence's 32-yard touchdown pass to Jakobi Meyers early in the third quarter stretched the run to 31 unanswered points. Cleveland never found a rhythm against a pass rush that sacked the Browns five times, with Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker getting 1.5 apiece. The Browns converted one of eight third downs and came away from both red-zone trips without a touchdown; their first points were Andre Szmyt's 26-yard field goal after a drive that began at the Jacksonville 23.

Watson finished 16 of 22 for 205 yards, and his 46-yard touchdown pass to Denzel Boston late in the fourth quarter came with the outcome long settled. Jacksonville held the ball for 33:51 and outgained Cleveland 360 yards to 272. The Jaguars opened 1-0; the Browns fell to 0-1.

2026_01_CHI_CAR.headline: Swift scores three times as Bears pull away from Panthers 59–37
paragraphs: Chicago and Carolina were tied 31–31 midway through the third quarter before the Bears scored the next 21 points, pulling away for a 59–37 win on Sunday in a game that produced 96 combined points. D'Andre Swift ran for 124 yards and three touchdowns, and Chicago finished with 291 rushing yards.

Luther Burden III fumbled early in the game, and Bryce Young turned the short field into a 4-yard touchdown pass to Chuba Hubbard. Chicago answered with 21 straight points, Carolina tied it with 14 of its own, and the teams traded field goals before Caleb Williams ran 29 yards for a touchdown with 32 seconds left in the half for a 31–24 lead.

Hubbard's 2-yard run tied it again in the third quarter, and Carolina never drew even after that. Swift capped a 13-play drive with a 1-yard run, and Kyle Monangai went 61 yards for a touchdown on the first play of Chicago's next drive. After Tetairoa McMillan lost a fumble at the start of the fourth quarter, Williams finished a 12-play drive with a 1-yard touchdown pass to Jahdae Walker for a 52–31 lead.

Chicago converted 10 of 14 third downs and was four of four in the red zone. Williams completed 21 of 29 passes for 269 yards and two touchdowns and ran for two more. Young threw for 361 yards and three touchdowns for Carolina, two of them to Jalen Coker, who caught eight passes for 138 yards, but the Panthers committed three turnovers. Chicago opened 1-0; Carolina fell to 0-1.

2026_01_DAL_NYG.headline: Dart throws three touchdowns as Giants upset Cowboys 28–20
paragraphs: The New York Giants, 3-point underdogs, beat the Dallas Cowboys 28–20 on Sunday night by sustaining drive after drive. They converted nine of 11 third downs, were four of four in the red zone and held the ball for 36:40, and Jaxson Dart threw three touchdown passes.

The game turned in the final two minutes of the first half. Dallas recovered a Tyrone Tracy Jr. fumble with the score tied 7–7, but Jevon Holland intercepted Dak Prescott on the ensuing possession, and Dart threw a 15-yard touchdown pass to Isaiah Likely with 25 seconds left for a 14–7 halftime lead.

Dart and Likely connected again from 2 yards out to finish a 12-play drive midway through the third quarter. Javonte Williams' 1-yard run late in the period pulled Dallas within 21–14, but the Giants answered with a 13-play march that ended in Dart's 9-yard touchdown pass to Devin Singletary midway through the fourth quarter.

Prescott threw for 175 yards and two scores, the second a 17-yard pass to Williams with 5:26 left that made it 28–20 on the Cowboys' final possession. Dart completed 23 of 29 passes for 230 yards and ran for 54 more, Likely caught all eight of his targets for 78 yards, and Cam Skattebo ran for 81 yards and the opening touchdown. The division win moved the Giants to 1-0; the Cowboys fell to 0-1.

2026_01_DEN_KC.headline: Walker runs for 173 yards as Chiefs beat Broncos 31–10
paragraphs: Kansas City pulled away from Denver after halftime, outscoring the Broncos 17–3 in the second half of a 31–10 win on Monday night. Kenneth Walker III ran for 173 yards on 23 carries, and the Chiefs' defense held Denver to 176 yards.

Mansoor Delane intercepted Bo Nix early in the first quarter, and Patrick Mahomes ran 15 yards for a touchdown on the next possession. Nix answered with a 19-yard scoring pass to Evan Engram, and the game stayed level until Mahomes found Rashee Rice for a 13-yard touchdown late in the second quarter, capping an 80-yard drive, for a 14–7 halftime lead.

Walker broke a 60-yard touchdown run early in the third quarter for a 21–7 lead. Denver's best opening came when Brandon Jones intercepted Mahomes and the Broncos took over at the Kansas City 5, but they lost 8 yards on the drive and settled for Wil Lutz's 31-yard field goal. Harrison Butker answered with a 28-yarder, and after Nix fumbled on a sack late in the quarter, Walker caught a 2-yard touchdown pass early in the fourth to make it 31–10.

Kansas City ran for 220 yards and converted nine of 17 third downs. Denver converted two of 12, was sacked four times and averaged 3.7 yards per play, and Nix completed 17 of 28 passes for 131 yards. Mahomes threw for 184 yards and two touchdowns with an interception and ran for another score. The division win moved the Chiefs to 1-0; the Broncos fell to 0-1.

2026_01_GB_MIN.headline: Vikings score 29 straight points to rally past Packers 39–22
paragraphs: Minnesota lost Kyler Murray midway through the first quarter and trailed Green Bay 22–10 in the third, then scored the game's last 29 points to beat the Packers 39–22 on Sunday. Carson Wentz threw three touchdown passes in relief, two of them to Justin Jefferson.

Green Bay built its lead on Jordan Love's arm. Keisean Nixon intercepted Murray early in the first quarter, setting up Trey Smack's 59-yard field goal, and Love hit Christian Watson for an 81-yard touchdown. After Wentz found Jefferson for a 39-yard score late in the second quarter, Love answered with a 2-yard touchdown pass to Watson with 18 seconds left, and Smack's third field goal made it 22–10.

Wentz's 16-yard touchdown pass to T.J. Hockenson late in the third quarter started the rally, and Aaron Jones Sr. capped an 83-yard drive with a 3-yard run with 6:42 left to put Minnesota ahead 25–22. Green Bay then gave the ball away twice in a row. Love fumbled on a sack, and Jordan Mason scored from the 1 on the next play; on the Packers' following series James Pierre intercepted Love, and Wentz threw a 9-yard touchdown pass to Jefferson.

Minnesota won despite being outgained 419 yards to 239. Love threw for 387 yards and Watson caught six passes for 147 yards and two touchdowns, but Green Bay was one of four in the red zone and three of 12 on third downs. The division win moved the Vikings to 1-0; the Packers fell to 0-1.

2026_01_MIA_LV.headline: Jeanty scores twice as Raiders beat Dolphins 27–13
paragraphs: Las Vegas opened with a 16-play, 93-yard touchdown drive and never trailed, beating the Miami Dolphins 27–13 on Sunday. Ashton Jeanty ran for 102 yards and caught two touchdown passes from Kirk Cousins, and the Raiders sacked the Dolphins five times.

Cousins finished that first drive with a 15-yard touchdown pass to Jack Bech, and his 13-yard scoring pass to Jeanty late in the second quarter made it 17–3. Riley Patterson's 37-yard field goal with five seconds left cut the halftime lead to 17–6.

Miami got back into it early in the third quarter. Michael Taaffe intercepted Cousins, and Malik Willis ran 14 yards for a touchdown on the next drive to make it 17–13. Las Vegas answered at once: Cousins hit Jeanty for another 13-yard touchdown, and on the Dolphins' next possession Treydan Stukes intercepted Willis, setting up Matt Gay's 30-yard field goal at the end of a 13-play drive.

Cousins threw a second interception, to Dante Trader Jr., early in the fourth quarter, but Miami could not turn it into points. The Dolphins converted two of 10 third downs, and their final possession, which began at their own 3, ended when Malik Washington fumbled after a 24-yard catch with two minutes left. Willis threw for 220 yards without a touchdown pass. The Raiders opened 1-0; the Dolphins fell to 0-1.

2026_01_NE_SEA.headline: Maye's three interceptions help Seahawks rally past Patriots 13–10
paragraphs: Seattle lost Sam Darnold on its opening drive and trailed New England 10–0 in the third quarter, then took advantage of three fourth-quarter interceptions of Drake Maye to win 13–10 on Wednesday night.

Darnold was hurt on a sack by Dre'Mont Jones early in the first quarter and did not return, and Drew Lock played the rest of the way. Seattle's offense struggled to stay on the field, converting two of 11 third downs on the night, while Maye's 2-yard touchdown pass to Eli Raridon in the second quarter and Andy Borregales' 50-yard field goal early in the third gave New England its 10–0 lead.

Jason Myers' 30-yard field goal late in the third quarter put Seattle on the board. Then Nehemiah Pritchett intercepted Maye early in the fourth, and Lock hit Jaxon Smith-Njigba for a 45-yard touchdown on the next drive to tie it 10–10. Julian Love picked off Maye minutes later, and Myers' 26-yard field goal with 5:53 left gave the Seahawks their first lead.

New England answered with a 15-play drive from its own 27, but it ended when Josh Jobe intercepted Maye in the end zone with 26 seconds left. Maye completed 23 of 33 passes for 178 yards and ran for 47 more, and the Patriots, who lost A.J. Brown to an injury early in the third quarter, held the ball for 34:17. Lock finished 16 of 22 for 187 yards, and Smith-Njigba caught eight passes for 122 yards. Seattle opened 1-0; New England fell to 0-1.

2026_01_NYJ_TEN.headline: Hall runs for 102 yards as Jets grind past Titans 23–10
paragraphs: The New York Jets held the ball for 38:46 and kept Tennessee's offense off the field, beating the Titans 23–10 on Sunday. Breece Hall ran for 102 yards and a touchdown, and Jason Sanders kicked three field goals, including two from 51 and 52 yards.

Kenyon Sadiq ran 3 yards for a touchdown early in the first quarter, and Joey Slye answered with a 42-yard field goal. New York then went 19 plays and 74 yards on a second-quarter drive that ended in Sanders' 33-yard field goal and a 10–3 lead, and the Jets recovered a Tennessee fumble moments later.

Hall's 4-yard run capped an 80-yard drive midway through the third quarter, and Sanders' two long kicks stretched the Jets' run to 16 unanswered points. Geno Smith completed 19 of 24 passes for 215 yards, with Garrett Wilson catching six for 79, and New York was not sacked.

Tennessee gained 195 yards, ran the ball 14 times and punted seven times. Cam Ward completed 19 of 32 passes for 140 yards and was sacked three times; his 11-yard touchdown pass to Elic Ayomanor with 2:45 left came too late to matter. The Jets opened 1-0 without a turnover; the Titans fell to 0-1.

2026_01_NO_DET.headline: Lions hold off Saints 31–30 in overtime behind Gibbs, St. Brown
paragraphs: Detroit turned two New Orleans turnovers in the third quarter into a 21–0 lead, then needed overtime to escape with a 31–30 win over the Saints on Sunday. Amon-Ra St. Brown caught the deciding 4-yard touchdown pass from Jared Goff, and Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 156 yards and two scores.

Gibbs' 1-yard run capped a 13-play, 89-yard drive for the only points of the first half. Derrick Barnes intercepted Tyler Shough at the start of the third quarter, and Gibbs scored from the 1 again; Shough then fumbled on a sack, and Goff found St. Brown for a 19-yard touchdown three plays later.

New Orleans answered with 17 straight points. Kendre Miller ran 8 yards for a score, Shough hit Devaughn Vele for a 1-yard touchdown, and Daniel Carlson's 28-yard field goal midway through the fourth quarter made it 21–17. After Jake Bates' 23-yarder, Shough found Chris Olave for 42 yards and then Juwan Johnson for a 9-yard touchdown with 1:13 left to tie it 24–24.

Detroit opened overtime with a 10-play, 70-yard drive that ended in Goff's second touchdown pass to St. Brown. The Saints matched it with an 80-yard drive, but Shough's 8-yard touchdown pass to Noah Fant with 1:38 remaining left them a point short, and the game ended 31–30.

Shough completed 35 of 56 passes for 410 yards, and Olave caught 10 passes for 182 yards, but the Saints were sacked five times and committed three turnovers. Detroit held the ball for 36:51. The Lions opened 1-0; the Saints fell to 0-1.

2026_01_SF_LA.headline: Purdy throws three touchdowns as 49ers beat Rams 27–7 in Melbourne
paragraphs: After Kyren Williams' touchdown run at the start of the second quarter gave Los Angeles a 7–3 lead in Melbourne, Australia, the San Francisco 49ers scored the game's last 24 points and beat the Rams 27–7 on Thursday night. The 49ers were 3.5-point underdogs.

The game turned on back-to-back interceptions. Quentin Lake picked off Brock Purdy in the second quarter, but Renardo Green intercepted Matthew Stafford on the Rams' very next possession. Purdy then finished an 86-yard drive with a 39-yard touchdown pass to Demarcus Robinson for a 10–7 halftime lead.

Purdy's 2-yard scoring pass to Mike Evans early in the third quarter made it 17–7. Early in the fourth, San Francisco drove 99 yards from its own 1, finishing with Purdy's 15-yard touchdown pass to Deebo Samuel Sr., and a Tyler Higbee fumble soon after set up Eddy Pineiro's 56-yard field goal.

Purdy completed 25 of 34 passes for 205 yards, and San Francisco ran for 174 yards while holding the ball for 33:50. Stafford completed 15 of 25 passes for 155 yards without a touchdown, and the Rams converted two of nine third downs and reached the end zone on one of three red-zone trips. The division win moved the 49ers to 1-0; the Rams fell to 0-1.

2026_01_WAS_PHI.headline: Goedert scores twice as Eagles hold off Commanders 24–22
paragraphs: Washington had the ball longer, but Philadelphia had the big plays, and the Eagles beat the Commanders 24–22 on Sunday. Jalen Hurts threw three touchdown passes, two to Dallas Goedert, the second a 43-yarder midway through the fourth quarter that made it 24–16.

Drew Stevens' 55-yard field goal gave Washington an early lead before Hurts hit Dontayvion Wicks for 64 yards late in the first quarter, setting up Goedert's 17-yard touchdown catch early in the second. Hurts found Wicks for a 9-yard score midway through the quarter, and Jacory Croskey-Merritt's 1-yard run at the end of a 12-play drive late in the half left Philadelphia ahead 14–9.

Jake Elliott's 35-yard field goal late in the third quarter made it 17–9. Jayden Daniels answered early in the fourth with a 10-yard touchdown pass to Stefon Diggs to pull Washington within 17–16, but Philadelphia needed only eight plays to go 74 yards for Goedert's second touchdown.

Washington drove 63 yards in 12 plays on its last possession, and Daniels' 1-yard touchdown pass to Antonio Williams with 1:05 left made it 24–22, but the Commanders got no closer. They held the ball for 33:20 and were three of three in the red zone, yet averaged 4.4 yards per play to the Eagles' 6.0. Neither team committed a turnover. The division win moved Philadelphia to 1-0; Washington fell to 0-1.

2026_01_TB_CIN.headline: Bengals cash in four Buccaneers fumbles in 33–27 win
paragraphs: Tampa Bay never punted, but it lost four fumbles, and Cincinnati turned every one of them into points in a 33–27 win on Sunday. Three came in the first quarter and early in the second, when the Bengals built a 21–3 lead, and Evan McPherson made all four of his field-goal attempts.

Baker Mayfield fumbled on a sack midway through the first quarter, and Demetrius Knight Jr. returned it for a touchdown. Moments later Bucky Irving fumbled after a catch, and Joe Burrow found Mike Gesicki for a 2-yard touchdown. When Mayfield lost a fumble on a run early in the second quarter, Chase Brown's 5-yard touchdown run on the next drive made it 21–3.

Cincinnati led 24–10 at halftime, and Tampa Bay worked back into the game in the third quarter. Josiah Trotter, who also had a sack, intercepted Burrow and returned it for a touchdown late in the period to cut the lead to 27–20.

McPherson answered with a 58-yard field goal early in the fourth quarter, and Tampa Bay's fourth fumble, by Mayfield on a sack, set up his 32-yarder for a 33–20 lead. Mayfield's 9-yard touchdown run with 3:25 left came on the Buccaneers' last possession.

Mayfield completed 23 of 28 passes for 216 yards and ran for 30, and the Buccaneers converted five of 10 third downs, but the giveaways left them chasing from the first quarter on. Burrow threw for 254 yards. Cincinnati opened 1-0; Tampa Bay fell to 0-1.

2026_02_CAR_ATL.headline: Lloyd's two interceptions lead Panthers' 34–3 rout of Falcons
paragraphs: Atlanta lost a fumble on the first play of the game and turned the ball over five times in all, and Carolina beat the Falcons 34–3 on Sunday. Devin Lloyd intercepted two passes, returning one for a touchdown, and added a sack.

Bryce Young turned Cooper Rush's fumble into a 3-yard touchdown pass to Chuba Hubbard, and Ryan Fitzgerald's two field goals built a 13–0 lead. Nick Folk's 41-yard field goal late in the second quarter put Atlanta on the board, but Young answered with a 55-yard completion to Xavier Legette and a 7-yard touchdown pass to Darren Waller with 24 seconds left for a 20–3 halftime lead.

Young and Waller connected again from 12 yards midway through the third quarter. Lloyd then intercepted Rush, and when Atlanta turned to Jack Strand, Lloyd picked him off too and returned it for a touchdown late in the quarter for a 34–3 lead.

Young completed 23 of 36 passes for 287 yards and three touchdowns, and Tetairoa McMillan caught five passes for 101 yards. Atlanta ran for 157 yards, 72 of them by Bijan Robinson, but the Falcons never reached the red zone, and their last drive ended when Strand fumbled on a sack in the final minute. The division win moved Carolina to 1-1; Atlanta fell to 0-2 with its second straight loss.

2026_02_CIN_HOU.headline: Chase scores twice as Bengals stop Texans 20–6
paragraphs: Houston outgained Cincinnati 374 yards to 267 and reached the red zone four times, but the Texans failed to score a touchdown on any of those trips, and the Bengals won 20–6 on Sunday as 3-point underdogs. Ja'Marr Chase caught both of Joe Burrow's touchdown passes.

After a scoreless first quarter, Burrow hit Chase for a 32-yard touchdown late in the second, finishing an 81-yard drive, and Ka'imi Fairbairn's 37-yard field goal made it 7–3 at halftime. Evan McPherson's 51-yard field goal early in the third quarter and Burrow's 18-yard scoring pass to Chase late in the period pushed the lead to 17–3.

C.J. Stroud completed 30 of 55 passes for 353 yards, and Dalton Schultz caught 12 passes for 140 yards, but Houston came away with only two Fairbairn field goals. Cincinnati sacked the Texans four times, two by Cedric Johnson, and allowed five conversions on 17 third downs. McPherson's 57-yard field goal early in the fourth quarter made it 20–6.

Houston's last drive covered 50 yards in 13 plays before ending on downs. Burrow threw for 207 yards despite being sacked five times, and Tee Higgins caught five passes for 95 yards. Neither team turned the ball over. Cincinnati improved to 2-0; Houston fell to 0-2 with its second straight loss.

2026_02_DET_BUF.headline: Bills build 21–0 lead and hold off Lions 41–31
paragraphs: Buffalo opened with 21 unanswered points and had an answer for every Detroit push after that, beating the Lions 41–31 on Thursday night. Josh Allen threw three touchdown passes and ran for two more, and the Bills converted nine of 12 third downs and scored touchdowns on all five red-zone trips.

Allen's 1-yard run and a 43-yard touchdown pass to Joshua Palmer made it 14–0 after one quarter, and a 1-yard throw to Dawson Knox early in the second stretched the lead to 21–0. Jared Goff got Detroit going with an 11-yard touchdown pass to Jahmyr Gibbs, but Allen answered with a 16-yard scoring pass to Dalton Kincaid, and Buffalo led 27–10 at halftime.

Goff's 2-yard touchdown pass to Amon-Ra St. Brown midway through the third quarter cut it to 27–17. Buffalo responded with a 15-play, 75-yard drive capped by Allen's 2-yard run, and after Sam LaPorta's 1-yard touchdown catch early in the fourth made it 34–24, James Cook III scored from the 1 with 2:53 left.

Cook ran for 135 yards as Buffalo piled up 203 on the ground and held the ball for 33:45. Goff completed 26 of 38 passes for 327 yards and four touchdowns, and St. Brown caught nine passes for 142 yards, including a 27-yard touchdown with 1:48 left. Buffalo lost DJ Moore to an injury in the second quarter, and he did not return. Neither team committed a turnover. The Bills improved to 2-0; the Lions fell to 1-1.

2026_02_CLE_TB.headline: Watson's late touchdown pass lifts Browns past Buccaneers 23–19
paragraphs: Cleveland trailed Tampa Bay 16–6 midway through the third quarter, then outscored the Buccaneers 17–3 the rest of the way to win 23–19 on Sunday as an 8.5-point underdog. Deshaun Watson's 17-yard touchdown pass to Blake Whiteheart with 3:57 left provided the winning points.

The first half was a kicking contest. Chase McLaughlin made field goals from 59, 45 and 31 yards for Tampa Bay, and Andre Szmyt answered twice for Cleveland, the second after Myles Harden intercepted Baker Mayfield late in the first quarter, leaving the Buccaneers ahead 9–6 at halftime. Mayfield's 5-yard touchdown pass to Emeka Egbuka midway through the third quarter made it 16–6.

Szmyt's third field goal cut into the deficit, and Watson then found Denzel Boston for a 55-yard touchdown late in the third quarter, capping a three-play, 83-yard drive that tied it 16–16. McLaughlin's 31-yarder early in the fourth, set up by Mayfield's 49-yard completion to Tez Johnson, put Tampa Bay back in front, but Watson answered with a 12-play, 68-yard drive that ended with the throw to Whiteheart.

Tampa Bay's final possession began at its own 49 with 3:51 left and ended on downs. The Buccaneers outgained Cleveland 313 yards to 267 but reached the end zone on only one of four red-zone trips. Watson completed 24 of 30 passes for 238 yards without a turnover, and Boston caught five passes for 95 yards. Cleveland evened its record at 1-1; Tampa Bay fell to 0-2 with its second straight loss.

2026_02_GB_NYJ.headline: Packers rally from 10 down to beat Jets 20–17 in overtime
paragraphs: Green Bay gained 199 yards and converted one of nine third downs, yet it scored the game's last 13 points and beat the New York Jets 20–17 in overtime on Sunday. Trey Smack's 26-yard field goal decided it after the Jets lost 8 yards and punted on the first possession of overtime.

The Packers lost Jayden Reed to an injury on their opening drive. Jordan Love's 6-yard touchdown pass to MarShawn Lloyd in the second quarter was answered by Braelon Allen's 5-yard run, and Geno Smith's 5-yard scoring pass to Garrett Wilson late in the third put New York ahead 14–7. When Lloyd fumbled early in the fourth, Jason Sanders turned the short field into a 32-yard field goal and a 17–7 lead.

Love answered with a 73-yard drive that ended in his 3-yard touchdown pass to Christian Watson midway through the fourth quarter, and Smack tied it with a 34-yard field goal with 3:03 left after Green Bay took over at the New York 19.

In overtime, Green Bay drove 58 yards in five plays to set up the winning kick. New York held the ball for 37:40 and outgained the Packers 285 yards to 199, with Smith completing 27 of 41 passes for 247 yards, but the Jets were sacked four times and got only a field goal from their lone takeaway. Green Bay and New York both stand at 1-1.

2026_02_IND_KC.headline: Butker wins it with one second left as Chiefs edge Colts 33–30 in OT
paragraphs: Overtime came down to a trade of field goals, and Harrison Butker had the last one. His 40-yarder with one second left gave the Kansas City Chiefs a 33–30 win over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday night, after Spencer Shrader had matched Butker's first overtime kick.

Patrick Mahomes completed 32 of 47 passes for 382 yards and three touchdowns in a game with five lead changes and three ties. Kristian Fulton's first-quarter interception of Daniel Jones set up Mahomes' 13-yard touchdown pass to Travis Kelce two plays later. Shrader's two field goals put the Colts up 13–10, Mahomes answered with a 1-yard scoring pass to Xavier Worthy, and Jonathan Taylor's 24-yard run with 1:04 left made it 20–17 at halftime.

Kansas City answered with two long drives after halftime. Mahomes finished a 14-play, 80-yard march with a 1-yard touchdown pass to Jalen Royals, and Butker's 28-yard field goal early in the fourth quarter capped a 13-play drive that began at the Kansas City 9, making it 27–20. Taylor tied it with a 5-yard run with 5:41 left, ending a 13-play drive of his own.

In overtime, Butker's 31-yard field goal put Kansas City ahead, Jones hit Laquon Treadwell for 48 yards to set up Shrader's 38-yarder, and Mahomes moved the Chiefs 46 yards in seven plays for the winner. Kenneth Walker III ran for 117 yards and caught six passes for 61 more, and Kansas City outgained Indianapolis 523 yards to 329 without a turnover. The Chiefs improved to 2-0; the Colts fell to 0-2 with their second straight loss.

2026_02_JAX_DEN.headline: Broncos rally from 13–3 down to beat Jaguars 20–13
paragraphs: Denver scored the game's last 17 points, turning a third-quarter interception into the tying touchdown, and beat the Jacksonville Jaguars 20–13 on Sunday. Jonah Coleman's 3-yard run with 7:24 left provided the winning points.

Jacksonville had the better of the first half. Bhayshul Tuten's 1-yard run put the Jaguars ahead early in the second quarter, and a Denver drive late in the half ended when Jourdan Lewis intercepted Bo Nix in the end zone. Jacksonville turned that into Cam Little's 44-yard field goal with three seconds left, and Little's 23-yarder midway through the third quarter made it 13–3.

Wil Lutz's 45-yard field goal cut the lead to 13–6, and Riley Moss intercepted Trevor Lawrence late in the third quarter. Nix turned the turnover into a 10-play drive that ended with a 7-yard touchdown pass to Nate Adkins early in the fourth, and Denver went 56 yards in five plays on its next possession for Coleman's touchdown.

Jaylen Waddle caught eight passes for 138 yards, and Nix completed 22 of 31 for 288 yards without being sacked. Jacksonville's last possession, starting at its own 20, gained 14 yards before a punt, and Lawrence finished 17 of 29 for 189 yards without a touchdown pass. Both teams are now 1-1.

2026_02_LV_LAC.headline: Masses picks off Herbert twice as Raiders top Chargers 26–14
paragraphs: Las Vegas held a 17–14 lead when Omarion Hampton fumbled inside the final four minutes, and the Raiders turned that into a 26–14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday as 6.5-point underdogs. Hezekiah Masses intercepted Justin Herbert twice.

Masses' first interception, late in the first quarter, produced no points. Kirk Cousins hit Tre Tucker for a 40-yard touchdown early in the second quarter, Hampton answered with a 1-yard run, and Matt Gay's 59-yard field goal with eight seconds left sent Las Vegas to halftime ahead 10–7.

Herbert put Los Angeles ahead 14–10 with a 10-yard touchdown pass to Oronde Gadsden midway through the third quarter, but Cousins answered with an 11-play, 74-yard drive that ended in a 13-yard scoring pass to Cody White. After Hampton's fumble, Cousins needed three plays to find White again from 11 yards for a 24–14 lead with 3:03 left. Masses intercepted Herbert on the next series, and after a Raiders punt the Chargers took over at their own 6 and gave up a safety on the first play.

Cousins completed 19 of 29 passes for 253 yards and three touchdowns, with Tucker catching five for 119. Hampton ran for 94 yards, but the Chargers, who lost David Njoku to an injury at the start of the second quarter, turned the ball over three times. The division win moved Las Vegas to 2-0; Los Angeles fell to 0-2 with its second straight loss.

2026_02_MIA_SF.headline: 49ers pull away in third quarter to beat Dolphins 35–13
paragraphs: Brock Purdy completed 20 of 22 passes for 287 yards, and San Francisco scored touchdowns on all five of its red-zone trips in a 35–13 win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. Miami reached the red zone twice and came away without a touchdown either time.

Christian McCaffrey's 1-yard run capped a 12-play drive in the first quarter. Riley Patterson's 28-yard field goal at the end of a 17-play Miami drive cut it to 7–3, but Purdy ran 2 yards for a touchdown midway through the second quarter, and Patterson's 24-yarder with two seconds left made it 14–6 at halftime.

Purdy opened the second half with a 40-yard completion to George Kittle and finished that drive with a 12-yard touchdown pass to him. Kyle Juszczyk caught a 6-yard scoring pass midway through the quarter, and McCaffrey's second 1-yard touchdown run, two plays after the 49ers took over at the Miami 28, made it 35–6.

San Francisco was not sacked, converted five of seven third downs and averaged 7.8 yards per play. Malik Willis threw for 197 yards, 77 of them on a late touchdown pass to Ryan Miller, and De'Von Achane ran for 74 yards. Neither team turned the ball over. The 49ers improved to 2-0 with their second straight win; the Dolphins fell to 0-2.

2026_02_NO_BAL.headline: Shough's late touchdown run lifts Saints past Ravens 24–17
paragraphs: The New Orleans Saints trailed for most of the game in Baltimore, then scored the last 15 points to beat the Ravens 24–17 on Sunday. Tyler Shough capped a 16-play drive with a 1-yard touchdown run with 1:32 left, and the Saints, who closed as 8.5-point underdogs, evened their record at 1-1.

Baltimore controlled the first half. Derrick Henry's 1-yard run late in the first quarter put the Ravens ahead, and Lamar Jackson's 22-yard touchdown pass to Rashod Bateman with 28 seconds left in the half made it 14–3. Daniel Carlson answered with a 47-yard field goal just before halftime and a 51-yarder early in the third quarter, but Tyler Loop's 49-yard kick late in the third made it 17–9.

New Orleans owned the ball from there. Shough found Chris Olave for a 21-yard touchdown midway through the fourth quarter to tie it at 17, then led a 68-yard drive that began with 8:06 left and ended with his own run. Shough completed 27 of 34 passes for 252 yards, Olave caught eight for 86, and the Saints held the ball for 32:45 and converted eight of 15 third downs without a turnover.

Baltimore had one chance left, and Jackson moved the Ravens 34 yards from their 29 before Julian Blackmon intercepted him with 20 seconds remaining. Jackson finished 21 of 31 for 235 yards. The comeback left both teams at 1-1, with the Ravens unable to hold an 11-point lead at home.

2026_02_NYG_LA.headline: Adams catches 195 yards, two scores as Rams beat Giants 28–6
paragraphs: The New York Giants lost Jaxson Dart on their opening drive, and the Los Angeles Rams gave them no way back on Monday night. Matthew Stafford threw four touchdown passes, two to Davante Adams, in a 28–6 win at SoFi Stadium that left both teams 1-1.

Dart was hurt early in the first quarter and did not return. Jameis Winston completed 11 of 27 passes for 111 yards in relief, and New York finished with 182 yards, 3.3 per play, and three conversions on 14 third downs. Stafford hit Adams for a 31-yard touchdown with 19 seconds left in the first quarter and found Kyren Williams from 10 yards early in the second.

Three turnovers in the last 6:31 of the first half changed little. Trent McDuffie intercepted Winston in the end zone, Jevon Holland picked off Stafford on the Rams' next possession, and a Williams fumble set up Dominic Zvada's 24-yard field goal, the only points from the stretch. Los Angeles led 14–3 at halftime.

Adams finished with eight catches for 195 yards, and his 11-yard touchdown midway through the third quarter made it 21–3. Stafford, 22 of 31 for 327 yards, closed the scoring with a 5-yard pass to Terrance Ferguson midway through the fourth.

Los Angeles outgained New York 481-182, averaged 8.0 yards per play and scored touchdowns on all three of its red-zone trips. The Giants went zero for two inside the 20, and their only points came on two Zvada field goals.

2026_02_PHI_TEN.headline: Hurts finds Cooper with 14 seconds left as Eagles edge Titans 24–20
paragraphs: Jalen Hurts' second interception set up the field goal that put Tennessee ahead late in the fourth quarter, and he answered with a 65-yard drive that ended in a 3-yard touchdown pass to Darius Cooper with 14 seconds left. The Philadelphia Eagles won 24–20 on Sunday to move to 2-0, and the Titans fell to 0-2.

Tennessee scored first after Amani Hooker intercepted Hurts in the end zone, with Cam Ward running in from a yard out late in the first quarter. Philadelphia answered with 14 unanswered points, on Tank Bigsby's 2-yard run and Hurts' 22-yard touchdown pass to DeVonta Smith, and led 14–10 at halftime after a Joey Slye field goal.

The lead changed hands three times. Jake Elliott's 58-yard field goal and Ward's second 1-yard touchdown run left it tied at 17 entering the fourth quarter. Marcus Harris then intercepted Hurts midway through the period, and Ward led a 69-yard drive that ended with Slye's 33-yard field goal with 2:00 left.

Hurts took over at his 35 with 1:56 to play and needed nine plays, one of them a 20-yard completion to Dontayvion Wicks, to reach the end zone. He finished 26 of 37 for 264 yards, and Smith caught 10 passes for 117 yards.

Philadelphia held the ball for 36:25 and converted 11 of 18 third downs, enough to outlast its two giveaways. Tennessee played without a turnover and averaged 5.7 yards per play but dropped its second straight game. The Eagles lost Jalen Carter to an injury late in the fourth quarter; he did not return.

2026_02_PIT_NE.headline: Patriots hold Steelers to a field goal in 20–3 win
paragraphs: The New England Patriots held the Pittsburgh Steelers to 235 yards and a single field goal, and a fourth-quarter fumble return finished off a 20–3 win at Gillette Stadium on Sunday. Both teams left at 1-1.

TreVeyon Henderson's 39-yard touchdown run midway through the first quarter capped a four-play drive that began at the Pittsburgh 49, and Andy Borregales added a 30-yard field goal early in the second. Chris Boswell's 56-yarder with five seconds left in the half was all Pittsburgh managed.

The Steelers could not sustain drives. They converted two of 12 third downs, averaged 3.5 yards per play and punted eight times, and Aaron Rodgers was sacked four times while completing 23 of 39 passes for 187 yards. New England's own mistakes, a Rhamondre Stevenson fumble in the first quarter and Patrick Queen's interception of Drake Maye early in the third, cost nothing; Pittsburgh punted after both.

Maye completed 14 of 22 passes for 208 yards, and Romeo Doubs turned three catches into 96 yards, including a 63-yarder late in the third quarter before Borregales' 45-yard field goal made it 13–3. Early in the fourth, Rodgers fumbled on a sack and Elijah Ponder returned it for a touchdown, making it 20–3. Gabe Jacas later intercepted Rodgers.
Pittsburgh never reached the end zone. New England sacked Rodgers four times and took the ball away twice, and its own two giveaways cost nothing.

2026_02_SEA_ARI.headline: Smith-Njigba catches three touchdowns as Seahawks beat Cardinals 31–7
paragraphs: The Seattle Seahawks were tied with Arizona at halftime, then scored the last 24 points to beat the Cardinals 31–7 on Sunday. Drew Lock threw all three of his touchdown passes to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and Seattle moved to 2-0.

Smith-Njigba's first score was an 82-yarder on a two-play drive early in the first quarter. Jacoby Brissett tied it at the start of the second with a 2-yard touchdown pass to Trey McBride, the end of a 12-play drive, and neither team scored again before the break. Arizona did nothing with a Jadarian Price fumble early in the second quarter.

Seattle took control early in the third. Lock found Smith-Njigba from 7 yards to finish a four-play drive, and Julian Love's interception of Brissett soon after led to Jason Myers' 33-yard field goal. Smith-Njigba's 12-yard catch early in the fourth made it 24–7, and AJ Barner's 1-yard run with 1:15 left capped a 16-play, 70-yard drive.

Smith-Njigba finished with nine catches for 155 yards, and Lock completed 19 of 26 passes for 235 yards without an interception. Seattle ran 40 times for 162 yards, Emanuel Wilson carrying 21 times for 92, and held the ball for 36:33.

Arizona had no answer after halftime. The Cardinals gained 151 yards, 3.2 per play, converted three of 12 third downs and punted seven times, and Brissett completed 17 of 28 passes for 95 yards. Seattle outgained them 381-151, and Arizona fell to 1-1.

2026_03_ARI_SF.headline: Purdy throws four touchdowns as 49ers hold off Cardinals 36–30
paragraphs: Arizona pulled within 29–27 late in the fourth quarter, and Brock Purdy answered with a 65-yard drive that ended in his second touchdown pass to George Kittle, carrying the San Francisco 49ers to a 36–30 win on Sunday. The 49ers improved to 3-0, and the Cardinals fell to 1-2 with a second straight loss.

San Francisco built its lead fast. Purdy hit Mike Evans for an 82-yard touchdown midway through the first quarter and found him again from 23 yards at the start of the second, but Evans was hurt late in the half and did not return. Christian McCaffrey's 1-yard run early in the third quarter made it 23–6.

Arizona came back by keeping the ball. Jacoby Brissett completed 38 of 52 passes for 280 yards, the Cardinals held possession for 38:44, and touchdowns by Michael Wilson and Jeremiyah Love, 14 unanswered points, cut the lead to 23–20 early in the fourth quarter. Kittle's 10-yard catch midway through the quarter and Brissett's 1-yard run made it 29–27.
Purdy then ran for 35 yards, and Kittle caught a 20-yard touchdown with 1:36 left for a 36–27 lead. Chad Ryland's 49-yard field goal with 39 seconds remaining was Arizona's last score.

The 49ers had the ball for just 21:16 but averaged 8.7 yards per play, and Purdy's 297 yards came on 15 completions. Kittle finished with six catches for 82 yards and two scores, and McCaffrey added 116 yards from scrimmage. San Francisco stayed unbeaten, while Arizona has lost two straight.

2026_02_WAS_DAL.headline: Prescott throws four touchdowns as Cowboys beat Commanders 37–20
paragraphs: Washington lost Jayden Daniels at the end of the first half and trailed 20–13 in the third quarter when a fumble handed Dallas the ball at the Washington 13. The Dallas Cowboys turned it into a touchdown and pulled away for a 37–20 win at AT&T Stadium on Sunday, evening their record at 1-1 and dropping the Commanders to 0-2.

Dak Prescott's 3-yard touchdown pass to CeeDee Lamb and Brandon Aubrey's 25-yard field goal put Dallas up 10–0 in the first quarter, and Jake Ferguson's 10-yard catch made it 17–3. Daniels answered with a 4-yard scoring pass to Stefon Diggs before he was hurt with three seconds left in the half. Marcus Mariota took over.

Drew Stevens' 47-yard field goal early in the third quarter cut the lead to 17–13. Aubrey answered from 44 yards, Dyami Brown fumbled after a catch moments later, and Prescott found Ferguson for a 12-yard touchdown two plays after that. Aubrey's 60-yard field goal early in the fourth made it 13 unanswered points.

Mariota's 20-yard touchdown pass to Diggs made it 30–20 midway through the fourth, but Dallas answered with an 11-play, 83-yard drive that ended in Lamb's 24-yard touchdown with 3:13 left. Lamb finished with eight catches for 153 yards.

Washington outgained Dallas 389 to 332 and ran for 182 yards, but it scored one touchdown in three red-zone trips. The Cowboys converted seven of 11 third downs and did not turn the ball over, though they lost Ferguson to an injury midway through the fourth quarter.

2026_03_ATL_GB.headline: Bijan Robinson runs for 194 yards as Falcons beat Packers 35–14
paragraphs: Green Bay took an early lead on Thursday night, and the Atlanta Falcons answered with 27 unanswered points on the way to a 35–14 win at Lambeau Field. The Packers closed as 4.5-point favorites; both teams are now 1-2.

Jordan Love's 4-yard touchdown pass to Christian Watson put Green Bay ahead midway through the first quarter. Bijan Robinson tied it late in the quarter with a 3-yard run, finishing a drive that included his 55-yard burst, and Michael Penix Jr.'s 5-yard touchdown pass to Austin Hooper with 1:02 left in the half made it 17–7. Brian Robinson Jr. capped a 92-yard drive late in the third, and Nick Folk's 31-yard field goal early in the fourth made it 27–7.

Atlanta wore Green Bay down on the ground. Bijan Robinson carried 29 times for 194 yards, the Falcons ran for 242 as a team and held the ball for 37:05, and they converted four of five red-zone trips. Penix completed 18 of 25 passes for 256 yards, and Drake London caught nine for 194.

Green Bay never found a running game, finishing with 17 yards on nine carries. Love completed 28 of 53 passes for 312 yards, and his 15-yard touchdown to Matthew Golden made it 27–14 midway through the fourth. Bijan Robinson's 2-yard run with 3:35 left answered it, and Xavier Watts intercepted Love on the final drive.
Atlanta's only giveaway, a Penix interception early in the first quarter, ended in a Green Bay punt, and the Falcons were never sacked.

2026_03_BAL_DAL.headline: Loop's 56-yard field goal with one second left lifts Ravens past Cowboys 34–31
paragraphs: Dallas tied the game with 10 seconds left in Rio de Janeiro, and the Baltimore Ravens still had time for one more kick. Lamar Jackson hit Zay Flowers for 27 yards, and Tyler Loop made a 56-yard field goal with one second remaining to give Baltimore a 34–31 win over the Cowboys on Sunday. Baltimore moved to 2-1, and Dallas fell to 1-2.

The Cowboys led 10–0 in the first quarter on Brandon Aubrey's 28-yard field goal and Javonte Williams' 2-yard run. Derrick Henry answered with two short touchdown runs, and Loop's 27-yard field goal finished a run of 17 unanswered points. Baltimore led 17–13 at halftime and 24–13 after Jackson's 4-yard touchdown pass to Chris Moore late in the third quarter.

Dallas then scored 15 straight. Dak Prescott's 19-yard touchdown pass to Jake Ferguson came late in the third, and KaVontae Turpin finished a 96-yard drive with a 9-yard touchdown run midway through the fourth for a 28–24 lead.
Jackson answered with an 11-play, 64-yard drive that ended with a 2-yard touchdown pass to Matthew Hibner with 1:34 left. Aubrey's 23-yard field goal tied it, leaving Baltimore seven seconds.

Jackson completed 15 of 20 passes for 186 yards and ran for 50 more, and Henry carried 26 times for 89 yards. Dallas outgained Baltimore 415 to 378, but the Ravens did not turn the ball over and were not sacked, while the Cowboys lost a Ferguson fumble early in the third quarter and Aubrey made three of four field goal tries.

2026_03_CAR_CLE.headline: Watson hits Fannin late as Browns edge Panthers 21–18
paragraphs: Deshaun Watson was hurt with 2:36 left and Cleveland trailing, and he was back in time to throw the winning touchdown. His 14-yard pass to Harold Fannin Jr. with 1:55 remaining gave the Cleveland Browns a 21–18 win over the Carolina Panthers on Sunday, their second straight victory, and moved them to 2-1.

Neither team scored in the first quarter. Andre Szmyt's 48-yard field goal midway through the second quarter and Watson's 2-yard touchdown pass to Fannin late in it put Cleveland ahead, and Ryan Fitzgerald's 35-yarder made it 10–3 at halftime.

Carolina kicked its way in front. Fitzgerald, who made all four of his field goals, connected twice in the third quarter, the second from 53 yards, and again from 37 early in the fourth for a 12–10 lead. Szmyt's 45-yarder put Cleveland back ahead, and Bryce Young's 8-yard touchdown pass to John Metchie III with 4:29 left made it 18–13 in a game with four lead changes.

Watson then led a 65-yard drive that included his 21-yard run and finished it with the pass to Fannin. Carolina got one more chance after Cleveland turned it over on downs, but Ronnie Hickman intercepted Young with 16 seconds left.

Carolina outgained Cleveland 360 to 259, but Young needed 48 attempts for his 291 yards, and the Panthers converted four of 15 third downs and scored one touchdown in three red-zone trips. Mason Graham sacked Young twice, and Carolina fell to 1-2.

2026_03_HOU_IND.headline: Shrader's 53-yarder late lifts Colts past Texans 19–17
paragraphs: Daniel Jones' third turnover set up the touchdown that put Houston ahead with 1:50 left, and Spencer Shrader took the lead back. Shrader's 53-yard field goal with 21 seconds remaining, his fourth of the game, gave the Indianapolis Colts a 19–17 win over the Texans on Sunday and left Houston 0-3.

Indianapolis controlled the ball but kept settling for kicks. Shrader's 39-yard field goal and Jones' 6-yard touchdown pass to Keenan Allen made it 10–0, C.J. Stroud answered with a 1-yard scoring pass to Foster Moreau, and Shrader's 58-yarder late in the half made it 13–7. The Colts held the ball for 35:13 but reached the end zone once in three red-zone trips.

Houston's pass rush kept the game close. Will Anderson Jr. finished with 2.5 sacks, Jones fumbled on a sack in the first quarter and Reed Blankenship intercepted him early in the third, though the Texans got no points from either. After Shrader's 37-yard field goal early in the fourth and Ka'imi Fairbairn's 24-yarder made it 16–10, Jones fumbled on another sack late in the quarter, and Woody Marks scored from a yard out for a 17–16 Houston lead.

Jones answered from his own 35. A 20-yard completion to Laquon Treadwell kept the drive moving, and Shrader finished it. Jones completed 24 of 36 passes for 235 yards, and Indianapolis held Houston to 223 yards.
The Colts improved to 1-2 despite three giveaways, while Houston, which did not turn the ball over, lost its third straight.

2026_03_KC_MIA.headline: Mahomes completes 20 of 24 as Chiefs beat Dolphins 24–10
paragraphs: Miami lost De'Von Achane on its opening drive and Ollie Gordon II in the third quarter, and the Kansas City Chiefs scored the last 10 points to beat the Dolphins 24–10 on Sunday. Kansas City is 3-0; Miami is 0-3.

Kenneth Walker III scored on a 10-yard run early in the first quarter and on a 5-yard catch early in the second, around Gordon's 3-yard touchdown run that finished a 17-play, 91-yard Miami drive. Patrick Mahomes completed 20 of 24 passes for 246 yards and was not sacked.

The turnovers late in the half canceled out. Malik Willis fumbled and Kansas City recovered, but Jacob Rodriguez intercepted Mahomes on the next possession, and Miami punted. Riley Patterson's 37-yard field goal early in the third quarter cut the lead to 14–10, and those were the Dolphins' last points.

Kansas City put it away in the fourth. Starting at its own 4, it drove 80 yards in 13 plays for Harrison Butker's 34-yard field goal, and Mahomes found Travis Kelce for an 11-yard touchdown with 3:01 left. George Karlaftis then intercepted Willis to end Miami's last drive.

Miami held the ball for 34:21 and converted eight of 16 third downs, but it scored one touchdown in two red-zone trips, and Willis completed 20 of 36 passes for 210 yards. The Chiefs averaged 6.8 yards per play to the Dolphins' 4.9, enough to stay unbeaten as Miami lost its third straight.

2026_03_LAC_BUF.headline: Bills overcome five turnovers to beat Chargers 24–16
paragraphs: The Buffalo Bills turned the ball over five times and still beat the Los Angeles Chargers 24–16 on Sunday, because Los Angeles scored one touchdown in four red-zone trips. James Cook III ran for 154 yards, and Buffalo moved to 3-0 while the Chargers fell to 0-3.

Buffalo's mistakes came early. Cook fumbled early in the first quarter, and Justin Herbert's 1-yard touchdown pass to Keaton Mitchell followed. Genesis Smith then intercepted Josh Allen twice, late in the first quarter, which led to Cameron Dicker's 31-yard field goal and a 10–0 lead, and at the start of the second, which ended in a missed field goal.

Buffalo steadied before halftime. Tyler Bass kicked a 28-yard field goal, and Allen's 1-yard run with 19 seconds left tied it 10–10. Dicker's 21-yarder put Los Angeles back in front midway through the third, and a Dalton Kincaid fumble late in the quarter came to nothing.

The fourth quarter opened with Allen fumbling on a sack, but C.J. Gardner-Johnson intercepted Herbert on the Chargers' next possession, and Buffalo drove 58 yards in 13 plays for Allen's second 1-yard touchdown run and a 17–13 lead midway through the quarter. Cook, who carried 24 times, added a 3-yard touchdown with 3:16 left, and Dicker's 33-yard field goal was the last score.
Herbert completed 20 of 34 passes for 226 yards and was sacked twice by Greg Rousseau. Buffalo's 176 rushing yards and a defense that gave up one touchdown were enough to cover five giveaways.

2026_03_LV_NO.headline: Raiders score the last 19 points to beat Saints 35–27
paragraphs: New Orleans led by 11 points in the third quarter, then turned the ball over four times in the fourth, and the Las Vegas Raiders scored the last 19 points to win 35–27 on Sunday. The Raiders, who closed as 3.5-point underdogs, are 3-0; the Saints fell to 1-2.

The first half was even. Tyler Shough threw touchdown passes to Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant, Kirk Cousins found Michael Mayer, and Matt Gay's 25-yard field goal with four seconds left gave Las Vegas a 16–13 halftime lead. New Orleans then scored 14 unanswered points in the third quarter, including Shough's 1-yard pass to Johnson, to lead 27–16.

Mike Washington Jr.'s 36-yard touchdown run late in the third cut it to 27–22. Early in the fourth, Shough fumbled on a sack, and Cousins turned the takeaway into a 4-yard touchdown pass to Cody White for a 28–27 lead midway through the quarter. Hezekiah Masses then intercepted Shough, and Las Vegas started at the New Orleans 4, from where Cousins found Brock Bowers for a 35–27 lead.

The Saints gave the ball away twice more: Shough fumbled on another sack late in the game, and Johnson lost a fumble with 1:02 left. Shough finished 29 of 42 for 255 yards and four touchdowns, and New Orleans scored touchdowns on all four of its red-zone trips.
Cousins completed 22 of 33 passes for 248 yards and three touchdowns without an interception, and Bowers caught 10 passes for 116 yards. New Orleans lost a game it led through three quarters.

2026_03_LA_DEN.headline: Hufanga's two interceptions carry Broncos past Rams 30–26
paragraphs: Denver trailed 16–0 at halftime on Sunday night and won because Talanoa Hufanga intercepted Matthew Stafford twice in the fourth quarter, returning one for a touchdown and taking the other in the end zone with two seconds left. Bo Nix's 1-yard run with 48 seconds remaining gave the Denver Broncos a 30–26 win over the Los Angeles Rams, their second straight, and a 2-1 record.

Los Angeles controlled the first half but kept settling for field goals. Stafford's 5-yard touchdown pass to Tyler Higbee was followed by three Harrison Mevis kicks, the last with three seconds left in the half. The Rams outgained Denver 482 to 257 but scored one touchdown in four red-zone trips.

Denver tied it in the third quarter with 16 unanswered points on Nix touchdown passes to Pat Bryant and Nate Adkins. Josh Wallace's interception of Nix early in the fourth set up a 48-yard Mevis field goal for a 19–16 lead, but Hufanga intercepted Stafford midway through the quarter and returned it for a touchdown to put Denver up 23–19.

Stafford answered with a 48-yard touchdown pass to Konata Mumpfield with 3:46 left, and Nix responded with a 65-yard drive, helped by a 39-yard completion to Bryant, that ended with his own 1-yard run. Stafford, who finished 30 of 55 for 390 yards, moved the Rams 48 yards on the final possession before Hufanga's second interception.
Hufanga also had a sack, and Denver scored on all three of its red-zone trips. The Rams fell to 1-2 despite 158 yards from scrimmage by Kyren Williams.

2026_03_MIN_TB.headline: Reichard's three field goals help Vikings outlast Buccaneers 23–16
paragraphs: Neither offense could convert on third down, and the Minnesota Vikings leaned on their kicker. Will Reichard made field goals from 54, 56 and 43 yards, Minnesota sacked Tampa Bay quarterbacks six times, and the Vikings beat the Buccaneers 23–16 on Sunday to move to 3-0. Tampa Bay fell to 0-3.

Reichard's 54-yarder opened the scoring early in the first quarter, and the teams traded touchdowns, Tampa Bay's on Ted Hurst III's only catch, a 40-yard score, leaving Minnesota ahead 10–7 after one quarter. Chase McLaughlin tied it with a 28-yard field goal midway through the second, and Kyler Murray answered with a 41-yard touchdown pass to Jordan Addison late in the half for a 17–10 lead.

The second half belonged to the defenses. A'Shawn Robinson intercepted Murray midway through the third, setting up McLaughlin's 38-yard field goal, and his 54-yarder midway through the fourth made it 17–16. The teams combined for 16 punts, and Minnesota converted two of 15 third downs to Tampa Bay's two of 17.

Reichard's 56-yard field goal with 3:15 left made it 20–16. Andrew Van Ginkel intercepted Baker Mayfield with 1:54 left, and Reichard added a 43-yarder. Mayfield, hurt with 1:54 remaining, did not return, and Isaiah Rodgers intercepted his replacement, Jalon Daniels, with eight seconds left.
Minnesota gained only 230 yards, but a pass rush led by Eric Wilson and Kyle Van Noy, with 1.5 sacks each, held Tampa Bay to 3.8 yards per play and out of the end zone on both of its red-zone trips.

2026_03_NE_JAX.headline: Jaguars turn Maye's turnovers into 35–6 rout of Patriots
paragraphs: New England gained more yards than Jacksonville on Sunday and lost by 29 points. Drake Maye turned the ball over three times, the Patriots scored no touchdowns on three red-zone trips, and the Jacksonville Jaguars won 35–6 to move to 2-1. New England fell to 1-2.

Maye's fumble on a sack late in the first quarter set up Trevor Lawrence's 12-yard touchdown pass to Josh Cameron early in the second. New England's only answer was Andy Borregales' 35-yard field goal after Marcus Jones intercepted Lawrence, and Lawrence's 10-yard touchdown pass to Jakobi Meyers late in the quarter made it 14–3. Travis Hunter then intercepted Maye in the end zone before halftime.

Jacksonville put it away in the last two minutes of the third quarter. Lawrence finished a 15-play, 72-yard drive with a 17-yard touchdown pass to Parker Washington, Jarrian Jones intercepted Maye moments later, and Chris Rodriguez Jr. scored from 5 yards on the following play for a 28–3 lead.

Lawrence completed 19 of 29 passes for 182 yards and three touchdowns, and Jacksonville scored touchdowns on all five of its red-zone trips and converted eight of 12 third downs. Bhayshul Tuten's 1-yard run midway through the fourth closed the scoring.

Maye completed 14 of 25 passes for 199 yards with two interceptions, and Mack Hollins caught six for 87. The Patriots' last drive covered 48 yards and ended on downs, and their only points came on two Borregales field goals.

2026_03_NYJ_DET.headline: Gibbs scores three times as Lions hold off Jets 31–24
paragraphs: The New York Jets erased a 24–10 deficit in the fourth quarter, and Detroit needed four plays to answer. Jared Goff's 49-yard completion to Isaac TeSlaa on the first of them and his 11-yard touchdown pass to Jahmyr Gibbs with 2:30 left gave the Detroit Lions a 31–24 win on Sunday.

Geno Smith's 24-yard touchdown pass to Kenyon Sadiq midway through the second quarter gave New York its only lead, and Goff's 4-yard touchdown pass to Amon-Ra St. Brown late in the half put Detroit ahead 10–7 at the break. Gibbs ran 17 yards for a touchdown early in the third, and his 1-yard run on the first play of the fourth quarter made it 24–10.

Smith brought the Jets back. He found Jeremy Ruckert for a 4-yard touchdown early in the fourth and Garrett Wilson for 23 yards with 4:11 left to tie it. Smith completed 31 of 37 passes for 321 yards and three touchdowns, with Wilson catching 10 for 107 and Sadiq seven for 105.

Gibbs finished with 99 rushing yards on 20 carries and 164 yards from scrimmage. Detroit sacked Smith five times, twice by DJ Wonnum, and Smith fumbled on a sack with 51 seconds left, with the Lions recovering to close it out.

Detroit did not turn the ball over and scored touchdowns on four of five red-zone trips. The Lions improved to 2-1; the Jets, who lost Breece Hall to an injury early in the fourth quarter and Wilson in the final minute, fell to 1-2 with a second straight loss.

2026_03_PHI_CHI.headline: Keenum accounts for three touchdowns as Bears beat Eagles 27–7
paragraphs: Philadelphia turned the ball over three times on Monday night, and the Chicago Bears turned two of those giveaways into points on the way to a 27–7 win at Soldier Field. The Eagles closed as 3-point favorites; both teams are now 2-1.

Case Keenum's 8-yard touchdown pass to Luther Burden III midway through the first quarter put Chicago ahead, and a Tank Bigsby fumble late in the quarter came to nothing for either side. Jalen Hurts was hurt midway through the second quarter, and with Andy Dalton in the game, Dillon Thieneman intercepted him in the end zone; Chicago followed with Cairo Santos' 29-yard field goal. Hurts returned and ran in from a yard out with one second left in the half to make it 10–7.

Chicago scored the last 17 points. Santos hit from 48 yards early in the third, Keenum found Kalif Raymond for a 41-yard touchdown midway through the quarter, and after T.J. Edwards intercepted Hurts late in the third, the Bears drove 58 yards in 13 plays for Keenum's 1-yard touchdown run midway through the fourth.

Keenum completed 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards without an interception and was not sacked, Raymond caught six passes for 90 yards, and D'Andre Swift carried 20 times for 84. Chicago held the ball for 36:53.

Philadelphia finished with 248 yards and converted two of nine third downs. Hurts completed 16 of 25 passes for 153 yards, Saquon Barkley ran 15 times for 82, and the Eagles' last possession ended on downs.

2026_03_SEA_WAS.headline: Medrano's pick-six lifts Commanders past Seahawks 33–31
paragraphs: Seattle outgained Washington 437 to 258 and still lost, because each of its three turnovers became a Washington touchdown. The last, Kain Medrano's interception return late in the fourth quarter, held up in the Washington Commanders' 33–31 win on Sunday as 8.5-point underdogs. Washington is 1-2; Seattle fell to 2-1.

Jadarian Price's fumble early in the first quarter set up Marcus Mariota's 6-yard touchdown pass to Rachaad White. Sam Darnold answered with a 1-yard scoring pass to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Mariota found Treylon Burks from 11 yards, and Jason Myers and Drew Stevens traded 57-yard field goals late in the half for a 17–10 Washington lead.

Sonny Styles intercepted Darnold early in the third, and Mariota hit Terry McLaurin for a 30-yard touchdown three plays later for a 24–10 lead. Seattle answered with 14 unanswered points, on Darnold's touchdown passes to Eric Saubert and Smith-Njigba, to tie it 24–24 early in the fourth.

Washington then put together a 12-play drive for Stevens' 36-yard field goal with 4:39 left, and on Seattle's next possession Medrano intercepted Darnold and returned it for a touchdown to make it 33–24. Darnold's 7-yard touchdown pass to Cooper Kupp with 2:55 left made it 33–31, but the Seahawks did not score again.

Darnold completed 31 of 45 passes for 379 yards and four touchdowns, and Smith-Njigba caught 10 for 128. Mariota threw three touchdown passes without a turnover, which was enough for an offense that averaged 4.0 yards per play and converted three of 13 third downs.

2026_03_TEN_NYG.headline: Zvada kicks four field goals as Giants hold off Titans 12–7
paragraphs: Tennessee's last drive covered 70 yards, and Jevon Holland ended it by intercepting Cam Ward in the end zone with 24 seconds left, preserving the New York Giants' 12–7 win on Sunday. Dominic Zvada made all four of his field goals, and the Giants improved to 2-1 while the Titans fell to 0-3.

Zvada supplied all of New York's points. Tennessee lost a fumble at the start of the game, and the Giants' next possession ended in his 39-yard field goal. He added a 27-yarder and another 39-yarder with three seconds left in the half for a 9–0 lead, and his 30-yarder midway through the third made it 12–0. The Giants reached the red zone twice without scoring a touchdown.

Tennessee did not score until midway through the fourth quarter, when Ward capped a 13-play, 91-yard drive with a 4-yard touchdown pass to Wan'Dale Robinson. New York punted after four plays, and Ward moved the Titans from their 23 before Holland's interception.

Jameis Winston completed 14 of 22 passes for 118 yards, and Cam Skattebo had 100 yards from scrimmage as New York ran 33 times for 138 yards and held the ball for 34:26. Ward finished 23 of 36 for 181 yards, and Joey Slye missed his only field goal attempt, leaving the Titans winless after three games.

2026_04_ARI_NYG.headline: Banks' late pick-six finishes Giants' 36–24 win over Cardinals
paragraphs: Arizona trailed 30–24 and had driven 63 yards on its final possession when Deonte Banks intercepted Jacoby Brissett and returned it for a touchdown with 11 seconds left, finishing the New York Giants' 36–24 win on Sunday. The Giants, who trailed 14–3 in the first quarter, improved to 3-1 with their second straight win; the Cardinals fell to 1-3 with a third straight loss.

Brissett's 12-yard touchdown pass to Marvin Harrison Jr. and Tyler Allgeier's 22-yard run, around a 39-yard Dominic Zvada field goal, built the early lead. New York answered with 16 unanswered points: Zvada's 50-yard field goal, Jameis Winston's 12-yard touchdown pass to Malachi Fields and, after Arvell Reese intercepted Brissett, a 25-yard scoring throw to Malik Nabers two plays later.

The interceptions kept coming, and the next two produced points for Arizona. Denzel Burke picked off Winston late in the half, setting up Chad Ryland's 60-yard field goal with two seconds left, and Budda Baker intercepted him early in the third quarter before Brissett's 2-yard touchdown pass to Elijah Higgins put the Cardinals back ahead 24–19.

Winston answered late in the third with an 11-yard touchdown pass to Theo Johnson for a 27–24 lead, and Zvada's 52-yard field goal with 2:16 left made it 30–24. Winston finished with 250 yards and three touchdowns, and Nabers caught six passes for 112 yards.

New York scored the last 17 points despite three turnovers of its own, including a Najee Harris fumble early in the fourth that Arizona could not convert, and its defense intercepted Brissett three times.

2026_04_ATL_NO.headline: Bijan Robinson runs for 145 yards as Falcons rout Saints 45–24
paragraphs: Bijan Robinson broke a 59-yard touchdown run early in the first quarter, and the Atlanta Falcons ran through the New Orleans Saints from there, winning 45–24 on Monday night. Robinson finished with 145 yards on 19 carries, and Brian Robinson Jr. added three short touchdown runs as Atlanta evened its record at 2-2.

The Saints helped build the early gap. Kendre Miller fumbled late in the first quarter, Atlanta recovered, and Bijan Robinson's 4-yard run on the next possession made it 14–0. Alvin Kamara scored to open the second quarter, but Robinson Jr. and a 29-yard field goal by Nick Folk sent Atlanta to halftime ahead 24–7.

The Falcons rarely stalled. They ran for 205 yards, averaged 7.5 yards per play, went 4 of 5 in the red zone and punted only twice. Michael Penix Jr. completed 15 of 20 passes for 223 yards, and his 31-yard touchdown pass to Jahan Dotson midway through the fourth quarter made it 38–17 after New Orleans had pulled within 31–17.

New Orleans moved the ball through the air but could not run it. Tyler Shough completed 30 of 48 passes for 286 yards and Chris Olave caught eight for 116, while the Saints managed 50 yards on the ground. Kamara scored twice, and Shough's 3-yard touchdown pass to Devaughn Vele came with 1:19 left. The division win was the Falcons' second straight victory; the Saints fell to 1-3 with their second straight loss.

2026_04_DAL_HOU.headline: Prescott hits Lamb with 43 seconds left as Cowboys rally past Texans 34–30
paragraphs: Houston kicked its way to a 16–6 halftime lead, and Dallas spent the second half running it down. Dak Prescott's 12-yard touchdown pass to CeeDee Lamb with 43 seconds left gave the Cowboys a 34–30 win on Sunday and handed the Texans, favored by 3, their fourth straight loss.

Ka'imi Fairbairn made all three of his field goals in the first half, the last from 54 yards with two seconds left, while Dallas settled for two from Brandon Aubrey. The Cowboys found the end zone after the break. Javonte Williams scored on runs of 8, 1 and 2 yards, the last finishing a 14-play, 81-yard drive early in the fourth quarter that gave Dallas its first lead, 27–23.
