C.J. Stroud kept Houston in it. He passed for 347 yards, two of his touchdowns going to Nico Collins, and Woody Marks' 6-yard run with 2:26 left finished an 87-yard drive and put Houston back in front 30–27.

Dallas needed 11 plays and 74 yards to answer, and Prescott's 22-yard completion to George Pickens set up the winning throw. Lamb caught 17 of his 21 targets for 189 yards, and Prescott threw for 335. Neither team turned the ball over, but the Cowboys went 4 of 4 in the red zone and held the ball for 33:27 while outscoring Houston 28–14 after halftime. Dallas evened its record at 2-2; Houston fell to 0-4.

2026_04_DEN_SF.headline: Kittle's 56-yard touchdown seals 49ers' 24–14 win over Broncos
paragraphs: A game tied 3–3 at halftime turned on San Francisco's answers in the fourth quarter, and the 49ers beat the Denver Broncos 24–14 on Sunday to move to 4-0.

San Francisco took the lead late in the third quarter, when Brock Purdy hit Deebo Samuel Sr. for a 1-yard touchdown at the end of a 28-yard drive. Wil Lutz's 40-yard field goal early in the fourth cut it to 10–6, and the 49ers responded with a 74-yard drive that Christian McCaffrey finished with a 1-yard run.

Denver kept coming. Bo Nix found Jaylen Waddle for a 13-yard touchdown with 4:10 left, pulling the Broncos within 17–14. Purdy needed five plays to respond, the last a 56-yard touchdown pass to George Kittle with 2:25 to go, and Denver's final drive ended with a missed field goal.

Nix completed 25 of 42 passes for 214 yards and RJ Harvey caught all 10 of his targets, but Denver averaged 4.6 yards per play and reached the red zone only once. The Broncos also lost Pat Surtain II in the final minute of the first half and Pat Bryant late in the third quarter; neither returned. San Francisco, which ran for 140 yards and was not sacked, won its fourth straight. Denver fell to 2-2.

2026_04_DET_CAR.headline: McMillan catches 14 passes for 192 yards as Panthers top Lions 32–26
paragraphs: Detroit kept pace with Carolina for most of Sunday night, but it kept settling for field goals while the Panthers finished drives. Tetairoa McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and two touchdowns, and Carolina beat the Lions 32–26 as a 3.5-point underdog.

Jake Bates made all four of his field goals, the third from 41 yards with five seconds left in the first half to tie it 16–16. Carolina pulled ahead after the break. Bryce Young found McMillan for a 10-yard touchdown midway through the third quarter, and Chuba Hubbard's 2-yard run late in the quarter, at the end of an 85-yard drive, made it 29–19.

Jared Goff threw for 412 yards, completing 32 of 52 passes, and Jameson Williams caught six for 102. But Detroit ran for 46 yards on 15 carries and scored touchdowns on only two of its four trips inside the red zone, and Bates' 26-yard field goal midway through the third was the Lions' only answer in the second half until late.

Young completed 29 of 41 passes for 329 yards and Hubbard ran for 122, part of an offense that held the ball for 33:15 and did not turn it over. Goff's 8-yard touchdown pass to Sam LaPorta with 3:42 left cut the lead to 32–26, but Detroit's last drive, from its own 13, ended on downs. Both teams are 2-2.

2026_04_GB_TB.headline: Packers cash in on two interceptions, hold off Buccaneers 17–14
paragraphs: Green Bay turned both of Jalon Daniels' interceptions into points, then survived two turnovers of its own in the fourth quarter to beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 17–14 on Sunday.

Evan Williams' interception in the first quarter led to a 16-play drive that Jordan Love finished with a 2-yard touchdown pass to Matthew Golden. After Sean Tucker tied it, Edgerrin Cooper picked off Daniels with 41 seconds left in the half, and Trey Smack made a 58-yard field goal with two seconds left for a 10–7 lead. Love's 2-yard scoring pass to Tucker Kraft early in the third quarter, at the end of an 80-yard drive, made it 17–7.

Daniels' 10-yard touchdown pass to Kenny Gainwell seconds into the fourth quarter finished an 84-yard drive and pulled Tampa Bay within 17–14. Green Bay then gave the Buccaneers two more chances. Kaleb Johnson lost a fumble midway through the quarter, and Tampa Bay punted; Jacob Parrish intercepted Love with 4:26 left, and the Buccaneers' final drive, from their own 15, ended on downs.

Tampa Bay outrushed Green Bay 141 to 86, and Daniels added 55 yards on the ground, but he threw for 148 and Tampa Bay was sacked three times. Love completed 22 of 30 passes for 197 yards. The Packers, who lost Cooper midway through the third quarter, improved to 2-2. The Buccaneers fell to 0-4 with their fourth straight loss.

2026_04_IND_WAS.headline: Taylor scores twice as Colts pull away from Commanders 30–13 in London
paragraphs: Washington lost Marcus Mariota midway through the first quarter in London, and once Indianapolis steadied itself, the Commanders could not keep up. Jonathan Taylor ran for two touchdowns and the Colts scored the final 13 points of a 30–13 win on Sunday.

The Colts started poorly. Daniel Jones fumbled on a sack moments into the game, setting up Drew Stevens' 31-yard field goal, and Washington led 6–0 after a second kick. Rasul Douglas later intercepted Jones, but the Commanders turned it over on downs. Indianapolis then scored 17 straight points: Taylor's 5-yard run late in the second quarter, Spencer Shrader's 48-yard field goal with three seconds left in the half and, after Jaylon Carlies intercepted Athan Kaliakmanis early in the third, another 5-yard Taylor run that made it 17–6.

Kaliakmanis, who replaced Mariota, hit Treylon Burks for a 47-yard touchdown to cut it to 17–13, but Washington did not score again. He completed 15 of 33 passes, and the Commanders converted two of 15 third downs and did not score a touchdown on either trip into the red zone.

Indianapolis won with little from its passing game, as Jones threw for 143 yards. Shrader made all three of his field goals, including one from 52 yards, and Jones' 4-yard touchdown run early in the fourth quarter made it 27–13. The Colts evened their record at 2-2 with their second straight win. Washington fell to 1-3.

2026_04_KC_LV.headline: Walker runs for 177 yards as Chiefs edge Raiders 30–27
paragraphs: Las Vegas outgained Kansas City and held the ball for 35:42, but it kept settling for field goals, and the Chiefs made their big plays count. Kenneth Walker III ran for 177 yards and two touchdowns as Kansas City beat the Raiders 30–27 on Sunday to stay unbeaten at 4-0.

Matt Gay made all four of his field goals, including a 48-yarder with three seconds left in the half for a 13–10 lead, and the Raiders failed to reach the end zone on either of their red-zone trips. Walker's 76-yard run late in the third quarter set up Patrick Mahomes' 8-yard touchdown pass to Tyquan Thornton at the start of the fourth, but Gay's kicks from 44 and 48 yards put Las Vegas back ahead 19–17 with 4:58 left.

Kansas City needed four plays to answer. Mahomes hit Thornton for 55 yards, and Walker scored from 2 yards out with 3:25 left for a 23–19 lead. Walker struck again on a 22-yard touchdown run with 3:10 left, making it 30–19, the last of 13 straight Kansas City points. Thornton, injured on the go-ahead drive, did not return.

Kirk Cousins threw for 365 yards and found Brock Bowers for a 20-yard touchdown with 1:54 left to cut it to 30–27. Pinned at its own 1 after a punt, Las Vegas drove 50 yards before Xavier Nwankpa intercepted Cousins with 10 seconds left. Kansas City, which did not turn the ball over, won its fourth straight. Las Vegas fell to 3-1 with the division loss.

2026_04_JAX_CIN.headline: Jaguars withstand Burrow's 428 yards, beat Bengals 22–17
paragraphs: Joe Burrow threw for 428 yards on Sunday, but Cincinnati lost Ja'Marr Chase early, could not run the ball and handed Jacksonville its only first-half touchdown. The Jaguars beat the Bengals 22–17 for their second straight win.

Chase was hurt early in the second quarter and did not return. Jacksonville led 6–3 on two Cam Little field goals, the first from 55 yards, when Jourdan Lewis intercepted Burrow with 2:00 left in the half. Four plays later, Trevor Lawrence found Brian Thomas Jr. for a 7-yard touchdown and a 13–3 halftime lead.

Burrow's 15-yard touchdown pass to Mike Gesicki midway through the third quarter pulled Cincinnati within 13–10, but Little answered from 54 yards. Foyesade Oluokun intercepted Burrow early in the fourth, and Chris Rodriguez Jr. broke a 25-yard touchdown run midway through the quarter to make it 22–10.

Burrow completed 39 of 54 passes and Tee Higgins caught 11 for 157 yards, but the Bengals ran for 23 yards on 15 carries and scored touchdowns on two of four red-zone trips. Burrow's 1-yard run with 3:33 left made it 22–17, and Cincinnati's last drive, from its own 17, moved 71 yards before ending on downs.

Jacksonville did not turn the ball over. Lawrence completed 18 of 23 passes for 227 yards, Brenton Strange caught seven for 95 and Little made all three field goals. The Jaguars moved to 3-1. The Bengals fell to 2-2 with their second straight loss.

2026_04_LAC_SEA.headline: Wilson scores twice as Seahawks hold off Chargers 30–23
paragraphs: Seattle built a 20–6 halftime lead out of a turnover-filled first half and held on through a Los Angeles rally, beating the Chargers 30–23 on Sunday. Emanuel Wilson ran for 81 yards and a touchdown and caught a scoring pass for the Seahawks.

The game opened with three turnovers in a five-minute stretch of the first quarter, and two of them produced points. Tuli Tuipulotu intercepted Sam Darnold, setting up Cameron Dicker's 40-yard field goal, and after Seattle recovered a Los Angeles fumble, Darnold hit Wilson for a 23-yard touchdown on the next play, the start of 20 unanswered Seattle points. Rashid Shaheed scored on a 28-yard run, and after Ernest Jones IV intercepted Justin Herbert late in the half, Wilson ran in from 8 yards with 47 seconds left.

Darnold's 6-yard touchdown pass to Tory Horton early in the third quarter made it 27–6. Los Angeles rallied from there. Herbert found Kimani Vidal for a 9-yard touchdown late in the third, and after a Jason Myers field goal, the Chargers scored the final 10 points: Omarion Hampton finished a 16-play, 85-yard drive midway through the fourth quarter, and Dicker kicked a 36-yard field goal with 2:17 left to make it 30–23.

Seattle finished three of 12 on third downs, but its defense closed the game. Herbert fumbled on a sack with 1:03 left, and Seattle recovered to end the last Los Angeles drive. The Chargers committed four turnovers and were sacked four times. Seattle moved to 3-1, while Los Angeles fell to 0-4 with its fourth straight loss.

2026_04_LA_PHI.headline: Kyren Williams scores twice late as Rams rally past Eagles 24–20
paragraphs: Philadelphia lost Saquon Barkley in the first quarter and, after halftime, could not move the ball at all. The Los Angeles Rams shut out the Eagles in the second half and rallied from a 20–10 deficit for a 24–20 win on Sunday, with Kyren Williams running for two touchdowns in the final 4:02.

The Eagles built their lead largely on Matthew Stafford's mistakes. Andrew Mukuba's interception early in the first quarter set up a 29-yard field goal by Jake Elliott, and Jalen Hurts' 18-yard touchdown pass to Darius Cooper made it 13–3. Puka Nacua's 2-yard touchdown run pulled the Rams within 13–10, but Cooper DeJean intercepted Stafford with 34 seconds left in the half, and Hurts found Cooper again from 10 yards out for a 20–10 halftime lead.

That was nearly all Philadelphia's offense produced. The Eagles finished with 172 yards and 3.0 yards per play, converted none of their 12 third downs and were sacked four times, 2.5 of them by Byron Young. Hurts completed 12 of 27 passes for 93 yards.

Stafford, who threw for 317 yards, led the comeback. A 98-yard drive that began at the Los Angeles 2, helped by a 32-yard catch by Nacua, ended with Williams' 1-yard run with 4:02 left. The next possession covered 79 yards, and Williams scored from 7 yards with 1:17 to go. Philadelphia's last drive lost 15 yards and ended on downs.
Williams finished with 147 yards from scrimmage as the Rams overcame two interceptions to reach 2-2. The Eagles fell to 2-2 with their second straight loss.

2026_04_MIA_MIN.headline: Reichard kicks five field goals as Vikings edge Dolphins 15–10
paragraphs: Minnesota never reached the end zone, failing to score a touchdown on any of its three red-zone trips, yet it still controlled Sunday's game. Will Reichard made all five of his field goals, and the Vikings beat the Miami Dolphins 15–10 to stay unbeaten at 4-0.

Reichard's kicks from 47, 50 and 33 yards, the last with four seconds left in the half, gave Minnesota a 9–0 halftime lead. The Vikings' defense took the ball away once in that span, when Malik Willis fumbled on a sack in the second quarter, though Minnesota punted after the recovery.

Miami found its footing on the ground in the third quarter. Ollie Gordon II broke a 53-yard run early in the quarter to set up Riley Patterson's 27-yard field goal, and after another Reichard kick, Gordon scored on a 12-yard run with 15 seconds left in the third to make it 12–10.

Minnesota answered with a 15-play, 60-yard drive that ended in Reichard's 29-yard field goal with 6:43 left, and Miami's final possession went three plays for 2 yards before a punt. The Vikings held the ball for 39:11. Kyler Murray completed 27 of 37 passes for 247 yards, and T.J. Hockenson caught all 13 of his targets for 119 yards.
Gordon ran for 100 yards on nine carries, but Willis threw for 85 and Miami finished with 198 yards. Minnesota won its fourth straight; Miami fell to 0-4, its fourth straight loss.

2026_04_NE_BUF.headline: Maye's late touchdown pass lifts Patriots past Bills 29–26
paragraphs: New England answered Buffalo's go-ahead touchdown with one of its own and then took the ball away, beating the Bills 29–26 on Sunday as a 7-point underdog. Drake Maye threw for 269 yards and three touchdowns, the last a 23-yarder to Efton Chism III with 1:55 left.

Maye opened the scoring with a 14-yard touchdown pass to Romeo Doubs at the end of a 97-yard drive, and the teams were tied 14–14 late in the first half when it turned chaotic. Khalil Shakir fumbled with 23 seconds left and New England recovered, but Dee Alford intercepted Maye moments later, and Tyler Bass kicked a 27-yard field goal with five seconds left for a 17–14 Buffalo lead at the break.

Maye's 2-yard touchdown pass to Doubs midway through the third quarter capped a 14-play drive and put New England back in front 21–17. Bass made it 21–20 early in the fourth, and Josh Allen hit Keon Coleman for a 34-yard touchdown with 4:33 left to give Buffalo a 26–21 lead.

The Patriots needed eight plays to cover 73 yards, and Chism's touchdown made it 29–26. Craig Woodson then intercepted Allen with 1:14 left to end Buffalo's last drive. New England went 3 of 3 in the red zone, ran for 143 yards and held the ball for 33:41, overcoming two turnovers and the loss of Mack Hollins in the third quarter. The division win evened the Patriots at 2-2, and the Bills fell to 3-1.

2026_04_NYJ_CHI.headline: Monangai runs for 146 yards as Bears grind past Jets 23–12
paragraphs: Chicago never punted and held the ball for 42:45, and the New York Jets stayed within reach mostly on the Bears' own mistakes. Kyle Monangai carried 30 times for 146 yards and two touchdowns in Chicago's 23–12 win on Sunday.

Monangai's 1-yard run late in the first quarter finished a 12-play drive for a 7–0 lead. Minkah Fitzpatrick then intercepted Tyson Bagent, and Jason Sanders turned it into a 36-yard field goal. Cairo Santos answered with two 30-yard field goals, the second with two seconds left in the half, for a 13–3 lead. When D'Andre Swift lost a fumble in the third quarter, Sanders kicked another field goal to make it 13–6.

Both New York scores to that point came after Chicago turnovers, and the Bears kept the Jets from building on them. Monangai's 5-yard run late in the third quarter made it 20–6, and Santos added a 21-yarder early in the fourth. Chicago ran for 232 yards, though it scored touchdowns on only two of seven red-zone trips.

New York's offense barely had the ball. The Jets ran 14 times, converted none of their seven third downs and finished with 157 yards; their only touchdown came on Geno Smith's 58-yard pass to Isaiah Williams midway through the fourth quarter. Bagent completed 25 of 34 passes for 268 yards. Chicago moved to 3-1 with its second straight win, and New York fell to 1-3, its third straight loss.

2026_04_PIT_CLE.headline: Szmyt's 56-yarder in the final seconds lifts Browns over Steelers 27–24
paragraphs: Pittsburgh erased a 21–10 halftime deficit and tied the game in the final two minutes, but Cleveland had one more answer. Andre Szmyt made a 56-yard field goal with 15 seconds left, and the Browns beat the Steelers 27–24 on Thursday night for their third straight win.

Aaron Rodgers opened the scoring with a 12-yard touchdown pass to Roman Wilson at the end of a 17-play drive, but Denzel Ward intercepted him early in the second quarter, and Cleveland scored 21 straight points. Jaleel McLaughlin ran 28 yards for a touchdown after the interception, Quinshon Judkins scored from 2 yards and Deshaun Watson threw a 2-yard touchdown pass to Harold Fannin Jr.

Neither team scored in the third quarter, in which Watson lost a fumble. Robert Spears-Jennings intercepted Watson early in the fourth, and Rodgers hit Darnell Washington for a 21-yard touchdown on the next possession. Szmyt's 44-yard kick made it 24–16, but Rodgers found DK Metcalf for gains of 22 and 28 yards on an 80-yard drive, and his 3-yard touchdown pass to Pat Freiermuth with 1:46 left tied it 24–24.

Cleveland moved 36 yards in seven plays to set up Szmyt, and Grant Delpit intercepted Rodgers with 10 seconds left to end it. Rodgers threw for 299 yards and three touchdowns but was intercepted twice and sacked five times. Watson completed 24 of 33 passes for 268 yards. The division win lifted Cleveland to 3-1, and Pittsburgh fell to 2-2.

2026_05_BAL_ATL.headline: Huntley scores in overtime as Ravens rally past Falcons 30–23
paragraphs: Baltimore trailed from midway through the first quarter until 44 seconds were left in regulation, then won it in overtime. Tyler Huntley ran 1 yard for the deciding touchdown, and the Ravens beat the Atlanta Falcons 30–23 on Sunday night as 3-point underdogs.

The deficit began with a Baltimore mistake. Mark Andrews fumbled after a catch, and Jessie Bates III returned it for a touchdown and a 7–3 Atlanta lead. Michael Penix Jr.'s 5-yard touchdown pass to Kyle Pitts Sr. late in the second quarter kept the Falcons ahead 14–9 at halftime, despite two 51-yard field goals from Tyler Loop.

Atlanta kept settling for kicks, scoring a touchdown on one of its three red-zone trips. Justice Hill's 47-yard run set up Huntley's 18-yard touchdown pass to Derrick Henry midway through the third quarter, but Nick Folk made all three of his field goals, the last from 48 yards with 2:35 left for a 23–15 lead.

Huntley then drove the Ravens 71 yards in six plays and threw a 7-yard touchdown pass to Devontez Walker, and Baltimore tied it 23–23. The Ravens took the opening possession of overtime 68 yards in 14 plays, and Kyle Hamilton intercepted Tua Tagovailoa on Atlanta's answering drive.

Henry ran for 102 yards as Baltimore piled up 208 on the ground and held the ball for 35:10, and Huntley completed 24 of 32 passes for 201 yards. The Ravens moved to 4-1 with their third straight win. The Falcons fell to 2-3.

2026_04_TEN_BAL.headline: Ravens lose Lamar Jackson, hold off Titans 24–18
paragraphs: Baltimore built a 24–7 halftime lead before Lamar Jackson was hurt in the final seconds of the first half, then held on without him. The Ravens did not score after the break but beat the Tennessee Titans 24–18 on Sunday for their second straight win.

Both Tennessee turnovers fed that lead. Trenton Simpson intercepted Cam Ward early in the first quarter, and Derrick Henry's 5-yard run made it 7–0. After Tony Pollard tied it, Jackson threw touchdown passes of 19 yards to Zay Flowers and 3 yards to Mark Andrews, the second ending a 98-yard drive. Carnell Tate then fumbled after a 33-yard catch with 46 seconds left in the half, and Tyler Loop made a 64-yard field goal with five seconds left. Jackson was injured with 12 seconds left on that drive and did not return.

Jackson finished 15 of 20 for 222 yards. Tyler Huntley completed eight of nine passes for 63 yards in relief, but Baltimore's second-half possessions produced no points, and its last one, an 11-play drive, ended with a missed field goal.

Tennessee crept back with a 33-yard field goal by Joey Slye in the third quarter and Ward's 3-yard touchdown pass to Wan'Dale Robinson with 1:16 left, which made it 24–18. Tate caught nine passes for 145 yards. Baltimore, which did not turn the ball over and scored touchdowns on all three of its red-zone trips, moved to 3-1. Tennessee fell to 0-4 with its fourth straight loss.

2026_05_BUF_LA.headline: Bass kicks Bills past Rams 37–34 in overtime after Mevis misses
paragraphs: Buffalo fumbled away a chance to win in overtime, and the Los Angeles Rams could not make it count. After the Rams missed a field goal on their next possession, Tyler Bass made a 45-yarder with 2:00 left in the extra period, and the Bills won 37–34 on Monday night as 3.5-point underdogs.

Buffalo led 13–7 at halftime, and the lead changed hands six times. The Rams had an answer for nearly every Buffalo score: Josh Allen's 1-yard touchdown run made it 27–20, and Matthew Stafford's 5-yard touchdown pass to Davante Adams tied it. James Cook III's 5-yard run with 1:44 left put Buffalo up 34–27, and Kyren Williams scored from 1 yard with eight seconds left to force overtime.

Khalil Shakir's 57-yard catch moved Buffalo into position early in overtime, but Cook lost a fumble on the drive. The Rams then moved 50 yards before the drive ended with a missed field goal, one of two misses for Harrison Mevis. Allen's 19-yard run helped set up Bass' winning kick.

Buffalo won on the ground. Allen ran for 121 yards on 10 carries, Cook ran for 111 and two touchdowns, and the Bills averaged 7.6 yards per play while Allen threw only 19 passes. Stafford completed 40 of 54 for 383 yards and three touchdowns, Puka Nacua caught 17 passes for 138 yards, and the Rams scored touchdowns on all five red-zone trips without a turnover. Buffalo moved to 4-1; Los Angeles fell to 2-3.

2026_05_CHI_GB.headline: Watson scores twice, McKinney picks off two as Packers rout Bears 31–7
paragraphs: Chicago turned the ball over five times, and Green Bay converted both of Xavier McKinney's interceptions into touchdowns on the way to a 31–7 rout of the Bears on Sunday.

Jordan Love's 42-yard touchdown pass to Christian Watson finished a 91-yard drive that began at the Green Bay 9. McKinney intercepted Tyson Bagent on the next Chicago possession, and MarShawn Lloyd's 7-yard run to open the second quarter made it 14–0. D'Andre Swift's 1-yard run at the end of a 16-play drive cut the lead to 14–7 at halftime.

Green Bay put it away in the third quarter. Love found Watson for a 53-yard touchdown early in the quarter, and Trey Smack added a 35-yard field goal. McKinney then picked off Bagent again late in the third, and Lloyd's 4-yard run on the first play of the fourth made it 31–7.

The Packers could have added more. Ty'Ron Hopper intercepted Case Keenum in the end zone and Rome Odunze lost a fumble, but Smack missed field goals after both. Love completed 25 of 31 passes for 367 yards, Watson finished with 143 receiving yards and Matthew Golden added 123. Chicago managed 246 yards and 3.6 per play and was sacked four times. Green Bay moved to 3-2 with its second straight win, and Chicago fell to 3-2.

2026_05_CIN_MIA.headline: Burrow throws four touchdown passes as Bengals hold off Dolphins 31–24
paragraphs: Miami ran for 217 yards on Sunday, but the Dolphins could not keep the ball out of Cincinnati's hands. Jordan Battle intercepted Malik Willis twice, Joe Burrow threw four touchdown passes, and the Bengals won 31–24, sending Miami to its fifth straight loss.

Burrow's 4-yard touchdown pass to Mike Gesicki early in the first quarter and a 6-yard throw to Samaje Perine early in the second gave Cincinnati a 14–7 lead. Three turnovers followed in a five-minute stretch. Battle intercepted Willis, Chase Brown gave the ball back on a fumble, and Battle picked off Willis again. That one counted: Burrow found Tanner Hudson for a 2-yard touchdown with 1:00 left in the half, making it 21–7.

After a Miami field goal, Burrow's 45-yard touchdown pass to Ja'Marr Chase with 47 seconds left in the third quarter made it 28–10. The Dolphins answered with a 14-play, 80-yard drive capped by Willis' 3-yard touchdown pass to Kevin Coleman Jr., cutting it to 28–18 midway through the fourth. But Willis fumbled on a sack with 2:34 left, and Evan McPherson's 26-yard field goal made it 31–18 before Willis ran in from 1 yard with 48 seconds left.

Burrow completed 23 of 32 passes for 190 yards and was not sacked, and Cincinnati converted nine of 13 third downs. Willis ran for 74 yards and Ollie Gordon II for 88, but Miami turned the ball over three times. The Bengals improved to 3-2; the Dolphins fell to 0-5.

2026_05_CLE_NYJ.headline: Braelon Allen's late touchdown lifts Jets past Browns 17–12
paragraphs: Cleveland finally took the lead midway through the fourth quarter, then lost it amid a string of fumbles. Braelon Allen's 22-yard touchdown run with 3:07 left lifted the New York Jets to a 17–12 win on Sunday.

Points were scarce. Geno Smith's 32-yard touchdown pass to Garrett Wilson in the first quarter and two Andre Szmyt field goals left the Jets ahead 7–6 at halftime, and neither team scored in the third. Jason Sanders made a 54-yard field goal early in the fourth, and Deshaun Watson answered with an 86-yard drive, finishing it with a 29-yard touchdown pass to Denzel Boston for a 12–10 Cleveland lead.

Then the ball started coming loose. Smith fumbled on a sack with 4:20 left and Cleveland recovered, but on the Browns' next possession Corey Bojorquez fumbled, and the Jets recovered at the Cleveland 23. Allen scored three plays later. Watson fumbled on a sack with 57 seconds left, ending Cleveland's last drive.

The Jets' pass rush shaped the game. Cleveland was sacked eight times, three of them by David Bailey, and finished with 198 yards, 3.0 per play and four conversions on 16 third downs. Watson completed 15 of 33 passes for 155 yards. Allen ran for 116 yards on 24 carries and Wilson caught seven passes for 104. New York improved to 2-3, and Cleveland fell to 3-2.

2026_05_DEN_LAC.headline: Broncos turn late Chargers turnovers into 23–17 win
paragraphs: Denver converted one of 12 third downs and gained 224 yards, and it still won because Los Angeles kept giving it the ball. The Broncos scored the final 13 points, two field goals coming after Justin Herbert turnovers, to beat the Chargers 23–17 on Sunday.

A fumble by Charlie Kolar in the first quarter set up J.K. Dobbins' 2-yard touchdown run, and Wil Lutz's 34-yard field goal made it 10–3 at halftime. Herbert tied it with a 7-yard touchdown pass to Hayden Rucci midway through the third quarter. Then Bo Nix fumbled late in the quarter, and Kimani Vidal ran 42 yards for a touchdown on the next play to put Los Angeles ahead 17–10.

Nix's 5-yard touchdown pass to Courtland Sutton midway through the fourth tied it. Herbert then fumbled on a sack, and Lutz's 19-yard field goal with 5:10 left put Denver in front 20–17. Brandon Jones intercepted Herbert with 3:26 left, and Lutz added a 36-yarder with 1:12 to go.

Denver's defense did the rest. It sacked the Chargers five times, two by Nik Bonitto, forced three turnovers and held Los Angeles to 82 passing yards; Herbert completed 14 of 24 passes for 121. The division win moved Denver to 3-2. Los Angeles fell to 0-5 with its fifth straight loss.

2026_05_DET_ARI.headline: Gibbs runs for 151 yards as Lions pull away from Cardinals 45–21
paragraphs: Arizona opened the scoring with a 14-play touchdown drive, and Detroit answered with the next 31 points. The Lions beat the Cardinals 45–21 on Sunday, with Jahmyr Gibbs running for 151 yards and two touchdowns.

The second quarter decided it. Gibbs tied the game with a 1-yard run, Jared Goff threw touchdown passes of 38 yards to Sam LaPorta and 8 yards to Jameson Williams, and Jake Bates' 46-yard field goal made it 24–7. Keith Abney II then intercepted Jacoby Brissett with three seconds left in the half, and Detroit's next possession ended with Goff's 39-yard touchdown pass to Williams for a 31–7 lead.

Brissett's second touchdown pass to Teagan Quitoriano, from 13 yards, cut it to 31–14 in the third quarter, but Detroit answered each time. Goff ran in from 1 yard late in the third, and Gibbs finished a 13-play, 79-yard drive with a 3-yard run midway through the fourth to make it 45–14.

Detroit scored touchdowns on all four of its red-zone trips and did not turn the ball over. Goff completed 19 of 30 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns, and Gibbs added five catches for 56 yards, giving him 207 yards from scrimmage. Brissett threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns, the last to Trey McBride late in the game, but Arizona ran for 56 yards and was sacked five times, twice by DJ Wonnum. The Lions improved to 3-2, and the Cardinals fell to 1-4 with their fourth straight loss.

2026_05_HOU_TEN.headline: Anderson's three sacks lead Texans past Titans 26–3
paragraphs: Tennessee kicked a field goal on its opening drive and never scored again. The Houston Texans scored the final 26 points, and Will Anderson Jr. sacked Cam Ward three times, in a 26–3 win over the Titans on Sunday.

Ka'imi Fairbairn made all four of his field goals in the first half, from 45, 35, 26 and 53 yards, and two of them followed Tennessee turnovers. Tyjae Spears fumbled late in the first quarter, and Jake Hansen intercepted Ward early in the second. Houston led 12–3 at halftime.

The Texans finished drives after the break. C.J. Stroud capped a 17-play, 74-yard march with a 2-yard touchdown run midway through the third quarter, and his 9-yard touchdown pass to Jaylin Noel early in the fourth made it 26–3. Stroud completed 26 of 34 passes for 261 yards, and Houston held the ball for 34:39 without a turnover.

Tennessee managed 187 yards and 3.2 yards per play and was sacked four times. Ward completed 23 of 36 passes for 170 yards, and the Titans' last drive took 14 plays to cover 27 yards before ending on downs. The division win moved Houston to 1-4, and Tennessee fell to 0-5 with its fifth straight loss.

2026_05_IND_PIT.headline: Jaylen Warren's two long scores lift Steelers past Colts 34–22
paragraphs: Indianapolis kept kicking field goals, and Pittsburgh kept answering with touchdowns. Spencer Shrader made all five of his attempts, but the Steelers beat the Colts 34–22 on Sunday behind 188 yards from scrimmage by Jaylen Warren.

Shrader's 57-yard field goal midway through the first quarter put Indianapolis ahead, and on the next play Aaron Rodgers hit Warren for an 80-yard touchdown. Rodgers added a 1-yard touchdown pass to Pat Freiermuth, Tyler Warren answered with a 1-yard run for the Colts, and Chris Boswell's 48-yard field goal with 25 seconds left sent Pittsburgh to halftime ahead 17–13.

Jaylen Warren broke a 50-yard touchdown run midway through the third quarter for a 24–16 lead. Shrader kept the Colts close with kicks of 40 and 28 yards, the second making it 24–22 early in the fourth, but Indianapolis scored a touchdown on only one of its three red-zone trips.

Pittsburgh answered with a 10-play, 64-yard drive that ended in Rodgers' 17-yard touchdown pass to Freiermuth with 6:40 left, and Boswell added a 54-yard field goal. The Colts' final drive ended on downs. Rodgers completed 22 of 31 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns, while Daniel Jones threw for 267 yards without a touchdown. Neither team turned the ball over. Pittsburgh moved to 3-2, and Indianapolis fell to 2-3.

2026_05_LV_NE.headline: Maye throws four touchdown passes as Patriots rout Raiders 45–17
paragraphs: The Las Vegas Raiders matched New England's opening touchdown and then spent the rest of Sunday chasing. Drake Maye completed 26 of 34 passes for 374 yards, threw four touchdowns and ran for another as the Patriots beat the Raiders 45–17.

Brock Bowers' 13-yard touchdown catch from Kirk Cousins tied it 7–7 in the first quarter. New England answered with 21 unanswered points, scoring on Rhamondre Stevenson's 5-yard run, an 11-yard pass to Hunter Henry with 28 seconds left in the half and Maye's 34-yard strike to Kyle Williams early in the third quarter for a 28–7 lead. The Raiders' best chance to close the gap came when Corey Kiner fumbled late in the second quarter, but Las Vegas missed a field goal on the possession that followed.

The Patriots averaged 8.1 yards per play, gained 536 yards and scored on four of five trips into the red zone. Williams caught three passes for 91 yards, and DeMario Douglas scored twice, on catches of 35 and 8 yards. Elijah Ponder had two of the three sacks of Las Vegas quarterbacks, and when Bowers fumbled late in the third quarter, New England turned it into an Andy Borregales field goal.

Bowers finished with eight catches for 110 yards, and Dylan Laube's 2-yard run gave Las Vegas a fourth-quarter touchdown, but the Raiders ran for only 38 yards and their last drive ended on downs. New England improved to 3-2 with a second straight win. Las Vegas, also 3-2, has lost two straight.

2026_05_MIN_NO.headline: Murphy intercepts two as Vikings beat Saints 23–13, move to 5-0
paragraphs: Minnesota gave New Orleans both of its touchdowns on fumbles, and its defense made sure that was all the Saints got. Byron Murphy Jr. intercepted Tyler Shough twice as the Vikings won 23–13 on Sunday to stay unbeaten.

The Vikings lost tight end T.J. Hockenson to an injury on their opening drive, and an Aaron Jones Sr. fumble late in the first quarter set up Kendre Miller's 2-yard touchdown run. Will Reichard's 54-yard field goal with three seconds left in the half cut the New Orleans lead to 7–6. Minnesota went ahead 13–7 in the third quarter, only for Jonas Sanker to return a Myles Price fumble for a touchdown late in the period that pulled New Orleans even.

Jones made up for his fumble early in the fourth quarter with an 8-yard touchdown run, and Reichard's 55-yarder midway through the quarter made it 23–13. Jones carried 25 times for 113 yards, and Kyler Murray completed 24 of 30 passes for 229 yards and a touchdown while adding 51 yards rushing.

The New Orleans offense never found a rhythm. The Saints gained 142 yards, averaged 3.3 yards per play, converted two of 10 third downs and held the ball for 20:23 to Minnesota's 39:37. Shough completed 16 of 25 passes for 96 yards, and Murphy's second interception ended the last New Orleans possession late in the fourth quarter.
Minnesota improved to 5-0 with its fifth straight win. New Orleans fell to 1-4 and has lost three straight.

2026_05_PHI_JAX.headline: Little's 57-yard field goal lifts Jaguars past Eagles 19–17
paragraphs: Jacksonville trailed by a point with eight seconds left in London and still found a way to win. Cam Little made a 57-yard field goal with one second remaining, and the Jaguars beat the Philadelphia Eagles 19–17 on Sunday.

Trevor Lawrence's 51-yard touchdown pass to Parker Washington midway through the first quarter put Jacksonville ahead, but Philadelphia answered with two second-quarter touchdowns, Will Shipley's 2-yard run and Jalen Hurts' 62-yard strike to Darius Cooper, to lead 14–7 at halftime. Little's 34-yard field goal was the only score of the third quarter, and a Quinyon Mitchell interception of Lawrence late in the period kept Jacksonville from going further.

The finish turned on three scores in the final 3:26. Lawrence found Washington again from 27 yards out to give the Jaguars a 16–14 lead, and Jake Elliott answered with a 48-yard field goal with 12 seconds left. Jacksonville then took over at the Philadelphia 39 with eight seconds to go, and Little won it on the next play.

Washington caught six passes for 124 yards and two touchdowns, and Lawrence threw for 331 yards. Jacksonville outgained Philadelphia 408 to 232 despite failing to score a touchdown on any of its three red zone trips. The Eagles averaged 3.9 yards per play, ran for 22 yards and punted six times, while Hurts completed 21 of 40 passes for 220 yards. Jalen Carter had two sacks.
The Jaguars improved to 4-1 with their third straight win. The Eagles fell to 2-3 and have lost three straight.

2026_05_SF_SEA.headline: Pineiro's late field goal sends 49ers past Seahawks 32–29
paragraphs: San Francisco turned Seattle's mistakes into a halftime lead, gave most of it back in a turnover-filled third quarter and still came away with its fifth straight win. Eddy Pineiro's 44-yard field goal with 2:00 left beat the Seahawks 32–29 on Sunday, a result that went against Seattle's standing as a 3-point favorite.

Renardo Green intercepted Sam Darnold early in the first quarter, setting up Brock Purdy's 2-yard touchdown pass to Mike Evans. Seattle turned the ball over three more times around halftime, and San Francisco scored after two of them: Christian McCaffrey ran 11 yards for a touchdown one play after an Emanuel Wilson fumble, and Gracen Halton returned a George Holani fumble for a touchdown with 18 seconds left in the half for a 21–13 lead.

The 49ers then handed the ball back. A Nehemiah Pritchett interception of Purdy set up Darnold's 16-yard touchdown pass to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and a Deebo Samuel Sr. fumble led to a field goal as Seattle scored 13 unanswered points to lead 26–21. Samuel was hurt in the third quarter and did not return. Purdy's 7-yard touchdown pass to Brandin Cooks put San Francisco back in front early in the fourth quarter, and Jason Myers, who made all five of his field goals, tied it at 29 before Pineiro's kick.
The 49ers sacked Darnold five times and forced four turnovers. Seattle's final drive started at its 15 and ended on downs. San Francisco moved to 5-0 with the division win, and Seattle fell to 3-2.

2026_05_TB_DAL.headline: Irving runs for 165 yards as Buccaneers upset Cowboys 24–16
paragraphs: Tampa Bay came out of halftime trailing and turned the game with two quick strikes. Bucky Irving ran for 165 yards, and the Buccaneers scored 17 unanswered points after the break to beat the Dallas Cowboys 24–16 on Thursday night as an 8.5-point underdog.

Dallas led 10–7 at halftime after Javonte Williams' 1-yard touchdown run and Brandon Aubrey's 41-yard field goal with 26 seconds left in the half. Tampa Bay needed only two plays to retake the lead: Irving broke a 72-yard run moments into the third quarter, and Emeka Egbuka finished the drive with a 14-yard touchdown run. Yaya Diaby then intercepted Dak Prescott, Jalon Daniels hit Tez Johnson for 64 yards, and Irving scored from a yard out midway through the quarter to make it 21–10. Chase McLaughlin added a field goal before the period ended.

Irving's 21 carries anchored an offense that ran for 241 yards, held the ball for 39:21 and did not turn it over. Daniels completed 19 of 25 passes for 189 yards and a touchdown, a 5-yard throw to Irving that tied the game at the start of the second quarter. Dallas ran only 13 times.

Prescott threw for 316 yards and George Pickens caught nine passes for 130 yards, including an 18-yard touchdown midway through the fourth quarter that capped a 99-yard drive and cut the deficit to 24–16. But Alex Anzalone intercepted Prescott in the final two minutes to end the last Dallas threat. Tampa Bay improved to 1-4, and Dallas fell to 2-3.

2026_06_ARI_LA.headline: Ryland kicks six field goals as Cardinals stun Rams 18–16
paragraphs: Arizona never reached the end zone, and it did not need to. Chad Ryland made all six of his field-goal attempts, the last a 43-yarder with three seconds left, and the Cardinals beat the Los Angeles Rams 18–16 on Sunday as a 13.5-point underdog.

In the division game, Blake Grupe's 44-yard field goal followed a Quentin Lake interception of Jacoby Brissett in the first quarter, and Grupe was hurt moments later and did not return. Matthew Stafford's 15-yard touchdown pass to Blake Corum put Los Angeles back in front 9–6, but Ryland answered with a 22-yard kick in the final minute, and the teams went to halftime tied 9–9.

Ryland's 38- and 27-yard field goals, the second capping a 14-play drive, put Arizona ahead 15–9, and a Tyler Higbee fumble midway through the fourth quarter gave the Cardinals the ball back. The Rams still went in front when Stafford drove them 86 yards, helped by a 43-yard catch by Puka Nacua, and hit Colby Parkinson for a 6-yard touchdown with 52 seconds left. Brissett then moved Arizona 40 yards in five plays, with a 21-yard throw to Jalen Brooks, to set up the winner.

The Cardinals reached the red zone five times without a touchdown, but they held the ball for 34:52 and sacked Stafford three times. Stafford threw for 222 yards and two touchdowns, and Los Angeles also lost Davante Adams to an injury in the final two minutes. Both teams are 2-4, and the Rams have lost two straight.

2026_06_BAL_CLE.headline: Browns rally from 10 down, beat Ravens 13–10 on last-play field goal
paragraphs: Baltimore scored 10 points in the first quarter and none after it, and Cleveland slowly took the game back. Andre Szmyt kicked a 37-yard field goal as time expired, and the Browns beat the Ravens 13–10 on Sunday after trailing 10–0.

Tyler Huntley's 2-yard touchdown pass to Josh Cuevas and a 34-yard Tyler Loop field goal gave the Ravens their lead in the first quarter. Neither team scored again until Szmyt's 48-yarder midway through the third quarter. It was a game for defenses: the teams combined for 14 punts, and Cleveland was sacked five times and Baltimore three.

The turning point came early in the fourth quarter, when Derrick Henry fumbled and Cleveland recovered. The Browns started at the Baltimore 35 and tied it 10–10 on Audric Estime's 2-yard run midway through the quarter. Baltimore's last possession gained three yards and ended in a punt, and Cleveland took over at its 20 with 1:59 left. Deshaun Watson moved the Browns 62 yards in 10 plays, the biggest a 33-yard completion to Jerry Jeudy with 42 seconds to go, and Szmyt finished it.

Watson completed 16 of 26 passes for 164 yards, and Jeudy caught all four of his targets for 69 yards. Huntley threw for 165 yards, and Henry ran 17 times for 58. The division win lifted Cleveland to 4-2, the same record as Baltimore, which had been a 3-point favorite.

2026_06_BUF_LV.headline: Cook's late touchdown run lifts Bills past Raiders 33–30
paragraphs: Las Vegas came back from 10 points down to tie it in the fourth quarter, and Buffalo answered with the two scores it needed. James Cook III ran 3 yards for the go-ahead touchdown with 4:49 left, and the Bills held off the Raiders 33–30 on Sunday.

The teams were tied 13–13 at halftime after Matt Gay's 27-yard field goal with four seconds left in the half. Buffalo moved in front with a Tyler Bass field goal, and Dorian Williams' interception of Kirk Cousins midway through the third quarter gave the Bills a short field; Josh Allen threw 12 yards to Keon Coleman six plays later for a 23–13 lead.

Las Vegas answered with a 15-play field-goal drive and a 91-yard march capped by Cousins' 11-yard touchdown pass to Tre Tucker, tying it at 23 midway through the fourth quarter. Cook, who finished with 95 rushing yards and 58 more on three catches, set up his own touchdown with a 26-yard reception, and Bass added a 38-yarder at the two-minute mark. Tucker's 44-yard touchdown catch with 1:39 left was the Raiders' last score.

Allen threw for 255 yards and two touchdowns, and Bass made all four of his field goals. Buffalo did not turn the ball over, though the Raiders outgained it 378 to 345. Cousins threw for 313 yards, and Tucker caught five passes for 97 yards and both Las Vegas touchdowns through the air. The Bills improved to 5-1 with their second straight win, and the Raiders fell to 3-3 with a third straight loss.

2026_06_CAR_PHI.headline: Hubbard runs for 120 yards as Panthers beat Eagles 25–14
paragraphs: Carolina wore Philadelphia down on the ground and pulled away in the fourth quarter. Chuba Hubbard carried 28 times for 120 yards and a touchdown, and the Panthers beat the Eagles 25–14 on Sunday, handing Philadelphia its fourth straight loss.

The Panthers led 10–7 at halftime after Bryce Young's 12-yard touchdown pass to Tommy Tremble and a Dameon Pierce touchdown run for the Eagles. Ryan Fitzgerald's 52-yard field goal stretched the lead early in the third quarter, and Carolina's biggest drive began at its own 8: 14 plays and 92 yards, ending with Hubbard's 1-yard run early in the fourth quarter for a 19–7 lead.

Tanner McKee pulled Philadelphia within 19–14 on a 19-yard touchdown pass to DeVonta Smith, but Carolina needed only four plays to answer. Young found Tremble again from 19 yards out midway through the quarter, and the Eagles' last drive ended on downs.

Young threw for 281 yards and two touchdowns, both to Tremble, and Jalen Coker caught six passes for 97 yards. Neither team turned the ball over, so the gap came from the line of scrimmage: Carolina held the ball for 34:48, while Philadelphia averaged 3.6 yards per play, ran 13 times for 35 yards and punted eight times. McKee completed 26 of 45 passes for 215 yards. The Eagles also lost Nolan Smith Jr. to an injury early in the second quarter.
Carolina moved to 3-2 with its second straight win. Philadelphia fell to 2-4.

2026_06_CHI_ATL.headline: Gordon's three sacks help Bears hold off Falcons 31–23
paragraphs: Chicago built a 31–7 lead and then needed its pass rush to finish the job. Kyler Gordon had three sacks, and the Bears beat the Falcons 31–23 on Sunday after Atlanta scored 16 unanswered points in the fourth quarter.

Caleb Williams opened the scoring with a 14-yard touchdown pass to Colston Loveland, and D'Andre Swift ran for two touchdowns as Chicago led 21–7 at halftime. Williams completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards. Roschon Johnson's 4-yard run late in the third quarter and a Cairo Santos field goal made it 31–7.

Atlanta then found its offense. Michael Penix Jr. threw touchdown passes of 10 and 5 yards to Kyle Pitts Sr., the second coming after Johnson fumbled midway through the fourth quarter, and the Falcons were within 31–23 with 5:46 left. Chicago's next drive lost a yard and ended in a punt, but Penix fumbled on a sack late in the quarter and the Bears recovered to close it out.

Atlanta was sacked five times and converted three of 12 third downs, and it ran only 12 times while Chicago held the ball for 40:08. Penix threw for 225 yards and three touchdowns. Luther Burden III caught all eight of his targets for 95 yards for Chicago. The Bears improved to 4-2, and the Falcons fell to 2-4 with their second straight loss.

2026_06_DAL_GB.headline: Packers take 17–0 halftime lead, hold off Cowboys 23–13
paragraphs: Green Bay turned two Dak Prescott interceptions into 10 first-half points and spent the second half protecting the lead. The Packers beat the Dallas Cowboys 23–13 on Sunday night for their third straight win.

Jordan Love opened the scoring with a 9-yard touchdown pass to Matthew Golden at the end of a 14-play, 90-yard drive. Love gave the ball back on a Dee Winters interception late in the first quarter, but Dallas returned the favor on its next possession when Evan Williams picked off Prescott. Green Bay followed with a 15-play drive that ended in a Trey Smack field goal, and after Brandon Cisse intercepted Prescott at the two-minute mark, Love ran 1 yard for a touchdown with 25 seconds left in the half for a 17–0 lead.

Dallas lost KaVontae Turpin to an injury on its opening drive and Winters early in the second quarter; neither returned. Javonte Williams scored on a 1-yard run in the third quarter, but Smack answered with field goals of 44 and 29 yards to make it 23–7. Green Bay converted 11 of 18 third downs, which kept its offense on the field even as it averaged 4.5 yards per play. Golden finished with six catches for 104 yards.

Prescott completed 34 of 54 passes for 258 yards, and his 6-yard touchdown pass to Ryan Flournoy came with 52 seconds left. The Cowboys ran 15 times for 48 yards. Green Bay moved to 4-2, and Dallas fell to 2-4 with its second straight loss.

2026_06_HOU_JAX.headline: Fairbairn's late field goal lifts Texans past Jaguars 34–31 in London
paragraphs: C.J. Stroud's interception in the end zone gave Jacksonville a way back in London, and Houston still had enough time to recover. Ka'imi Fairbairn made a 49-yard field goal with three seconds left, and the Texans beat the Jaguars 34–31 on Sunday.

The division game was a shootout from the second quarter on. Stroud and Trevor Lawrence traded touchdown passes, and Stroud's 1-yard throw to Foster Moreau with 12 seconds left in the half, set up by a 50-yard catch by Jaylin Noel, gave Houston a 17–14 lead. Noel's 13-yard touchdown catch extended it, and after Lawrence answered with a 1-yard pass to Nate Boerkircher, Jawhar Jordan's 25-yard run late in the third quarter made it 31–21.

Jacksonville pulled within 31–28 on Lawrence's 7-yard pass to Travis Hunter early in the fourth quarter. Hunter then intercepted Stroud in the end zone with 3:59 left, and Cam Little tied it with a 60-yard field goal at the two-minute mark. Stroud moved the Texans 36 yards in seven plays from their 32 to set up the winner.

Stroud completed 24 of 34 passes for 312 yards and three touchdowns, and Noel caught all four of his targets for 107 yards. Lawrence threw for 306 yards and four touchdowns, two of them to Bhayshul Tuten, and neither quarterback was sacked. Houston averaged 7.2 yards per play. The Texans improved to 2-4 with their second straight win, and the Jaguars fell to 4-2.

2026_06_LAC_KC.headline: Walker runs for two touchdowns as Chiefs beat Chargers 22–6
paragraphs: Kansas City scored both of its touchdowns in the first half and let its defense handle the rest. Kenneth Walker III ran for 128 yards and two scores, and the Chiefs beat the Los Angeles Chargers 22–6 on Sunday to stay unbeaten.

Walker's 33-yard touchdown run midway through the first quarter followed a Harrison Butker field goal, and his 2-yard run late in the second quarter finished an 80-yard drive. Butker's 50-yarder with seven seconds left in the half made it 19–3. The Chiefs could have led by more: Jack Cochrane intercepted Justin Herbert in the second quarter, but Cam Hart gave the ball right back by picking off Patrick Mahomes in the end zone.

The second half produced only a Cameron Dicker field goal until Kansas City recovered a KeAndre Lambert-Smith fumble midway through the fourth quarter and used 11 plays to set up Butker's 30-yarder with 3:56 left. Herbert completed 22 of 37 passes for 204 yards without a touchdown, and the Chargers were sacked four times and went without a touchdown on three red zone trips. Their last drive covered 62 yards and ended on downs.

Mahomes completed 23 of 30 passes for 272 yards, and Kansas City averaged 7.4 yards per play. The division win lifted the Chiefs to 5-0, their fifth straight victory. The Chargers fell to 0-6 and have lost six straight.

2026_06_NO_NYG.headline: Saints score 34 straight points, hold off Giants 34–27
paragraphs: New Orleans fell behind 10–0, then scored the next 34 points, many of them off New York mistakes, and held on through a late Giants rally to win 34–27 on Sunday.

Jameis Winston's 17-yard touchdown pass to Tyrone Tracy Jr. and a Dominic Zvada field goal put the Giants up 10–0 late in the first half. Daniel Carlson answered from 58 yards, and when the Saints recovered a New York fumble moments later, Tyler Shough turned it into a touchdown pass to Bryce Lance that tied it 10–10 at halftime.

Shough's 31-yard touchdown pass to Alvin Kamara early in the third quarter and his 1-yard run put New Orleans ahead to stay. Then Winston threw two interceptions, and both led to points. Martin Emerson Jr.'s first set up a 51-yard Carlson field goal, and Julian Blackmon's pick early in the fourth quarter led to Shough's 18-yard touchdown pass to Chris Olave for a 34–10 lead. Emerson also intercepted J.J. McCarthy, but CJ Donaldson fumbled the ball right back.

With McCarthy at quarterback, New York scored the last 17 points. Tracy ran 5 yards for a touchdown after the Donaldson fumble, McCarthy found Isaiah Likely for 24 yards, and Zvada kicked a 41-yarder with 2:08 left, but the Giants' last drive ended on downs. Malik Nabers caught 12 passes for 165 yards.
Shough threw three touchdown passes, and the Saints ran for 175 yards and sacked New York five times without allowing a sack. New Orleans improved to 2-4, and the Giants fell to 3-2-1.

2026_06_NYJ_NE.headline: Maye throws three touchdowns as Patriots hold off Jets 26–19
paragraphs: New England built its lead in the first half and protected it with a long drive at the end. Drake Maye threw three touchdown passes, and the Patriots beat the New York Jets 26–19 on Sunday for their third straight win.

Maye's 42-yard touchdown pass to Romeo Doubs came on a two-play drive after the Jets opened with a Jason Sanders field goal. Andy Borregales added a field goal, and Maye hit DeMario Douglas from 9 yards out with 20 seconds left in the half for a 17–3 lead.

The Jets closed in after halftime with help from New England fumbles. Geno Smith's 48-yard touchdown pass to Omar Cooper Jr. and a Sanders field goal after a TreVeyon Henderson fumble made it 17–13. Maye's 7-yard touchdown pass to Hunter Henry early in the fourth quarter made it 23–13, and Charles Woods intercepted Smith soon after, but Douglas fumbled at the end of a 39-yard catch and Sanders kicked another field goal.

Leading 23–16, New England took over at its 40 with 7:20 left and ran 13 plays before Borregales' 27-yard field goal with 1:14 to go. Sanders, four for four on field goals, hit from 36 yards with 36 seconds left. The Jets reached the red zone three times without a touchdown.

Maye completed 18 of 32 passes for 235 yards, Doubs did not return after a first-quarter injury, and Cooper caught six passes for 103 yards for the Jets. The Patriots moved to 4-2 with the division win, and the Jets fell to 2-4.

2026_06_PIT_TB.headline: Steelers rally from 13 down, beat Buccaneers 26–19 in overtime
paragraphs: Pittsburgh's offense spent three quarters stuck on a field goal, and then its defense started taking the ball away. Aaron Rodgers threw a 6-yard touchdown pass to Germie Bernard in overtime, and Pittsburgh beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 26–19 on Sunday.

Tampa Bay led 13–0 in the second quarter on Jalon Daniels' 2-yard touchdown pass to Emeka Egbuka and two Chase McLaughlin field goals, the first set up by an A'Shawn Robinson interception of Rodgers. McLaughlin's third kick, after a 17-play drive in the third quarter, made it 16–3.

The fourth quarter belonged to Pittsburgh's defense. Rodgers found Darnell Washington for a 5-yard touchdown early in the period, and Daylen Everette's interception of Daniels set up a Chris Boswell field goal. Boswell tied it with a 58-yarder at the two-minute mark, and when Jamel Dean intercepted Daniels moments later, Pittsburgh started at the Tampa Bay 3. The Steelers settled for Boswell's 20-yard kick and a 19–16 lead, and McLaughlin answered from 53 yards with 13 seconds left to force overtime.

Pittsburgh drove 70 yards in 12 plays on the first possession of overtime. Tampa Bay's answering possession gained 15 yards and ended on downs. Jalen Ramsey and Nick Herbig had two sacks apiece as the Buccaneers were sacked five times and averaged 3.1 yards per play.
Rodgers completed 33 of 49 passes for 253 yards, with DK Metcalf and Bernard catching 11 passes apiece. Pittsburgh improved to 4-2 with its second straight win, and Tampa Bay fell to 1-5.

2026_06_SEA_DEN.headline: Lutz's 53-yard field goal lifts Broncos past Seahawks 17–14 in OT
paragraphs: Denver gained 168 yards and still beat Seattle, because its defense kept taking the ball away. Ja'Quan McMillian intercepted Sam Darnold on the first possession of overtime, and Wil Lutz made a 53-yard field goal four plays later as the Broncos won 17–14 on Thursday night.

The Broncos did all their scoring in regulation in the second quarter. J.K. Dobbins finished a 16-play, 74-yard drive with a 4-yard touchdown run, and RJ Harvey's 1-yard run capped a 79-yard march for a 14–3 lead.

Seattle chipped back. George Holani's 1-yard touchdown run midway through the fourth quarter made it 14–11, and even after Kris Abrams-Draine intercepted Darnold with 1:31 left, the Seahawks got the ball back and drove into range for Jason Myers' 34-yard field goal with seven seconds left. But Seattle's overtime possession began at its 13 and ended with McMillian's interception, giving Denver the ball at the Seattle 43.

Darnold completed 27 of 51 passes for 278 yards with two interceptions, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 12 passes for 134 yards. Seattle was sacked five times and turned the ball over three times; Denver had no turnovers. Bo Nix threw for 107 yards, and the Broncos averaged 2.9 yards per play and punted eight times.
Denver, a 3-point underdog, improved to 4-2 with its second straight win. Seattle fell to 3-3 and has lost two straight.

2026_06_TEN_IND.headline: Slye's four field goals help Titans rally past Colts 26–20
paragraphs: Indianapolis led 13–0 at halftime and gave it away one turnover at a time. Tennessee scored 20 unanswered points, and Joey Slye's 49-yard field goal with 2:07 left put the Titans ahead for good in a 26–20 division win on Sunday, an upset of a Colts team favored by 6.5.

Daniel Jones' 1-yard touchdown pass to Mo Alie-Cox and two Spencer Shrader field goals, the second after Cam Bynum intercepted Cam Ward, built the Indianapolis lead. Three turnovers within 10 minutes each led to points, and two of them belonged to the Colts in the third quarter: Jonathan Taylor fumbled seconds into the half, and Cor'Dale Flott intercepted Jones midway through the quarter. Slye turned both into field goals, including a 56-yarder.

Ward's 8-yard touchdown pass to Carnell Tate tied it 13–13 early in the fourth quarter, and Oluwafemi Oladejo's defensive touchdown put Tennessee ahead 20–13. Taylor answered with a 4-yard run to tie it again midway through the quarter, but Slye's 49-yarder and a 44-yarder with 47 seconds left settled it. The Colts' final drive ended on downs.

Tennessee won with 186 yards of offense and the ball for 21:28 because its defense sacked Jones six times, two each by Jeffery Simmons and Jermaine Johnson II, and forced three turnovers. Jones threw for 269 yards with two interceptions, and Taylor ran for 94 yards with 151 yards from scrimmage. Ward completed 11 of 22 passes for 102 yards.
The Titans improved to 1-5. The Colts fell to 2-4 with their second straight loss.

2026_06_WAS_SF.headline: McCaffrey scores twice as 49ers hold off Commanders 23–17
paragraphs: San Francisco built a 20–3 halftime lead and then had to survive a Washington comeback. Christian McCaffrey ran for two touchdowns and caught nine passes, and the 49ers held on to beat the Commanders 23–17 on Monday night and stay unbeaten.

Brock Purdy's 11-yard touchdown pass to George Kittle opened the scoring, and McCaffrey added 1-yard touchdown runs late in the first quarter and with 18 seconds left in the half, the second finishing a 14-play drive. Mike Evans set up McCaffrey's first score with a 54-yard catch but was hurt late in the second quarter and did not return. Washington lost Terry McLaurin to an injury in the first quarter, and he did not return either.

Eddy Pineiro's 33-yard field goal made it 23–3 in the third quarter, and from there the Commanders scored 14 unanswered points. Jayden Daniels threw a 1-yard touchdown pass to Stefon Diggs with 18 seconds left in the third quarter and a 9-yard scoring pass to Rachaad White midway through the fourth. Washington's last drive went 13 plays and 61 yards before ending on downs.

Daniels completed 29 of 40 passes for 300 yards, and Chig Okonkwo caught all seven of his targets. But Washington converted three of 12 third downs and was sacked four times. Purdy completed 21 of 29 passes for 264 yards, and McCaffrey finished with 117 yards from scrimmage. San Francisco improved to 6-0 with its sixth straight win, and Washington fell to 1-4-1.

2026_07_CIN_BAL.headline: Burrow throws four touchdowns as Bengals rally past Ravens 35–13
paragraphs: Cincinnati was shut out in the first half and then scored five touchdowns in the second. Joe Burrow threw four touchdown passes, and the Bengals scored 35 unanswered points to beat the Baltimore Ravens 35–13 on Sunday.

Baltimore controlled the first half. Tyler Huntley hit Zay Flowers for a 48-yard touchdown early in the game, and Tyler Loop kicked field goals at the end of drives of 18 and 13 plays for a 13–0 halftime lead. The Ravens' failure to finish those drives proved costly: they went none for three in the red zone, while Cincinnati scored touchdowns on all five of its red zone trips.

Burrow's 6-yard pass to Mike Gesicki and a 13-yard scoring throw to Tee Higgins gave the Bengals a 14–13 lead late in the third quarter. Samaje Perine's 1-yard run capped an 88-yard drive early in the fourth, and Burrow's 2-yard pass to Ja'Marr Chase made it 28–13. Moments later, Demetrius Knight Jr. intercepted Huntley, and Burrow found Drew Sample for a 16-yard touchdown three plays after that.

Burrow completed 22 of 30 passes for 292 yards without an interception, and Higgins caught six passes for 148 yards, including gains of 44 and 43 yards in the fourth quarter. Cincinnati averaged 7.0 yards per play despite holding the ball for only 25:00. Huntley threw for 298 yards, but Derrick Henry was held to 45 yards on 17 carries.
The division win lifted the Bengals to 4-2, their second straight. The Ravens fell to 4-3 and have lost two straight.

2026_07_CLE_TEN.headline: Szmyt's late field goal lifts Browns past Titans 27–24
paragraphs: Cleveland fell behind 14–0 in the first quarter, answered with 17 straight points and won it with three seconds left when Andre Szmyt made a 32-yard field goal. The Browns beat the Tennessee Titans 27–24 on Sunday despite three touchdown runs by Tony Pollard.

Pollard scored from 36 yards early in the game, and after Cor'Dale Flott intercepted Deshaun Watson, he ran 10 yards for another touchdown. Quinshon Judkins answered with touchdown runs of 5 and 6 yards, the second after Denzel Ward intercepted Cam Ward, and Szmyt's 28-yarder with four seconds left in the half put Cleveland ahead 17–14.

Neither team scored in the third quarter. Joey Slye's 29-yard field goal tied it midway through the fourth, and Watson's 9-yard touchdown run put the Browns back in front with 4:39 left. Tennessee answered with an 11-play, 63-yard drive that Pollard finished from a yard out with 1:01 left to tie it 24–24. Watson then moved Cleveland 55 yards in four plays from its 31, hitting Harold Fannin Jr. for 36 yards, to set up the winning kick.

Watson completed 25 of 36 passes for 308 yards, and KC Concepcion caught eight passes for 129 yards as Cleveland averaged 7.4 yards per play and gained 491 yards. Judkins ran for 96 yards. Pollard carried 25 times for 129 yards for Tennessee, and Cam Ward threw for 181 yards.
Cleveland improved to 5-2 with its second straight win. Tennessee fell to 1-6.

2026_07_DEN_ARI.headline: Nix's long touchdowns carry Broncos past Cardinals 30–16
paragraphs: Arizona held the ball longer, but Denver kept producing the big gain. Bo Nix ran 62 yards for one touchdown and threw 52 yards for another, and the Broncos beat the Cardinals 30–16 on Sunday for their third straight win.

The game was tied 6–6 after two field goals apiece, Chad Ryland's second finishing a 14-play Arizona drive late in the second quarter. Denver needed two plays to answer, with Nix breaking his 62-yard touchdown run late in the half for a 13–6 lead. His 52-yard scoring pass to RJ Harvey early in the third quarter made it 20–6.

Jacoby Brissett pulled Arizona within 20–13 on a 7-yard touchdown pass to Trey McBride late in the third quarter, but Denver answered right away. Marvin Mims Jr. caught a 47-yard pass, and J.K. Dobbins scored on a 1-yard run with two seconds left in the period. Wil Lutz, who made all three of his field goals, added a 31-yarder in the fourth quarter.

Neither team turned the ball over, so the gap came from explosive plays and finishing drives. Denver averaged 6.7 yards per play to Arizona's 4.7, and the Cardinals reached the red zone five times but scored only one touchdown. Their last drive covered 84 yards in 13 plays and ended on downs. Nix finished with 222 passing yards and 73 rushing yards, and McBride caught 10 passes for 111 yards for Arizona.
The Broncos improved to 5-2. The Cardinals fell to 2-5.

2026_07_GB_DET.headline: Bates' last-second field goal lifts Lions past Packers 20–17
paragraphs: Green Bay had a chance to take the lead late and came away empty, and Detroit made the Packers pay. Jake Bates kicked a 22-yard field goal with one second left, and the Lions beat Green Bay 20–17 on Sunday.

Jared Goff's 16-yard touchdown pass to Jameson Williams and Bates' 40-yard field goal gave Detroit a 10–7 halftime lead around Jordan Love's 14-yard scoring pass to Tucker Kraft. The Lions also gave the ball away twice around halftime. Jahmyr Gibbs fumbled in the final minute of the first half, though Green Bay could not use it before the break, and Goff fumbled early in the third quarter, setting up Love's 25-yard touchdown pass to Josh Jacobs for a 14–10 Packers lead.

Goff answered with a 10-yard touchdown pass to Williams midway through the third quarter. Brian Branch intercepted Love early in the fourth, and after Trey Smack tied it 17–17 with a 43-yard field goal, the Packers took over at the Detroit 22 with 4:50 left. They gained five yards, and Smack, who made one of three field goals, missed.

Detroit then drove 71 yards in 10 plays from its 25, with Gibbs breaking a 15-yard run, to set up Bates. Goff completed 22 of 32 passes for 303 yards, and Amon-Ra St. Brown caught nine passes for 153 yards. Love threw for 274 yards and two touchdowns, but the Packers scored one touchdown in four red zone trips.
The division win lifted Detroit to 4-2, its second straight. Green Bay fell to 4-3.

2026_07_IND_MIN.headline: Vikings rally past Colts 16–10 to stay unbeaten
paragraphs: Minnesota trailed at halftime and needed until the fourth quarter to find the end zone, but its defense allowed nothing after the break. Kyler Murray threw a go-ahead touchdown pass to T.J. Hockenson early in the fourth quarter, and the Vikings beat the Indianapolis Colts 16–10 on Sunday to move to 6-0.

Jonathan Taylor's 38-yard touchdown run gave Indianapolis an early lead. Will Reichard answered with two second-quarter field goals, the second at the end of a 12-play drive that started at the Minnesota 4, and Spencer Shrader's 43-yarder with three seconds left in the half sent the Colts into halftime ahead 10–6.

Neither team scored in the third quarter. Murray's 5-yard pass to Hockenson put Minnesota in front 13–10, and the Vikings lost Aaron Jones Sr. to an injury early in the fourth quarter. Reichard's 52-yard field goal with 1:44 left made it a six-point game, and Harrison Smith intercepted Daniel Jones two plays into the Colts' final drive.

The Indianapolis passing game gave the Colts little. Jones completed 13 of 22 passes for 108 yards, Indianapolis finished with 64 net passing yards and was sacked four times, two by Blake Cashman. The Colts ran for 154 yards, Taylor accounting for 95, and converted eight of 15 third downs, but Shrader made only one of three field goals. Murray threw for 150 yards.
Minnesota extended its winning streak to six games. Indianapolis fell to 2-5 and has lost three straight.

2026_07_KC_SEA.headline: Smith-Njigba's 150 yards lead Seahawks past Chiefs 20–3
paragraphs: Seattle kept Kansas City's offense off the field and out of scoring range. The Chiefs never reached the red zone, and the Seahawks beat them 20–3 on Sunday night behind nine catches for 150 yards from Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

Seattle opened the scoring with a 15-play, 86-yard drive that ended in a Jason Myers field goal in the second quarter. Ty Okada then intercepted Patrick Mahomes, and Sam Darnold turned the takeaway into a 28-yard touchdown pass to Smith-Njigba with 1:49 left in the half. Nohl Williams intercepted Darnold in the end zone just before halftime, but Kansas City missed a field goal on the ensuing possession and trailed 10–0.

Myers' 35-yard field goal made it 13–0 in the third quarter, and Harrison Butker's 50-yarder, his only make in three tries, was all the Chiefs managed. Emanuel Wilson's 21-yard touchdown run late in the fourth quarter put it away, and Kansas City's last possession ended on downs.

Seattle converted 11 of 16 third downs, ran 41 times and held the ball for 35:51. Wilson carried 24 times for 100 yards, and Darnold completed 20 of 28 passes for 257 yards without being sacked. Mahomes completed 19 of 33 passes for 165 yards for a Kansas City offense that gained 213 yards.
Seattle improved to 4-3. Kansas City fell to 5-1.

2026_07_MIA_NYJ.headline: Willis, Douglas lift underdog Dolphins past Jets 28–25
paragraphs: Malik Willis threw two touchdown passes to Caleb Douglas and ran for another score, and the Miami Dolphins, 3.5-point underdogs, held off a late New York rally to beat the Jets 28–25 in a division game on Sunday.

Miami built its lead by keeping the ball. After the teams traded early touchdowns, the Dolphins put together a 14-play drive capped by Ollie Gordon II's 1-yard run and then a 15-play, 91-yard march that ended with Willis scoring from 2 yards with 12 seconds left in the half. That made it 21–7, and Miami finished with 41 rushes, 34:36 of possession and three touchdowns on three red zone trips. Gordon ran for 103 yards.

New York moved the ball efficiently all day, averaging 7.1 yards per play, and climbed back in the second half. Geno Smith's 3-yard touchdown pass to Omar Cooper Jr. and Jason Sanders' 33-yard field goal cut the deficit to 21–17 midway through the fourth quarter.

Willis had the answer. On a three-play, 76-yard drive, he hit Douglas for a 63-yard touchdown with 4:55 to play, and that score proved just enough. Smith found Mason Taylor for a 12-yard touchdown with 3:30 left, Taylor's second of the day, to make it 28–25, but the Jets got no closer.

Smith threw for 287 yards and three touchdowns, with an interception, and Cooper caught five passes for 115 yards. Willis completed 14 of 21 passes for 208 yards without a turnover. Miami improved to 1-5, and New York fell to 2-5 with its second straight loss.

2026_07_LA_LV.headline: Stafford throws three touchdowns as Rams hold off Raiders 35–21
paragraphs: The Los Angeles Rams built a 28–6 halftime lead with four touchdowns and then held on through a fourth-quarter push to beat the Las Vegas Raiders 35–21 on Sunday in Las Vegas.

Matthew Stafford threw two short touchdown passes to Davis Allen, the second early in the second quarter, and an 11-yard score to Puka Nacua. Kyren Williams added a 17-yard touchdown run with 1:25 left in the half, completing 21 unanswered points. Las Vegas answered only with two Matt Gay field goals, the second with two seconds left in the half.

Las Vegas broke through after a scoreless third quarter in which it recovered a Williams fumble and then turned the ball over on downs. Kirk Cousins hit Tre Tucker for a 37-yard touchdown to open the fourth, and moments later Nakobe Dean intercepted Stafford. The Raiders needed four plays to turn it into Cousins' 15-yard touchdown pass to Ashton Jeanty, and the lead was down to 28–18.

Los Angeles answered on the ground. A 12-play, 70-yard drive ended with Blake Corum's 4-yard touchdown run with 6:37 left, and Gay's 36-yard field goal was the Raiders' only reply. The Rams ran for 199 yards to 48 for Las Vegas, with Williams gaining 99 and Corum 93, and they scored on five of five red zone trips while the Raiders went one of five and converted three of 14 third downs.
Cousins threw for 295 yards and two touchdowns, and Tucker caught five passes for 103 yards. The Rams improved to 3-4; the Raiders, also 3-4, have lost four straight.

2026_07_NE_CHI.headline: Burden's 130 yards help Bears edge Patriots 30–24
paragraphs: Drake Maye's interception in the Chicago end zone late in the first half swung a tight game, and the Bears turned it into a touchdown on the way to a 30–24 win over the New England Patriots on Thursday night.

Chicago led 13–7 when D'Marco Jackson picked off Maye with 3:32 left in the second quarter. Caleb Williams then drove the Bears 80 yards, finishing with a 24-yard touchdown pass to Luther Burden III with 21 seconds left. Maye answered with a 48-yard scoring pass to Rhamondre Stevenson with three seconds to go, but New England still trailed 20–14 at the half.

Burden caught four passes for 130 yards, and his 58-yard catch set up D'Andre Swift's 4-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. Williams threw for 308 yards and two touchdowns without an interception. After Colston Loveland's 12-yard touchdown catch made it 27–14, Maye hit Eli Raridon for a 30-yard score late in the third quarter to make it 27–21.

The Bears then made New England wait. Starting at their own 9 with 6:22 left, they ran 12 plays, with Rome Odunze making two 21-yard catches, before Cairo Santos kicked a 58-yard field goal with 1:39 remaining. Andy Borregales answered with a 47-yarder with 42 seconds left, but that only made it 30–24.

Maye completed 24 of 31 passes for 321 yards and the Patriots averaged 7.6 yards per play, but the end zone interception was the game's only turnover. Chicago improved to 5-2 with its second straight win, and New England fell to 4-3.

2026_07_NYG_HOU.headline: Singletary's 30-yard run in overtime lifts Giants past Texans 27–21
paragraphs: Houston forced overtime with 57 seconds left, but the New York Giants needed only three plays to end it. Devin Singletary's 30-yard touchdown run with 7:33 left in the extra period gave the Giants a 27–21 win on Sunday over a Texans team that had been favored by 10.
The Texans had the first chance in overtime and went three plays for no yards before punting. Cam Skattebo then broke a 42-yard run, and Singletary finished the three-play, 81-yard drive.

New York was the better team for most of the afternoon. The Giants outgained Houston 420 yards to 237, ran for 188 and held the ball for 35:50, and neither side turned it over. Skattebo carried 17 times for 124 yards, and his 16-yard touchdown run capped a 14-play, 80-yard drive that broke a 14–14 tie midway through the fourth quarter. J.J. McCarthy threw for 252 yards without a touchdown pass, with Malik Nabers catching seven passes for 111 yards.

The Giants still left points on the field. Dominic Zvada missed both of his field goal attempts. C.J. Stroud threw two short touchdown passes, a 6-yarder to Marvin Harrison Jr. that tied the game at halftime and a 3-yarder to Xavier Hutchinson that forced overtime, and Ka'imi Fairbairn made field goals from 58 and 57 yards.

Houston, which averaged 4.4 yards per play and converted three of 12 third downs, fell to 2-5. New York, which lost Tyrone Tracy Jr. to an injury in the second quarter after his first-quarter touchdown run, moved to 4-2-1.

2026_07_PIT_NO.headline: Boswell's three field goals carry Steelers past Saints 16–10 in Paris
paragraphs: In a low-scoring game in Paris, the Pittsburgh Steelers kept New Orleans off the scoreboard after halftime and got enough from Chris Boswell's leg to beat the Saints 16–10 on Sunday.

The first half stayed close. Aaron Rodgers threw a 4-yard touchdown pass to Darnell Washington, and Tyler Shough answered with a 1-yard scoring pass to Devaughn Vele that tied it at 10 with 1:48 left. Pittsburgh then drove 11 plays, and Boswell hit a 47-yard field goal with three seconds remaining for a 13–10 lead.

Pittsburgh never gave the lead back. Payton Wilson intercepted Shough midway through the third quarter, and Pittsburgh turned it into a 14-play drive that ended with Boswell's 39-yard field goal with 18 seconds left in the period. Boswell made all three of his kicks, while Daniel Carlson made one of his two for New Orleans.

Pittsburgh controlled the ground and the clock. The Steelers ran for 148 yards to 18 for the Saints, converted 10 of 16 third downs and held the ball for 32:03. Jaylen Warren ran for 101 yards and added 36 more on three catches. The margin stayed narrow largely because the Steelers scored just one touchdown on four trips inside the red zone.

Shough completed 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards for New Orleans, but his interception was the game's only turnover, and the Saints did not score again after Vele's touchdown. Pittsburgh improved to 5-2 with its third straight win, and New Orleans fell to 2-5.

2026_07_SF_ATL.headline: Falcons force four turnovers, rally past 49ers 29–20
paragraphs: San Francisco outgained Atlanta and led by 11 in the second quarter, but four turnovers undid the 49ers. The Falcons scored 23 unanswered points and handed San Francisco its first loss, 29–20 on Sunday.

Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black ran for touchdowns as the 49ers built a 14–3 lead. Michael Penix Jr. had already cut it to 14–9 with a 1-yard touchdown pass to Nick Muse when Black fumbled at the end of a run, and Atlanta recovered and drove for Nick Folk's 33-yard field goal with two seconds left, making it 14–12 at the break.

Penix put the Falcons ahead for good midway through the third quarter with a 5-yard touchdown pass to Kyle Pitts Sr. Later in the quarter, Jessie Bates III intercepted Brock Purdy, and Atlanta followed with a 90-yard drive that ended on Penix's 21-yard scoring pass to Drake London to open the fourth quarter. That made it 26–14.

Purdy answered with a 1-yard touchdown pass to Kyle Juszczyk with 5:09 left, but the 49ers gave the ball away twice more. Kendal Daniels intercepted Purdy, setting up Folk's 31-yard field goal at the two-minute mark, and George Kittle fumbled after a 21-yard catch with 57 seconds left, ending the 49ers' final drive.

Penix completed 25 of 34 passes for 213 yards and three touchdowns, and Atlanta did not commit a turnover. Three of the 49ers' four turnovers led to Atlanta points while the fourth ended the game. The Falcons improved to 3-4, and the 49ers fell to 6-1.

2026_07_TB_CAR.headline: Buccaneers run over Panthers 43–13 behind Irving's two touchdowns
paragraphs: Tampa Bay threw for only 64 yards and still routed Carolina. The Buccaneers ran for 258 yards, took four turnovers and beat the Panthers 43–13 in a division game on Sunday, even though Carolina had been favored by 3.

The game turned in the second quarter, when the Tampa Bay defense started scoring too. Bryce Young was sacked and lost a fumble early in the period, and Calijah Kancey returned it for a touchdown. Young was later intercepted by Zyon McCollum, and Baker Mayfield's 14-yard touchdown pass to Tez Johnson with 12 seconds left sent the Buccaneers to halftime ahead 33–6.
