Carolina's only first-half touchdown came on Darren Waller's 50-yard catch.

Bucky Irving carried 24 times for 106 yards and scored twice, finishing a 14-play first-quarter drive from 4 yards and adding a 1-yard run late in the half. Kenny Gainwell ran for 88 yards, and Sean Tucker put the game further out of reach with a 46-yard touchdown run early in the fourth quarter that made it 43–6. Tampa Bay held the ball for 35:57.

Carolina could not protect Young. Yaya Diaby had three of the Buccaneers' five sacks, and Tykee Smith's third-quarter interception led to one of Chase McLaughlin's two field goals. Young finished 14 of 27 for 163 yards with two interceptions, and the Panthers' only second-half points came on Anthony Tyus III's 12-yard run midway through the fourth.
The Buccaneers improved to 2-5 with the division win, and Carolina fell to 3-3.

2026_08_ARI_DAL.headline: Cardinals rally from 14 down, beat Cowboys 33–30 in overtime
paragraphs: Gardner Minshew II threw a 13-yard touchdown pass to Michael Wilson with 10 seconds left in regulation, and Chad Ryland's 42-yard field goal in overtime finished the Arizona Cardinals' 33–30 win over the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday. Arizona closed as a 7-point underdog and trailed 14–0 in the first half.

Shemar James intercepted Jacoby Brissett late in the first quarter, setting up Javonte Williams' 2-yard touchdown run, and Dak Prescott's 9-yard touchdown pass to Ryan Flournoy made it 14–0 midway through the second. The Cardinals still trailed 17–3 when Tyler Allgeier broke a 63-yard touchdown run late in the third quarter.

Dallas led 27–17 after Brandon Aubrey's 35-yard field goal with 3:58 to play. Minshew hit Trey McBride for a 14-yard touchdown, Aubrey answered from 41 yards with 1:14 left, and Minshew then drove Arizona 80 yards in eight plays, finding Wilson for gains of 21 and 27 yards before the tying score. After Dallas went three-and-out in overtime, Ryland's kick came with 2:58 left.

Allgeier ran for 147 yards on 11 carries and caught five passes for 44 yards, including a 5-yard touchdown early in the fourth quarter. Minshew completed 17 of 23 passes for 188 yards and threw all three Arizona touchdown passes; Brissett was 10 of 23 for 119 yards. Arizona outgained Dallas 467 to 261, and the Cowboys averaged 3.6 yards per play.
Dallas sacked Arizona quarterbacks five times and took the ball away twice, but Arizona outscored it 33–16 after the 14–0 start, with 20 points in the fourth quarter. Both teams are 3-5.

2026_08_ATL_TB.headline: Irving runs for 170 yards as Buccaneers shut out Falcons 16–0
paragraphs: Tampa Bay won without a passing game. Bucky Irving ran for 170 yards and the only touchdown, Kenny Gainwell added 140, and the Buccaneers' defense intercepted Michael Penix Jr. four times in a 16–0 division win over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday.

The game was decided in a wild stretch early. Four turnovers came within 10 minutes across the first and second quarters, three of them interceptions thrown by Penix, two of those to Alex Anzalone. The Falcons recovered an Irving fumble in between but gave the ball right back, and two of Penix's interceptions set up Chase McLaughlin field goals. McLaughlin made all three of his kicks, and Tampa Bay led 9–0 at halftime.

The Buccaneers' running game carried the rest. Tampa Bay ran 56 times for 324 yards and held the ball for 35:16, and Irving's 46-yard run midway through the third quarter set up his own 4-yard touchdown that finished a 90-yard drive and made it 16–0.

Atlanta could not sustain anything. Penix completed eight of 24 passes for 125 yards, and the Falcons went zero for 12 on third downs. Zyon McCollum added the fourth interception early in the fourth quarter, and Atlanta's best chance ended late in the game when a drive that began at its own 2 and included Jahan Dotson's 76-yard catch stalled on downs.
Tampa Bay won its second straight game, and both teams are 3-5.

2026_08_BAL_BUF.headline: Ravens lose Jackson early as Bills pull away 36–10
paragraphs: Baltimore lost Lamar Jackson on its opening drive, and the Buffalo Bills gradually wore down a Ravens offense that could not replace him. Buffalo won 36–10 on Sunday for its third straight victory.

Josh Allen scored on a 1-yard run before Jackson went down, and Joe Fagnano took over at quarterback. Baltimore's only touchdown came off a Buffalo mistake, when Broderick Washington Jr. intercepted Allen to set up Derrick Henry's 2-yard run that cut it to 10–7. Tyler Huntley then lost a fumble on a sack early in the second quarter, setting up Tyler Bass' 22-yard field goal. A DJ Moore fumble late in the half gave Baltimore the ball back, but Davison Igbinosun intercepted Fagnano on that possession, and Bass kicked a 51-yard field goal with 14 seconds left to make it 16–7 at halftime.

After Tyler Loop's field goal got Baltimore within 16–10, Buffalo scored the game's final 20 points. James Cook III ran 5 yards for a touchdown, and Allen threw scoring passes of 11 yards to Moore and 23 yards to Dalton Kincaid in the fourth quarter.

The Baltimore offense never found a rhythm. The Ravens finished with 144 yards, averaged 2.9 per play and converted three of 13 third downs, while Fagnano completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards. Buffalo sacked Baltimore quarterbacks four times and held the ball for 37:36.
Allen threw for 289 yards and two touchdowns. Buffalo improved to 6-1 despite two turnovers of its own. Baltimore fell to 4-4 with its third straight loss.

2026_08_CAR_GB.headline: Love throws three touchdowns as Packers hold off Panthers 27–19
paragraphs: Green Bay took the lead for good in the second quarter and spent the rest of Thursday night keeping Carolina at arm's length. Jordan Love threw three touchdown passes, and the Packers' pass rush sacked Bryce Young six times in a 27–19 win over the Panthers.

The lead changed hands three times in the first half. Chuba Hubbard's 1-yard run to open the second quarter put Carolina ahead 10–6, but Green Bay answered with 21 unanswered points. Josh Jacobs finished a 90-yard drive with a 1-yard run midway through the quarter, helped by Christian Watson's 53-yard catch, and Ty'Ron Hopper then intercepted Young. Love turned that into a 24-yard touchdown pass to Matthew Golden, and Green Bay led 20–10 at halftime. Love's 4-yard scoring pass to Jacobs in the third quarter made it 27–10.
Carolina could not get much going against the rush. The Panthers averaged 3.7 yards per play and converted five of 18 third downs, and Young completed 23 of 41 passes for 209 yards.

The Panthers made it close anyway. Ryan Fitzgerald kicked a 50-yard field goal, and Young's 26-yard touchdown pass to Jalen Coker with 5:45 left cut the deficit to 27–19. Green Bay turned the ball over three times, including a Love interception early in the fourth quarter, but none of those turnovers led to points. Carolina's final chance ended when Tetairoa McMillan fumbled after a catch with four seconds left and the Packers recovered.
Green Bay improved to 5-3. Carolina fell to 3-4 with its second straight loss.

2026_08_CHI_SEA.headline: Swift scores three touchdowns as Bears beat Seahawks 34–17
paragraphs: Seattle had pulled within 20–17 early in the fourth quarter when the Chicago Bears answered with two touchdowns, both by D'Andre Swift. The Bears, who were 3-point underdogs, beat the Seahawks 34–17 on Monday night for their third straight win.

Chicago controlled the ball from the start. A 17-play, 80-yard drive in the first quarter ended with Caleb Williams' 1-yard touchdown pass to Luther Burden III, and Cairo Santos added two field goals. Sam Darnold's 43-yard touchdown pass to Jaxon Smith-Njigba with 37 seconds left in the half made it 13–9, and Swift's 1-yard run midway through the third quarter pushed the lead to 20–9.

The Seahawks got back in it on a Bears mistake. Colston Loveland fumbled after a catch early in the fourth quarter, and Seattle needed three plays to turn it into Darnold's 7-yard touchdown pass to Cooper Kupp, making it 20–17. Chicago responded with a six-play drive that included Kalif Raymond's 39-yard run and ended with Swift's 5-yard touchdown. Then James Lynch intercepted Darnold, the Bears took over at the Seattle 6, and Swift scored from 5 yards again with 4:46 left.

Swift needed 27 carries for his 69 yards, but the Bears scored touchdowns on all four of their red zone trips and held the ball for 35:03. Williams completed 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards without an interception. Seattle converted one of 11 third downs, and Smith-Njigba finished with six catches for 118 yards.
Chicago improved to 6-2. Seattle fell to 4-4, and its last drive ended on downs.

2026_08_CLE_PIT.headline: Steelers sack Watson eight times, beat Browns 27–6
paragraphs: Cleveland moved the ball between the 20s but never into the end zone, and the Pittsburgh Steelers turned their pass rush and Jaylen Warren's running into a 27–6 division win on Sunday, their fourth straight victory.

The Steelers' defense set the tone early. Cleveland lost two fumbles in the first quarter, the second when Deshaun Watson was sacked, and Rico Dowdle's 9-yard touchdown run five plays later gave Pittsburgh a 7–0 lead. Andre Szmyt's two field goals were all the Browns could manage, and they failed to score a touchdown on three red zone trips. Pittsburgh sacked Watson eight times, with T.J. Watt getting two and Patrick Queen and Cameron Heyward 1.5 each.

The game turned for good at the end of the first half. Szmyt's 49-yard field goal had made it 13–6 with 49 seconds left, but Warren broke a 23-yard run and Aaron Rodgers hit Pat Freiermuth for 28 yards before Freiermuth ran it in from 1 yard with five seconds to go. Early in the third quarter, Rodgers found Darnell Washington for 58 yards, and Warren scored from 1 yard on the next play to make it 27–6.

Warren carried 17 times for 143 yards, including a 51-yard run, and Pittsburgh ran for 200 yards to 34 for Cleveland. Watson completed 27 of 39 passes for 324 yards, and Harold Fannin Jr. caught 10 passes for 154 yards, but the Browns' last drive, 11 plays for 66 yards, ended on downs. Cleveland fell to 5-3, and Pittsburgh moved to 6-2.

2026_08_IND_JAX.headline: Lawrence throws three touchdowns as Jaguars rout Colts 42–7
paragraphs: Jacksonville scored 35 straight points before Indianapolis got on the board, and the Jaguars beat the Colts 42–7 in a division game on Sunday. Trevor Lawrence needed only 14 passes, completing 10 for 210 yards and three touchdowns, and Bhayshul Tuten scored twice.

The Jaguars opened the scoring with a 12-play, 98-yard drive that started at their own 2 and ended on Lawrence's 12-yard touchdown pass to Brian Thomas Jr. The rest of the first half turned on turnovers. Jonathan Taylor fumbled midway through the second quarter, and Lawrence followed with a 31-yard touchdown pass to Nate Boerkircher. Tuten then broke a 39-yard touchdown run. Indianapolis recovered a Lawrence fumble late in the half but gave the ball straight back, as Rayuan Lane III intercepted Daniel Jones and returned it for a touchdown with 25 seconds left for a 28–0 lead.

Chris Rodriguez Jr. added a 28-yard touchdown run in the third quarter, and Lawrence's 25-yard scoring pass to Tuten with six seconds left in the period closed the scoring. Tuten finished with 104 rushing yards and 55 receiving yards, and Jacksonville averaged 6.9 yards per play.

The Colts' offense managed 4.0 yards per play, was sacked four times and converted three of 11 third downs. Jones threw for 144 yards with two interceptions, and his 6-yard touchdown pass to Josh Downs late in the third quarter was Indianapolis' only score.
Jacksonville, which lost Travon Walker to an injury early in the third quarter, improved to 5-2. Indianapolis fell to 2-6 with its fourth straight loss.

2026_08_KC_DEN.headline: Broncos rally past Chiefs 28–24 on Coleman's late touchdown
paragraphs: Patrick Mahomes threw three touchdown passes and Kansas City led by 11 entering the fourth quarter, but the Denver Broncos scored the game's final 15 points and beat the Chiefs 28–24 on Sunday for their fourth straight win.

Kansas City did its damage through the air. Mahomes hit Emmett Johnson for a 73-yard touchdown in the second quarter, Harrison Butker's 45-yard field goal with 23 seconds left made it 17–13 at halftime, and Mahomes' 4-yard touchdown pass to Noah Gray late in the third quarter put the Chiefs ahead 24–13. Mahomes completed 30 of 41 passes for 321 yards, and Johnson caught five passes for 128 yards.

Denver answered with two touchdown drives. Bo Nix led a nine-play, 80-yard march that ended with his 2-yard touchdown pass to Nate Adkins midway through the fourth quarter, pulling the Broncos within 24–21. With 2:31 left, Nix found Jonah Coleman for 51 yards, and Coleman ran 5 yards for the go-ahead touchdown with 2:00 left.
Kansas City still had time. Starting at its own 44 with 1:56 to play, the Chiefs moved the ball with help from Travis Kelce's 32-yard catch, but the drive ended on downs.

Neither team turned the ball over, and Denver scored touchdowns on all three of its red zone trips despite converting only two of 11 third downs. Nix threw for 222 yards and two touchdowns. Denver improved to 6-2 in the division matchup, and Kansas City fell to 5-2 with its second straight loss.

2026_08_LAC_LA.headline: Rams score 21 straight, keep winless Chargers out of end zone 24–9
paragraphs: The Los Angeles Chargers led 9–3 late in the first half on three Cameron Dicker field goals and never scored again. The Los Angeles Rams answered with 21 unanswered points and won 24–9 on Sunday, sending the Chargers to 0-7.

The swing began in the final two minutes of the half. Matthew Stafford found Tutu Atwell for 40 yards, and Kyren Williams scored from 1 yard with 22 seconds left to give the Rams a 10–9 halftime lead. Blake Corum's 23-yard touchdown run early in the third quarter made it 17–9.

Both of Justin Herbert's interceptions cost the Chargers points. Quentin Lake picked him off in the first quarter to set up Brandon McManus' 30-yard field goal, and Trent McDuffie intercepted him late in the third. Two plays later, Stafford hit Puka Nacua for an 18-yard touchdown and a 24–9 lead.

Herbert completed 24 of 32 passes for 257 yards, and the Chargers held the ball for 32:24, but they reached the red zone only once and did not score a touchdown. Their final drive, which began early in the fourth quarter and ran 10 plays, ended on downs. Nacua caught 11 passes for 80 yards for the Rams, and Corum ran for 73 yards on 11 carries.
The Rams improved to 4-4 with their second straight win. The Chargers have lost seven straight.

2026_08_LV_NYJ.headline: Cousins, Bowers lead Raiders past Jets 38–33 in shootout
paragraphs: The New York Jets outgained Las Vegas and led 30–21 in the third quarter, but they kept settling for field goals, and the Raiders made them pay. Kirk Cousins threw three touchdown passes and ran for another, and Las Vegas beat the Jets 38–33 on Sunday after Jeremy Chinn intercepted Geno Smith in the end zone with 14 seconds left.

The lead changed hands five times. Smith threw touchdown passes to Isaiah Williams and Adonai Mitchell in the second quarter, and Dylan Laube answered the first of them immediately with a touchdown for Las Vegas. Jason Sanders kicked four field goals, and New York led 23–14 at halftime and went back ahead 30–21 on Braelon Allen's 21-yard touchdown run midway through the third quarter.

Las Vegas answered with 14 unanswered points. Cousins scored on a 1-yard run late in the third quarter, then capped an 84-yard drive with a 2-yard touchdown pass to Jalen Nailor with 11:37 left for a 35–30 lead. Sanders' 31-yard field goal cut it to 35–33, and Matt Gay made a 53-yarder with 31 seconds left.

Cousins completed 19 of 26 passes for 247 yards and three touchdowns, and Brock Bowers caught seven passes for 92 yards and two scores. The Raiders scored touchdowns on all four of their red zone trips, while the Jets managed two touchdowns in six. Allen ran for 147 yards and Mitchell caught seven passes for 142 for New York.
Las Vegas evened its record at 4-4. New York fell to 2-6 with its third straight loss.

2026_08_MIN_DET.headline: Goff's late touchdown pass lifts Lions past Vikings 19–15
paragraphs: Minnesota had just taken the lead in the fourth quarter when the Detroit Lions answered with the decisive drive. Jared Goff's 7-yard touchdown pass to Jameson Williams with 4:40 left gave Detroit a 19–15 win over the Vikings on Sunday and handed Minnesota its first loss.

The lead changed hands four times in a game with few touchdowns. Kyler Murray's 1-yard touchdown pass to Justin Jefferson early in the second quarter gave Minnesota its first lead, but D.J. Reed intercepted Murray late in the half, and Jake Bates' 37-yard field goal with five seconds left cut it to 7–6.

Jahmyr Gibbs carried the Detroit offense. He ran 23 times for 153 yards, and his 30-yard touchdown run late in the third quarter put the Lions ahead 12–7. Detroit ran for 230 yards and held the ball for 35:43, though it scored only one touchdown in three red zone trips.

Minnesota went back in front after Murray hit Jordan Addison for 51 yards and then found T.J. Hockenson for an 8-yard touchdown midway through the fourth quarter, making it 15–12. Detroit responded with a seven-play, 69-yard drive that included a 17-yard Gibbs run and ended with Goff's touchdown pass. The Vikings got the ball back with 4:35 left but went three plays for 5 yards and punted.
Andrew Van Ginkel had 2.5 of Minnesota's four sacks of Goff. The division win was Detroit's third straight and moved the Lions to 5-2. Minnesota fell to 6-1.

2026_08_PHI_WAS.headline: Commanders score 27 straight to beat Eagles 27–10
paragraphs: The Philadelphia Eagles scored the first 10 points on Sunday night and none after that, and the Washington Commanders came back for a 27–10 division win. Drew Stevens kicked four field goals, and Washington sacked Philadelphia quarterbacks five times and forced two second-half turnovers that led to a field goal and a touchdown.

Jake Elliott made a 40-yard field goal for Philadelphia, and after the Eagles recovered Chig Okonkwo's fumble, Saquon Barkley scored on a 3-yard run. Stevens answered with a 56-yard field goal late in the first quarter, Jayden Daniels tied it midway through the second with an 8-yard touchdown pass to Stefon Diggs at the end of an 89-yard drive, and Stevens' 39-yarder with 23 seconds left in the half put Washington ahead 13–10 for good.

The Eagles averaged 3.9 yards per play, converted five of 15 third downs and got 30 yards on 13 carries from Barkley. Late in the third quarter, Tanner McKee fumbled on a sack and Washington recovered; Daniels found Treylon Burks for 53 yards on the ensuing drive, and Stevens kicked a 25-yard field goal for a 16–10 lead.

Stevens added a 42-yarder late in the fourth quarter, and Rasul Douglas intercepted McKee on Philadelphia's next possession. Rachaad White broke a 33-yard run and scored from 1 yard out with 1:55 left.

Daniels completed 16 of 29 passes for 217 yards and a touchdown without an interception, and Washington did not turn the ball over after its first-quarter fumble. The Commanders moved to 2-4-1. Philadelphia fell to 2-6 and has lost six straight.

2026_08_NE_MIA.headline: Maye leads Patriots back from 10 down to beat Dolphins 24–19
paragraphs: New England trailed Miami by 10 at halftime, then scored three straight touchdowns to beat the Dolphins 24–19 in a division game on Sunday. Drake Maye threw two touchdown passes and ran for another as the Patriots rallied with 21 unanswered points.

Miami controlled the first half. An Efton Chism III fumble set up the first of Zane Gonzalez's two field goals, and Malik Willis' 1-yard touchdown pass to Malik Washington with 11 seconds left before the break made it 13–3.

Maye turned the game in the third quarter. He hit Kyle Williams for a 43-yard touchdown midway through the period, then finished a 13-play, 73-yard drive with a 2-yard run with 1:02 left in the quarter for a 17–13 lead. Early in the fourth quarter, Kevin Byard intercepted Willis, and on the next possession Maye found DeMario Douglas for a 48-yard touchdown that made it 24–13.

Maye completed 16 of 20 passes for 199 yards without an interception, and Rhamondre Stevenson ran for 82 yards. The New England defense sacked Miami quarterbacks five times, with Cory Durden and Gabe Jacas getting 1.5 each, and held the Dolphins to 4.5 yards per play.
Willis threw a 35-yard touchdown pass to Kevin Coleman Jr. with 2:10 left, but Miami got no closer. New England improved to 5-3, and Miami fell to 1-6.

2026_08_TEN_CIN.headline: Burrow's five touchdowns lift Bengals past Titans 43–36 in overtime
paragraphs: Joe Burrow threw three interceptions to the same Tennessee defender and still found a way to win. After Amani Hooker's third pick, Burrow threw two fourth-quarter touchdown passes and ran 9 yards for the winning score in overtime as the Cincinnati Bengals beat the Titans 43–36 on Sunday.

Hooker's first interception set up a Joey Slye field goal that capped a 13–0 Tennessee start, with Tony Pollard's 40-yard touchdown run in between. Burrow answered with touchdown passes to Ja'Marr Chase and Jack Endries, and the Bengals led 14–13 at halftime. In the third quarter, Hooker picked off Burrow again, but Cam Ward fumbled on a sack on Tennessee's ensuing possession, and Burrow hit Tee Higgins for a 17-yard touchdown on the next snap. Pollard's 1-yard run tied it at 21, and after Hooker's third interception, Tennessee's possession ended in a safety.

The fourth quarter swung back and forth. A Chase Brown fumble set up Ward's 11-yard touchdown pass to Chimere Dike for a 28–23 Titans lead, and Burrow answered with a 25-yard scoring pass to Mike Gesicki. Ward's 15-yard touchdown pass to Wan'Dale Robinson put Tennessee ahead 36–29 with 3:50 left, but Burrow drove 81 yards and found Higgins from 18 yards with 1:20 remaining to tie it.
Cincinnati had the ball first in overtime and went 70 yards in five plays.

Burrow completed 38 of 48 passes for 462 yards and five touchdowns. Higgins caught 10 passes for 155 yards and two scores. Cincinnati improved to 5-2 with its third straight win, and Tennessee fell to 1-7.

2026_09_ARI_SEA.headline: Barner scores twice as Seahawks shut down Cardinals 17–3
paragraphs: Arizona drove 89 yards from its own 1 in the first quarter and came away with a field goal, and that was all the Cardinals managed. The Seattle Seahawks scored the next 17 points and won the division game 17–3 on Sunday.

AJ Barner accounted for both Seattle touchdowns in the second quarter. The tight end ran for a 1-yard score early in the period, then caught a 7-yard touchdown pass from Drew Lock with 18 seconds left before halftime, finishing an 81-yard drive for a 14–3 lead. Jason Myers added a 45-yard field goal late in the third quarter.

Arizona never reached the end zone. The Cardinals were held to 198 yards and 3.9 yards per play, were sacked three times and went zero for two in the red zone. Tyler Allgeier carried 17 times for 46 yards, and Gardner Minshew II completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards. Arizona's last chance, a 14-play, 76-yard drive in the fourth quarter, ended on downs.
Lock completed 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards, and Zach Charbonnet ran for 77 yards. Neither team turned the ball over. Seattle moved to 5-4, and Arizona fell to 3-6.

2026_09_BUF_MIN.headline: Bills smother Vikings 23–6, hold ball for 42:32
paragraphs: Buffalo kept the ball for 42:32 and kept Minnesota out of the end zone, beating the Vikings 23–6 on Monday night for its fourth straight win. The Vikings did not convert any of their eight third downs.

The first half was tight. Josh Allen was intercepted in the end zone by Byron Murphy Jr. in the first quarter, but Carson Wentz fumbled on Minnesota's next possession, setting up Tyler Bass' 39-yard field goal. Allen's 25-yard touchdown pass to Keleki Latu with 53 seconds left in the half made it 10–3, and Will Reichard answered with a 53-yard field goal to cut it to 10–6 at the break.

Buffalo then wore Minnesota down with long drives. Dorian Williams intercepted Wentz early in the third quarter, and the Bills followed with a 14-play, 83-yard march to Bass' 25-yard field goal. Terrel Bernard picked off Wentz later in the quarter, though Buffalo punted on its next possession. James Cook III later capped a 15-play, 84-yard drive with a 5-yard touchdown run midway through the fourth for a 20–6 lead. Bass added a 52-yarder.

Cook carried 31 times for 107 yards, and Allen threw for 234 yards. Minnesota finished with 178 yards. Wentz completed eight of 25 passes for 81 yards with two interceptions, and Max Brosmer went six of seven for 58 yards.
Buffalo improved to 7-1. Minnesota fell to 6-2 with its second straight loss.

2026_09_CIN_ATL.headline: Burrow, Chase lead Bengals past Falcons 34–17 in Madrid
paragraphs: Atlanta led 10–7 late in the first quarter in Madrid, but the Cincinnati Bengals scored the next 17 points and beat the Falcons 34–17 on Sunday for their fourth straight win. Joe Burrow completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns and ran for another.

Ja'Marr Chase answered Atlanta's opening touchdown with a 47-yard scoring catch, and after Nick Folk's field goal put the Falcons back in front, Cincinnati owned the second quarter. Burrow scored on a 1-yard run early in the period, then capped a 10-play, 88-yard drive with a 4-yard touchdown pass to Tee Higgins. Dohnte Meyers' 42-yard catch set up Evan McPherson's 57-yard field goal with 29 seconds left, and the Bengals led 24–10 at halftime.

Atlanta pulled within 24–17 on Bijan Robinson's 1-yard touchdown run midway through the third quarter, but Burrow answered with an 8-yard touchdown pass to Higgins late in the period. McPherson's 43-yard field goal late in the fourth and Barrett Carter's interception of Michael Penix Jr. closed it out.

Chase caught 10 passes for 155 yards, and Higgins scored twice on five catches. Cincinnati averaged 7.1 yards per play, converted six of 10 third downs and did not turn the ball over. Robinson ran for 100 yards and caught six passes for 47 more for Atlanta.
Cincinnati improved to 6-2. Atlanta fell to 3-6 with its second straight loss.

2026_09_CLE_NO.headline: Saints survive Browns 23–22 on Johnson's overtime touchdown
paragraphs: Three quarters of field goals in New Orleans gave way to four scores in the last 5:44 of regulation and two more in overtime. The Saints scored first in the extra period and held on when Cleveland's answer left it a point short, beating the Browns 23–22 on Sunday.

Neither offense reached the end zone until the fourth quarter. Charlie Smyth's 48-yard field goal put New Orleans ahead 9–6 with 5:44 left, and on the next snap Shedeur Sanders hit KC Concepcion for a 64-yard touchdown. The Saints answered with a 55-yard drive that Audric Estime finished with a 2-yard run with 1:00 to play, but Sanders moved Cleveland into range and Andre Szmyt tied it at 16 with a 51-yard field goal with 12 seconds left.

New Orleans took the first possession of overtime and went 74 yards in 11 plays, ending with Tyler Shough's 15-yard touchdown pass to Juwan Johnson. Cleveland came back with a 39-yard scoring pass from Sanders to Harold Fannin Jr. with 1:11 left, but that touchdown brought the Browns only to 22.

Shough threw for 265 yards and ran for 51 more, and Chris Olave caught seven passes for 98 yards. Sanders threw for 297 yards and two touchdowns without an interception, yet Cleveland went 0 of 2 in the red zone and was sacked five times, twice by Carl Granderson.
The Saints also gave up five sacks and missed a field goal, but they held the ball for 34:51. New Orleans improved to 3-5. Cleveland fell to 5-4 with its second straight loss.

2026_09_DAL_IND.headline: Cowboys answer Colts' late field goal, win 27–23 in Indianapolis
paragraphs: Spencer Shrader's 50-yard field goal gave the Indianapolis Colts a 23–20 lead with 1:41 to play on Sunday, and the Dallas Cowboys needed four plays to take it back. Dak Prescott found Ryan Flournoy for 46 yards on the first snap of the drive, Javonte Williams ran in from 1 yard with 1:10 left, and Dallas held on for a 27–23 win.

The Cowboys led 17–7 at halftime. Prescott fumbled on a sack in the first quarter, setting up Seth McGowan's 2-yard touchdown run, but he answered with a 10-yard touchdown pass to Jake Ferguson early in the second quarter and a 44-yard scoring pass to CeeDee Lamb just before halftime.

Indianapolis scored the next 13 points after Dallas went up 20–10 late in the third quarter. Daniel Jones hit Ashton Dulin for a 55-yard touchdown, and Shrader tied the game with a 59-yard field goal midway through the fourth. In between, Lamb lost a fumble after a 48-yard catch, and Jonathan Taylor gave the ball back on Indianapolis' next possession.

Lamb finished with 10 catches for 195 yards, and Prescott threw for 335 yards and two touchdowns without an interception. Dallas outgained Indianapolis 508 to 271 and averaged 7.2 yards per play, while the Colts converted three of 13 third downs.

Caleb Downs intercepted Jones with 41 seconds left to end Indianapolis' final drive. Dallas overcame two lost fumbles and the loss of Ferguson to an injury late in the third quarter to improve to 4-5. The Colts fell to 2-7 with their fifth straight loss.

2026_09_DEN_CAR.headline: Key's end-zone interception turns tide as Broncos beat Panthers 26–21
paragraphs: Carolina was ahead and threatening late in the third quarter when Devon Key intercepted Bryce Young in the end zone. The Denver Broncos turned that stop into the go-ahead touchdown and held off the Panthers 26–21 on Sunday for their fifth straight win.

Denver led 13–7 at halftime after Bo Nix threw a 3-yard touchdown pass to Courtland Sutton and Wil Lutz made two field goals. Carolina's only first-half touchdown, a 10-yard pass from Young to Tommy Tremble, came on the possession after Corey Thornton intercepted Nix. Young then hit Darren Waller for a 15-yard score early in the third quarter, putting the Panthers ahead 14–13.

After Key's interception, Denver went 80 yards in 14 plays, and Jonah Coleman scored on a 9-yard run early in the fourth quarter for a 19–14 lead. Nix added a 26-yard touchdown pass to Pat Bryant midway through the quarter, the second of 13 unanswered points.

Nix completed 25 of 37 passes for 237 yards and two touchdowns, and Denver converted six of 10 third downs. Young threw for 276 yards and three touchdowns, and Waller caught eight passes for 90 yards, but Ryan Fitzgerald missed Carolina's only field goal try.

Young's 4-yard touchdown pass to Tetairoa McMillan late in the fourth cut the gap to 26–21, but Young fumbled on a sack in the final two minutes and Denver recovered to end it. The Broncos improved to 7-2. The Panthers fell to 3-5 with their third straight loss.

2026_09_DET_MIA.headline: Bates kicks four field goals as Lions grind past Dolphins 19–9
paragraphs: Points came three at a time in Miami until late in the third quarter, when Jahmyr Gibbs scored the game's only touchdown. Jake Bates made all four of his field goals, and the Detroit Lions beat the Dolphins 19–9 on Sunday for their fourth straight win.

Each team turned the other's interception into a field goal. Chris Johnson picked off Jared Goff in the first quarter, and Zane Gonzalez kicked a 34-yarder to tie it. Chuck Clark intercepted Malik Willis early in the third, and Bates converted the short field from 33 yards for a 9–3 lead.

After Gonzalez answered from 52 yards, Detroit went 65 yards in six plays, helped by Goff's 31-yard completion to Jameson Williams, and Gibbs ran in from 8 yards out to make it 16–6. Miami's next drive included a 46-yard pass from Bradley Pinion to Kaytron Allen but ended in another Gonzalez field goal, and Bates restored the 10-point margin late in the fourth quarter.

Goff completed 17 of 25 passes for 170 yards, and Amon-Ra St. Brown caught eight for 86. Gibbs ran 20 times for 74 yards. Detroit was only one of four in the red zone, but Miami was held to 228 yards and went 0 of 3 inside the 20, with Derrick Moore recording two of Detroit's three sacks.
The Dolphins' last possession ended on downs. Detroit improved to 6-2, while Miami fell to 1-7 with its second straight loss.

2026_09_GB_NE.headline: Love throws for 372 yards as Packers beat favored Patriots 45–27
paragraphs: Xavier McKinney intercepted Drake Maye less than a minute into the game, and the Green Bay Packers spent the afternoon turning New England's mistakes into points. Green Bay, a 3.5-point underdog by the closing line, beat the Patriots 45–27 on Sunday.

Jordan Love ran 13 yards for a touchdown two plays after McKinney's first interception, and the Packers scored the game's first 17 points. McKinney picked off Maye again midway through the second quarter, and Kaleb Johnson's 2-yard run made it 24–7 on the way to a 24–14 halftime lead. Three of New England's four turnovers led directly to Green Bay touchdowns.

The third quarter put the game away. Love hit Savion Williams for a 10-yard score, and after Trey Smack's 51-yard field goal, Rhamondre Stevenson fumbled after a catch. Love found Christian Watson for a 39-yard touchdown on the next play, part of 18 unanswered points that made it 42–14.

Love completed 23 of 29 passes for 372 yards and three touchdowns without an interception. Watson caught seven passes for 171 yards, and Matthew Golden caught all 10 balls thrown his way for 164 yards. Green Bay averaged 7.5 yards per play, scored on four of five trips inside the 20 and did not turn the ball over.

Maye threw for 299 yards and three touchdowns but was intercepted three times, and New England lost Stevenson to an injury late in the third quarter. The Packers improved to 6-3 with their second straight win. The Patriots fell to 5-4.

2026_09_HOU_LAC.headline: Stroud throws five touchdowns as Texans rout winless Chargers 44–22
paragraphs: Three Cameron Dicker field goals had pulled the Los Angeles Chargers within 10–9 midway through the second quarter. C.J. Stroud answered with four touchdown passes in a run of 28 unanswered points, and the Texans beat the Chargers 44–22 on Sunday.

The first came two plays after Dicker's third field goal, a 63-yard pass to Tank Dell. Stroud found Kayshon Boutte for a 12-yard score with 36 seconds left in the half, and Houston led 24–9. The Chargers then gave the ball away twice in the third quarter. Derek Stingley Jr. intercepted Justin Herbert, and Stroud hit Nico Collins for a 13-yard touchdown on the ensuing drive. Keaton Mitchell's fumble led to a 63-yard scoring pass to Boutte early in the fourth quarter that made it 38–9.

Stroud finished 21 of 35 for 384 yards and five touchdowns, with his only interception setting up one of Dicker's field goals. Boutte caught four passes for 125 yards and two scores, and Dell had 105 yards.

The Houston pass rush shaped the Chargers' afternoon. Los Angeles was sacked eight times, with two each from Sheldon Rankins, Jadeveon Clowney and Will Anderson Jr., and averaged 4.6 yards per play while converting five of 17 third downs. Herbert threw for 193 yards and a 58-yard touchdown to Quentin Johnston, and DJ Uiagalelei threw a late scoring pass to Derius Davis.
Houston improved to 3-5. Los Angeles fell to 0-8 with its eighth straight loss.

2026_09_JAX_BAL.headline: Jaguars hold Ravens to 55 passing yards in 33–10 win
paragraphs: Baltimore could not throw the ball, and the Jacksonville Jaguars made it pay. With Joe Fagnano at quarterback, the Ravens finished with 55 passing yards, and Jacksonville scored 26 unanswered points on the way to a 33–10 win on Thursday night.

Bhayshul Tuten's 1-yard run put Jacksonville ahead early in the first quarter, and after Jake Moody's 53-yard field goal for Baltimore, the Jaguars controlled the rest of the half. Trevor Lawrence hit Parker Washington for a 50-yard touchdown late in the second quarter, and Jacksonville led 17–3 at the break.

The second half turned on Baltimore's turnovers. Montaric Brown intercepted Fagnano early in the third quarter, and Jourdan Lewis did the same early in the fourth, and Cam Little turned both into field goals. Little made all four of his attempts, and Chris Rodriguez Jr. added a fourth-quarter touchdown run. Jacksonville gave the ball back once, on a Travis Hunter fumble, but the Ravens' ensuing drive ended on downs.

Fagnano completed 10 of 18 passes for 60 yards with two interceptions, and Baltimore never reached the red zone. Derrick Henry carried 17 times for 57 yards. Lawrence threw for 242 yards, and the Jaguars did not allow a sack.

Justice Hill broke a 65-yard touchdown run midway through the fourth quarter for Baltimore's only touchdown. Jacksonville improved to 6-2 with its second straight win, while Baltimore fell to 4-5 with its fourth straight loss.

2026_09_LA_WAS.headline: Nacua catches 14 passes as Rams rally past Commanders 20–13
paragraphs: Trailing 10–6 at halftime, the Los Angeles Rams leaned on Puka Nacua and a pass rush led by Myles Garrett to beat the Washington Commanders 20–13 on Sunday. Nacua caught 14 passes for 150 yards and the go-ahead touchdown, and Garrett sacked Jayden Daniels three times.

Washington led on Daniels' 7-yard touchdown pass to Van Jefferson early in the second quarter. Late in the half, Nacua fumbled, but Daniels gave the ball right back when he fumbled on a sack, and Brandon McManus kicked a 20-yard field goal with five seconds left.

Blake Corum's 1-yard run early in the third quarter put the Rams ahead 13–10. Nick Cross intercepted Matthew Stafford, and Drew Stevens tied it with a 41-yard field goal, but Los Angeles answered with a 12-play, 65-yard drive that ended with Stafford's 7-yard touchdown pass to Nacua early in the fourth quarter.

Stafford threw 43 times for 228 yards, and Nacua was his target on 19 of them. The Rams converted only three of 14 third downs, but their defense held Washington to three points after halftime and sacked Daniels four times. Daniels threw for 274 yards.

Washington had one more chance, starting at its 9 with 52 seconds left. Daniels found Stefon Diggs for 42 yards, but Chig Okonkwo fumbled after a catch with three seconds left and the Rams recovered. Los Angeles improved to 5-4 with its third straight win. Washington fell to 2-5-1.

2026_09_LV_SF.headline: Dugger's interception return sparks 49ers past Raiders 38–17
paragraphs: The Las Vegas Raiders came out of halftime trailing 21–10 and lost the ball seconds later, when Jaden Dugger intercepted Kirk Cousins and returned it for a touchdown. Las Vegas turned the ball over five times in all, and the San Francisco 49ers won 38–17 on Sunday.

San Francisco had already built a 21–10 lead with long, patient drives. Christian McCaffrey and Brock Purdy each ran in from a yard out in the first quarter, on drives of 12 and 13 plays, and Purdy threw a 12-yard touchdown pass to McCaffrey in the second.

Dugger's return made it 28–10. Cousins answered with a 21-yard touchdown pass to Brock Bowers, and the third quarter then produced three turnovers in a short stretch: Treydan Stukes intercepted Purdy, Bowers fumbled on the Raiders' next possession, and Michael Mayer fumbled after a 24-yard catch. San Francisco turned Mayer's fumble into a seven-play, 80-yard drive capped by Purdy's 37-yard touchdown pass to Jordan Watkins late in the quarter.

Renardo Green intercepted Cousins in the end zone early in the fourth quarter, and the 49ers used 12 plays to set up Eddy Pineiro's 35-yard field goal. Malik Mustapha's interception on the Raiders' last possession ended it.

Purdy threw for 232 yards, and Kaelon Black ran for 70 as San Francisco rushed for 190 yards, held the ball for 38:18 and did not punt. Bowers caught seven passes for 111 yards, but Cousins was intercepted three times and Las Vegas ran for 24 yards. San Francisco improved to 7-1. Las Vegas fell to 4-5.

2026_09_NYG_PHI.headline: Arvell Reese sacks Eagles three times as Giants win 19–11
paragraphs: The New York Giants did not reach the end zone until late in the third quarter, and that touchdown and four Dominic Zvada field goals were enough for a 19–11 division win over the Philadelphia Eagles. Philadelphia was sacked seven times, three of them by Arvell Reese.

Zvada made field goals of 53 and 49 yards in the first quarter before Saquon Barkley's 3-yard touchdown run late in the quarter put Philadelphia ahead 8–6. In a scoreless second quarter, the teams lost fumbles on back-to-back possessions, the second when Joe Milton lost the ball on a sack, and neither turnover led to points.

New York went ahead to stay late in the third quarter, when Jameis Winston threw a 5-yard touchdown pass to Isaiah Likely to finish a 14-play, 76-yard drive. Zvada added a 38-yarder midway through the fourth quarter and a 49-yarder late in it, the second after a 4-yard drive that started at the Philadelphia 35.

Philadelphia managed 220 yards and 3.3 yards per play and converted five of 18 third downs. Milton completed 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards and ran for 64, while Barkley gained 22 yards on 13 carries. New York was held to 243 yards and 3.8 yards per play, and Zack Baun sacked the Giants twice.

Jake Elliott's 45-yard field goal with 2:00 left made it 19–11, and the Eagles' last possession, which began at their own 5, ended on downs. The Giants improved to 5-2-1 with their second straight win. Philadelphia fell to 2-7 and has lost seven straight.

2026_09_NYJ_KC.headline: Walker scores three times as Chiefs pull away from Jets 35–12
paragraphs: Jason Sanders kicked four field goals for the New York Jets, but they never reached the end zone, and the Kansas City Chiefs shut them out after halftime in a 35–12 win on Sunday. Kenneth Walker III ran for 102 yards and scored three touchdowns, two of them on passes from Patrick Mahomes.

New York led 6–0 after the first quarter and was still in front 9–7 when Braelon Allen fumbled midway through the second. Mahomes hit Walker for a 25-yard touchdown two plays later. Sanders' 54-yard field goal kept the Jets within 14–12, and they got another chance when Mahomes fumbled on a sack by David Bailey late in the half, but New York missed the field goal that followed.

Kansas City pulled away with three second-half touchdowns. Travis Kelce ran 1 yard for a touchdown early in the third quarter, Walker ran in from 2 yards with 15 seconds left in the quarter, and Emmett Johnson added a 6-yard touchdown run late in the fourth.

Mahomes completed 23 of 31 passes for 242 yards, and Kansas City scored touchdowns on all four of its trips inside the 20. The Jets had one red-zone trip and came away without a touchdown. They converted two of 12 third downs, averaged 3.7 yards per play and were sacked five times, twice each by George Karlaftis and Chris Jones. Geno Smith threw for 165 yards.
Kansas City improved to 6-2. New York fell to 2-7 with its fourth straight loss.

2026_09_TB_CHI.headline: Santos kicks Bears past Buccaneers 27–24 with three seconds left
paragraphs: Caleb Williams threw four interceptions and the Chicago Bears let a 14–0 lead slip away, but Cairo Santos made a 38-yard field goal with three seconds left to beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 27–24 on Sunday night.

Williams threw touchdown passes to Rome Odunze and Luther Burden III, the second from 56 yards, in the first quarter. Then the final 8:12 of the first half brought four interceptions, three of them thrown by Williams, two to Zyon McCollum. Only one led to points, McCollum's second, which set up Chase McLaughlin's 21-yard field goal with three seconds left in the half. Chicago still led 17–6.

Bucky Irving's 2-yard run early in the third quarter pulled Tampa Bay within 17–13, and after Alex Anzalone intercepted Williams, the Bears took the swing back. Jaylon Johnson intercepted Baker Mayfield and returned it for a touchdown, giving Chicago a 24–13 lead.

Tampa Bay scored the next 11 points. McLaughlin kicked a 35-yard field goal early in the fourth quarter, and Burden fumbled after a catch late in the quarter. Irving scored on a 6-yard run two plays later to tie it at 24 with 2:56 left.

Chicago answered with an eight-play, 49-yard drive, and Williams' 38-yard completion to Colston Loveland set up Santos. Williams finished with 279 yards and two touchdowns, and Chicago overcame five turnovers while Tampa Bay converted two of 12 third downs. The Bears improved to 7-2 with their fourth straight win. The Buccaneers fell to 3-6.

2026_10_BUF_NYJ.headline: Cook runs for 157 yards as Bills pull away from Jets 31–12
paragraphs: Jason Sanders kicked four field goals and kept the New York Jets within 17–12 late in the third quarter, but New York never reached the end zone, and the Buffalo Bills scored the last 14 points of a 31–12 division win on Sunday.

Josh Allen gave Buffalo the lead with a 1-yard run late in the first quarter, and the Bills led only 10–6 at halftime. Allen added another 1-yard touchdown run midway through the third quarter, on a drive sparked by a 54-yard completion to Dalton Kincaid. Sanders answered from 48 yards, and the Bills needed just two plays to respond: a 21-yard run by James Cook III and Allen's 45-yard touchdown pass to DJ Moore.

Each team then threw an interception that went nowhere. Davison Igbinosun picked off Cade Klubnik late in the third quarter, and Azareye'h Thomas intercepted Allen early in the fourth. The decisive turnover came late in the game, when Garrett Wilson fumbled after a catch and Cook ran 74 yards for a touchdown on the next snap.

Cook finished with 157 yards on 18 carries, and Buffalo ran for 201 yards and averaged 7.2 yards per play. The Jets, who used both Geno Smith and Klubnik at quarterback, gained 376 yards but went 0 of 2 in the red zone, converted three of 13 third downs and were sacked four times. Wilson caught seven passes for 106 yards.
Buffalo improved to 8-1 with its fifth straight win. New York fell to 2-8 with its fifth straight loss.

2026_10_CAR_NO.headline: Hubbard's 172 yards, late field goal lift Panthers past Saints 20–17
paragraphs: Charlie Smyth's 55-yard field goal tied the game with 45 seconds left, and that was enough time for Carolina. Bryce Young moved the Panthers 30 yards in three plays, and Ryan Fitzgerald made a 54-yarder with two seconds left to beat the New Orleans Saints 20–17 on Sunday.

Chuba Hubbard carried the Carolina offense, with 92 rushing yards, five catches for 80 more and both of the Panthers' touchdowns. His 2-yard run in the second quarter came after Tyler Shough fumbled, and it stood up for a 7–0 halftime lead. Shough had also been intercepted by Devin Lloyd in the first quarter.

New Orleans found its footing after the break. Alvin Kamara ran 3 yards for the tying touchdown in the third quarter, and after Fitzgerald's 55-yard field goal, Shough threw a 4-yard touchdown pass to Kamara late in the fourth to give the Saints their only lead, 14–10.

It did not last. Young hit Hubbard for 29 and 34 yards on the next drive, and Hubbard finished it with a 1-yard run with 1:51 left. Smyth's kick forced one more possession, and Fitzgerald won it from 54 yards.

Carolina did not turn the ball over, while New Orleans lost two. Shough completed 25 of 35 passes for 187 yards, and Jordyn Tyson caught 11 of them for 80 yards, but New Orleans ran for 49 yards and averaged 3.6 yards per play. The Panthers improved to 4-5 with the division win. The Saints fell to 3-6.

2026_10_JAX_TEN.headline: Lawrence throws for 352 yards as Jaguars beat Titans 40–23
paragraphs: Tennessee hung within a touchdown into the fourth quarter on the strength of Joey Slye's leg, but the Jacksonville Jaguars kept the ball for 38:10 and finished with 10 straight points in a 40–23 division win over the Titans on Sunday.

Trevor Lawrence threw a 2-yard touchdown pass to Parker Washington on Jacksonville's first scoring drive, and an early exchange of interceptions went the Jaguars' way. Cedric Gray picked off Lawrence, but Travis Hunter intercepted Cam Ward on Tennessee's next possession, and Cam Little turned it into a 46-yard field goal. Little made all four of his kicks, including a 36-yarder with two seconds left in the half for a 16–10 lead.

Slye kept answering. His field goals of 54 and 50 yards in the third quarter came around Lawrence's 3-yard touchdown pass to Brenton Strange, and after Lawrence found Josh Cameron for a 25-yard score midway through the fourth, Ward's 32-yard touchdown pass to Tony Pollard made it 30–23. Jacksonville responded with Little's 40-yard field goal, stopped the Titans on downs and added Bhayshul Tuten's 6-yard touchdown run with 1:14 left.

Lawrence completed 25 of 35 passes for 352 yards and three touchdowns, and Washington caught seven for 152 yards. Jacksonville punted once. Ward threw for 231 yards and two touchdowns, but Tennessee converted two of 11 third downs.
The Jaguars improved to 7-2 with their third straight win. The Titans fell to 1-8 with their third straight loss.

2026_10_KC_ATL.headline: Mahomes throws five touchdowns as Chiefs beat Falcons 35–13
paragraphs: Atlanta moved the ball for 370 yards but reached the end zone once in five trips inside the 20, while the Kansas City Chiefs scored touchdowns on all three of theirs in a 35–13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.

Patrick Mahomes threw a 12-yard touchdown pass to Emmett Johnson to finish an 80-yard opening drive, and after Jake Moody's 28-yard field goal, he found Josh Downs for an 18-yard score with 24 seconds left in the half. Kansas City led 14–3 at the break.

The Chiefs then scored 21 unanswered points to put it away. Mahomes hit Cyrus Allen for a 39-yard touchdown midway through the third quarter, and an 87-yard drive, helped by Mahomes' 50-yard completion to Rashee Rice, ended with his second touchdown pass to Johnson early in the fourth. Bijan Robinson's 3-yard run and a field goal pulled Atlanta within 28–13, but Mahomes answered with a 43-yard touchdown pass to Andrew Armstrong late in the quarter.

Mahomes completed 22 of 35 passes for 348 yards and five touchdowns without an interception, and Johnson ran for 101 yards to go with his six catches for 70. Kansas City averaged 7.3 yards per play and did not turn the ball over.

Michael Penix Jr. threw for 286 yards but completed 23 of 43 attempts, and two late Atlanta possessions ended with a Kyle Pitts Sr. fumble and Nohl Williams' interception in the end zone. Kansas City improved to 7-2 with its second straight win. Atlanta fell to 3-7 with its third straight loss.

2026_10_LA_ARI.headline: Rams hold Cardinals to 123 yards in 34–6 division win
paragraphs: Arizona kicked two field goals in the first quarter and then did not score again. The Los Angeles Rams held the Cardinals to 123 total yards, sacked them five times and scored 31 unanswered points in a 34–6 win on Sunday.

Chad Ryland's two 49-yard field goals gave Arizona a 6–3 lead that lasted until late in the first half. Matthew Stafford threw a 5-yard touchdown pass to Tyler Higbee with 1:09 left, and Kamren Kinchens intercepted Carson Beck on the next possession. Stafford needed three plays to find Xavier Smith for a 22-yard touchdown, and the Rams led 17–6 at halftime.

The pattern repeated in the third quarter. Blake Corum ran 1 yard for a touchdown early in the quarter, Wesley Bailey intercepted Beck, and Stafford hit Davis Allen for a 19-yard score on the following drive. Brandon McManus closed the scoring with a 43-yard field goal to open the fourth quarter.

Los Angeles controlled the ball for 42:23 and ran for 202 yards, with Corum gaining 100 and Ronnie Rivers 81. Stafford completed 18 of 26 passes for 249 yards and three touchdowns. Arizona managed 34 rushing yards, went 0 of 6 on third downs and never reached the red zone. Beck completed 11 of 18 passes for 108 yards with two interceptions.
The Rams improved to 6-4 with their fourth straight win. The Cardinals fell to 3-7 with their second straight loss.

2026_10_MIA_IND.headline: Colts hold off Dolphins 24–22 in a game of defensive touchdowns
paragraphs: Two defensive touchdowns in the third quarter swung a game that neither offense could control, and the Indianapolis Colts held on to beat the Miami Dolphins 24–22 on Sunday when Miami's final drive ended on downs.

The first half had its own oddity: Miami receiver Malik Washington threw a 34-yard touchdown pass to Jalen Tolbert to answer Seth McGowan's 4-yard run. Daniel Jones then led a 92-yard drive that started at the Indianapolis 8 and ended with his 7-yard touchdown pass to Laquon Treadwell with 44 seconds left, and the Colts led 14–7 at halftime.

Early in the third quarter, Kyle McCord fumbled on a sack and Adetomiwa Adebawore returned it for a touchdown. After Zane Gonzalez's 53-yard field goal, Chris Johnson intercepted Jones and returned it for a touchdown to make it 21–16. Spencer Shrader's 51-yard field goal pushed the lead back to 24–16, and McCord's 3-yard run to open the fourth quarter made it 24–22.
Neither team scored again. Gonzalez made only one of his three field goal attempts, and the Dolphins' last possession, from their own 42, gained 9 yards before ending on downs.

Indianapolis ran for 172 yards, with Jonathan Taylor gaining 83 and McGowan 77, which covered for an offense that threw for 104 yards and gave up an interception return. Jones completed 11 of 22 passes. The Colts improved to 3-7. The Dolphins fell to 1-8 with their third straight loss.

2026_10_MIN_GB.headline: Vikings sack Love eight times in 30–10 win over Packers
paragraphs: Green Bay lost a fumble early in the first quarter and spent the rest of the afternoon trying to recover. The Minnesota Vikings sacked Jordan Love eight times, forced four turnovers and beat the Packers 30–10 on Sunday.

Mark Redman's fumble after a catch early in the first quarter set up Will Reichard's 34-yard field goal, and Kirk Cousins threw a 38-yard touchdown pass to Myles Price late in the quarter. Harrison Smith intercepted Love in the end zone to open the second quarter, and Aaron Jones Sr. ran 1 yard for a touchdown midway through it. Minnesota led 17–0 at halftime.

Love fumbled early in the third quarter, and Reichard's 32-yard field goal made it 20–0. Green Bay then found some rhythm, scoring 10 straight points on Love's 32-yard touchdown pass to J. Michael Sturdivant and Trey Smack's 40-yard field goal. Minnesota answered with an 11-play, 75-yard drive that ended with Cousins' 20-yard touchdown pass to Gavin Bartholomew midway through the fourth quarter, and Reichard's third field goal closed the scoring.

Cousins completed 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns, and Justin Jefferson caught nine passes for 74 yards. Minnesota held the ball for 35:16. Love threw for 220 yards, but Green Bay averaged 4.1 yards per play, ran for 56 yards and went 0 of 1 in the red zone. Levi Drake Rodriguez had two of the eight sacks.
The division win lifted Minnesota to 7-2. Green Bay fell to 6-4.

2026_10_PIT_CIN.headline: Chase catches 11 for 231 yards as Bengals beat Steelers 38–18
paragraphs: Joe Burrow completed 35 of 44 passes for 409 yards and four touchdowns, and the Cincinnati Bengals built a 24–3 halftime lead on the way to a 38–18 division win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday night.

Cincinnati set the tone with long drives. A 13-play march ended in Evan McPherson's 24-yard field goal, and another went 92 yards from the Cincinnati 8 before Burrow found Drew Sample for a 3-yard touchdown early in the second quarter. Ja'Marr Chase's 53-yard catch set up Burrow's 2-yard scoring pass to Chase Brown, and after Chris Boswell's 45-yard field goal, Burrow hit Dohnte Meyers for a 15-yard touchdown with 14 seconds left in the half.

Brown caught a second touchdown pass, from 4 yards, late in the third quarter, making it 31–3. Chase finished with 11 catches for 231 yards, and Cincinnati averaged 7.4 yards per play, scored touchdowns on five of six trips inside the 20 and did not turn the ball over.

Pittsburgh was held to 222 yards and 3.8 yards per play, and it came away empty on both of its red-zone trips. Aaron Rodgers completed 15 of 29 passes for 143 yards. His two fourth-quarter touchdown passes, 22 yards to DK Metcalf and 27 yards to Pat Freiermuth, came after the Bengals had built a 31–3 lead, and Samaje Perine's 1-yard run in between kept the margin wide.
Cincinnati improved to 7-2 with its fifth straight win. Pittsburgh fell to 6-3.

2026_10_SEA_LV.headline: Smith-Njigba's 171 yards lead Seahawks past Raiders 21–13
paragraphs: Drew Lock fumbled on a sack less than a minute into the game, and the Las Vegas Raiders turned it into a touchdown. Lock hardly missed after that, completing 14 of 17 passes for 240 yards, and the Seattle Seahawks rallied from a 10–7 halftime deficit to win 21–13 on Sunday.

Fernando Mendoza's 10-yard touchdown run put Las Vegas ahead in the first quarter. Lock answered with a 34-yard touchdown pass to Cooper Kupp late in the first quarter, but Matt Gay's 34-yard field goal gave the Raiders the lead at the break.

Seattle took control in a span of two possessions in the third quarter. Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught passes of 30 and 23 yards on an 87-yard drive that Jadarian Price finished with a 12-yard touchdown run, and on the next Seattle drive Lock found Smith-Njigba for a 71-yard touchdown and a 21–10 lead. Smith-Njigba finished with eight catches for 171 yards.

The Seattle defense made the lead hold. Las Vegas gained 163 yards, averaged 2.8 yards per play and was sacked six times, two of them by Devon Witherspoon. Mendoza completed 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards. Lock fumbled on another sack early in the fourth quarter, but the Raiders punted after the recovery, and Gay's 43-yard field goal with 2:08 left was their only second-half score.
Seattle improved to 6-4 with its second straight win. Las Vegas fell to 4-6 with its second straight loss.

2026_10_WAS_NYG.headline: Daniels recovers from two interceptions to lift Commanders past Giants 24–21
paragraphs: Jayden Daniels threw two fourth-quarter interceptions, one in the end zone, and still got a final chance. He used it to hit Stefon Diggs for a 32-yard touchdown with 1:05 left, and the Washington Commanders beat the New York Giants 24–21 on Thursday night.

The lead changed hands six times. Cam Skattebo scored on a 1-yard run to finish a 16-play drive late in the second quarter, but Daniels threw a 1-yard touchdown pass to Ben Sinnott with nine seconds left in the half for a 10–7 Washington lead. Skattebo's 13-yard run and Daniels' 31-yard touchdown pass to Antonio Williams traded the lead again in the third quarter.

J.J. McCarthy put New York ahead 21–17 midway through the fourth quarter with a 66-yard touchdown pass to Isaiah Likely, who caught nine passes for 127 yards. Daniels then threw two interceptions, to Jevon Holland in the end zone and to Ar'Darius Washington, but the Giants punted after both, and their lead stayed at 21–17.

Washington took over at its 29 with 1:46 left and needed three plays to cover 71 yards. Rasul Douglas then intercepted McCarthy with 34 seconds left to end the Giants' last drive. It was the third interception in a 5-minute stretch, and none of them produced points.

Daniels finished with 249 yards and three touchdowns, and Diggs caught six passes for 83 yards. Skattebo had 122 yards from scrimmage, and McCarthy threw for 293. The division win lifted Washington to 3-5-1, while New York fell to 5-3-1.

2026_07_DAL_PHI.headline: Javonte Williams runs for 155 as Cowboys beat Eagles 38–21
paragraphs: The Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles traded the lead six times through three quarters on Monday night before Dallas scored the final 18 points and won 38–21. The Cowboys did not turn the ball over or allow a sack.

Neither side held a lead for long in the first half. Saquon Barkley and Dameon Pierce ran for Philadelphia touchdowns, and Dak Prescott answered each with a scoring pass, a 9-yarder to CeeDee Lamb and a 21-yarder to George Pickens. Brandon Aubrey's 27-yard field goal with 3 seconds left sent Dallas to halftime ahead 20–14.

Philadelphia went back in front midway through the third quarter when Tanner McKee found Makai Lemon for a 4-yard touchdown at the end of a 17-play, 84-yard drive. Prescott's second touchdown pass to Lamb, from 16 yards late in the quarter, put Dallas ahead 28–21, and Aubrey and Javonte Williams added the rest in the fourth.

Williams carried 25 times for 155 yards and a touchdown, including a 34-yard run early in the fourth quarter, and Dallas finished with 204 rushing yards and eight conversions on 13 third downs. Prescott completed 15 of 27 passes for 212 yards and three touchdowns, and Aubrey made all three of his field goal attempts.

DeMarvion Overshown intercepted McKee midway through the fourth quarter, and Philadelphia's last possession ended on downs. The Eagles also lost Pierce and Moro Ojomo to injuries in the fourth, and neither returned. Dallas moved to 3-4 with the division win, while Philadelphia fell to 2-5 and has lost five straight.

2026_10_LAC_BAL.headline: Underdog Chargers run past Ravens 23–20 in Baltimore
paragraphs: Justin Herbert threw for only 129 yards, but the Los Angeles Chargers ran for 160 and did not turn the ball over in a 23–20 win over the Baltimore Ravens on Monday night. The Ravens had closed as 3.5-point favorites.

Herbert ran 22 yards for a touchdown early in the first quarter, and Cameron Dicker's 38-yard field goal made it 10–0. After Derrick Henry's 2-yard touchdown run early in the second quarter, Del'Shawn Phillips intercepted Jacoby Brissett, and Los Angeles turned it into a 13-play drive that ended with Omarion Hampton's 1-yard touchdown run with 2:00 left in the half. Riley Patterson's 26-yard field goal made it 17–10 at halftime.

Dicker added field goals of 34 yards midway through the third quarter and 35 yards at the start of the fourth for a 23–13 lead. Henry's 1-yard run early in the fourth pulled Baltimore within 23–20 at the end of a 71-yard drive, but the Ravens did not score again.

Brissett completed 33 of 49 passes for 340 yards, and Mark Andrews caught all eight of his targets for 82 yards, but Baltimore ran for 16 yards on 15 carries; Henry scored twice while gaining 10 yards on 10 attempts. Hampton carried 22 times for 105 yards, and Tre' Harris caught five passes for 86 yards.

Zay Flowers fumbled after a 15-yard catch with 2:11 left, and Los Angeles recovered. The Chargers converted only two of 13 third downs, but they forced two turnovers without committing one and improved to 1-8. Baltimore fell to 4-6 and has lost five straight.
